## Step 4.235 — the payload's boot path reaches the stick without `QcomBds`, `BDS_Menu.cfg` or `BootUSBFirst`: the one string all three of its boot-policy binaries carry is not a vendor policy but `EFI_REMOVABLE_MEDIA_FILE_NAME` — `MdePkg/Include/Uefi/UefiSpec.h:2271`, AARCH64 value `\EFI\BOOT\BOOTAA64.EFI`, one of the six per-architecture spec constants at 2267–2272 — and it has two independent consumers in this tree, `BdsDxe/BdsEntry.c:838` building the `Default PlatformRecovery` option out of it and `UefiBootManagerLib/BmBoot.c:1099` appending it to any BlockIo/SimpleFileSystem device path, so the USB-entry question 4.234 left open is answered by the library rather than by the menu; and the payload holds **89 ARM64 PE32+ images in 89 files**, not 88, because an image here has `e_lfanew = 0xE58` and a bound of `0x400` on that field silently discards 45 of them

**An instrument error of my own, recorded because the next reader will make it.** Enumerating the payload's images by scanning for `MZ` and requiring a `PE\0\0` signature at `e_lfanew` returned **44 images**, against 4.233's census of 88 files carrying a `0x10` section. The discrepancy was mine and not the census's: I had bounded `0 < e_lfanew < 0x400`, which is the usual range, but images built by this toolchain carry a **3,672-byte DOS stub** and `e_lfanew = 0xE58`. At `mz + 0xE58` the `PE\0\0` signature is there, with `Machine = 0xAA64` and `OptionalHeader magic = 0x20B`; the bound discarded every one of them. Loosening it to `0 < e_lfanew < 0x100000` and requiring the ARM64 machine type gives the true figure.

**The payload's image census, measured with the machine-type filter.** Of **91** occurrences of `MZ` in `/tmp/fvmain.bin`, **89** are ARM64 PE32+ images and 2 are data: the one at `0x999fc` has `e_lfanew = 0x2500` pointing at zeros with the nearest real `PE\0\0` 0x2610 bytes away, and the byte pair at `0x4d5a` there is followed by `61 22 15 00` rather than a DOS stub. All 89 have `Machine = 0xAA64` and `OptionalHeader magic = 0x20B` — there is no 32-bit and no Thumb image in the payload — and each maps to a **distinct** enclosing FFS file by the `0x10` section header immediately preceding it, so 89 files carry exactly one image each. Against 4.233's 88, the map-derived walk was **one short**; the map's own `0x10`-carrying count and the image count are two different quantities here, and the image count is the one that says how many drivers are in the volume.

**The string that 4.234 read as policy evidence is a UEFI specification constant.** The three boot-policy binaries each contain the wide string `\EFI\BOOT\BOOTAA64.EFI` exactly once, at `0x46b000` in `BdsDxe`, `0x5f8f10` in `BootManagerMenuApp` and `0x650800` in `MsBootPolicy` — and all three sit in the same string-table neighbourhood, which is MdePkg's **device-path text** table: `BBS(0x%x,%a`, `BBS(%s,%a`, `HD(%d,%d,0`, `NoTopology,0,0,0`, `SAS(0x%lx,0x%lx,0x%x,`, `Uart(%ld,`, `AcpiEx(%s,`, `,StatelessAutoConfigure,`, `,StatefulAutoConfigure,`, `CRC32C`, the device-type names `UsbDiagnostic`, `UsbHub`, `UsbCDCData`, `UsbHID`, `Media`, `CDROM`, `DVD/CDROM`, `HDDP`, `DHCP`, `HTTP`, `SATA`, `PCMCIA`, `Static`, and the vendor and model strings `Panasonic`, `Toshiba`, `YMTC`, `Corsair/AData`. So all three link the device-path library, and the literal is `EFI_REMOVABLE_MEDIA_FILE_NAME` — `MdePkg/Include/Uefi/UefiSpec.h:2271` — whose AARCH64 value is `L"\\EFI\\BOOT\\BOOTAA64.EFI"`, alongside `EFI_REMOVABLE_MEDIA_FILE_NAME_IA32` at 2267, `_IA64` at 2268, `_X64` at 2269, `_ARM` at 2270 and `_EBC` at 2272. The three occurrences are therefore one constant linked three times, not three independent USB-first policies, and the useful content of the finding is not that the string is present but that it is the *right* string: it is the file the stick carries — `tools/make-win-stick.sh:47` refuses a tree without `efi/boot/bootaa64.efi` and `:89` prints whether it is present — so a boot option built from a short-form removable-media path resolves to this installer.

**And that constant has two consumers in this tree, both of which reach removable media without Qualcomm's boot manager.** `MdeModulePkg/Universal/BdsDxe/BdsEntry.c:838` builds the short-form default: `FilePath = FileDevicePath (NULL, EFI_REMOVABLE_MEDIA_FILE_NAME);` and hands it to `EfiBootManagerInitializeLoadOption` as `LoadOptionTypePlatformRecovery` with the description `L"Default PlatformRecovery"`, the source's own comment above it citing the specification's requirement that firmware supporting Platform Recovery publish "a short-form File Path Media Device Path containing the platform default file path for removable media". `MdeModulePkg/Library/UefiBootManagerLib/BmBoot.c:1099`, inside `BmExpandMediaDevicePath`, does the other half: `NextFullPath = FileDevicePath (Handle, EFI_REMOVABLE_MEDIA_FILE_NAME);` appends the file to any BlockIo or SimpleFileSystem device path, which is how a short-form USB entry named in `BootOrder` becomes a bootable file path. `BdsDxe` contains the first directly; `BootManagerMenuApp` and `MsBootPolicy` link `UefiBootManagerLib` and so carry the second. Neither path reads `BDS_Menu.cfg`, neither consults `AttemptUSBFirst`, and neither needs `QcomBds` — so 4.234's finding that the stock `Boot USB First` toggle is dead data in this payload is true and **does not block the gate**, because the gate does not need the toggle: it needs a firmware that can name and load `\EFI\BOOT\BOOTAA64.EFI` on a removable FAT32 partition, and this payload can, by two independent mechanisms.

**What that leaves as the gate's real dependency.** Both mechanisms end in `FileDevicePath (Handle, …)` where `Handle` has already been located by `gEfiSimpleFileSystemProtocolGuid`. So the boot option is constructible only after the USB host stack has enumerated the stick and `UsbMassStorageDxe` has produced a BlockIo and a SimpleFileSystem on it — which is precisely the six drivers the payload adds and stock lacks, and precisely the half of P3 item 3 that has never run on the phone. The boot policy was the part that looked uncertain and is now sourced; the transport is the part that was always going to decide it, and it is still unflashed.

**decides**: that the payload holds **89** ARM64 PE32+ images, one per FFS file, with 2 of 91 `MZ` occurrences being data, and that an `e_lfanew` bound of `0x400` is the wrong instrument on this volume because these images carry `e_lfanew = 0xE58`; that the wide string `\EFI\BOOT\BOOTAA64.EFI` in `BdsDxe`, `BootManagerMenuApp` and `MsBootPolicy` is `EFI_REMOVABLE_MEDIA_FILE_NAME` defined at `MdePkg/Include/Uefi/UefiSpec.h:2271` as the AARCH64 member of a six-constant per-architecture family at 2267–2272, and that its presence is linkage to `UefiDevicePathLib` rather than a vendor boot policy; that `BdsDxe/BdsEntry.c:838` builds the `Default PlatformRecovery` load option from that constant and `UefiBootManagerLib/BmBoot.c:1099` appends it to BlockIo/SimpleFileSystem device paths; and therefore that the payload can reach `\EFI\BOOT\BOOTAA64.EFI` on removable media **without** `QcomBds`, without a reader for `BDS_Menu.cfg`, and without the stock `Boot USB First` toggle. **does not decide**: whether the six USB host drivers enumerate the stick on this hardware, which is the gate's actual unknown and needs the phone; whether `MsBootPolicy` orders, filters or defers to the PlatformRecovery option, since only the constant's presence is measured and not the policy that consumes it; whether `BootManagerMenuApp`'s menu shows the USB entry (it should, through `BmExpandMediaDevicePath`, but that is inference from linkage and not a read of the binary's control flow); whether the internal UFS's own ESP will be tried first and matter to a Setup run; and whether the map-derived `0x10` count of 88 was wrong by one because of a file with no image or a map line that is not a file — the image count is now measured and the map's count is not re-derived here. **Not an action**: `python3` over `/tmp/fvmain.bin` and `/usr/bin/grep` and `sed` over `work/uefi/Mu-Silicium/Mu_Basecore/` — all read-only, nothing written outside `/tmp`, no file in the repository changed except this step's own text, no QEMU process started or signalled, no device command issued. `device/dxe/UsbConfigDxe.efi` still `sha256 6943cc615f7d4ba502c87bcf14a76e6e1398975a4101ed2711ba9e1c6e2566f5`. **Working state**: the two `--no-tpm` runs have now passed their stops — control pid 1386277 and bypass pid 1389516 were under `SECS=10800` from about 10:57, so their last frames are the 77 and 76 counted at 13:31 and the census will not grow; `qemu-stick2` remains ended at `shot-121`; the two dry-run processes 468162 and 471324 are still alive. **device state**: unchanged — `adb devices` and `fastboot devices` both empty, both tty globs absent, `lsusb` showing only the two root hubs and a Huawei mouse, and `lsblk` showing no removable USB stick, which the gate itself requires. The three physical actions — a reset of the phone, the reboot to the bootloader, and the screen photograph `先读屏，再刷下一次` requires — remain outstanding, and `userdata` (107 GB, unbacked), the partition table and the firmware LUN remain untouched.

## Step 4.236 — the payload separates the two USB modes by DEPEX and not by order: the six host-stack drivers carry **no** dependency section at all, so their dispatch order is the firmware volume's own file order, and that order is `XhciPciEmulation` → `XhciDxe` → `UsbBusDxe` → `UsbKbDxe` → `UsbMassStorageDxe` — controller, host controller, bus, class drivers, a topological order of the stack — while the device-mode side is the gated side, `UsbDeviceDxe` waiting on `gEfiChipInfoProtocolGuid AND gEfiSMEMProtocolGuid AND gEfiPlatformInfoProtocolGuid AND gEfiAcpiSdtProtocolGuid` and `UsbConfigDxe` on `{E722B03F-B250-42CE-8EBD-5BD51812D037}`, which is the one GUID this repository's own instrumented DXE core names as `mP2GuidUsbCfg`; and `TRUE END` is a dependency section, so the map's "66 files carry a `0x13`" counts sections and not dependencies

**The census, over the six host drivers and the four controls, with the names resolved.** Reading each file's section stream from its own FFS header — found by scanning back from the image for a header whose `State` byte is `0x07` or `0xF8`, whose `Type` is in `0x01..0x20` and whose `Size` spans the image, because the earlier shortcut of assuming the PE32 is the first section is wrong for every file whose stream is `0x13 + 0x10 + 0x15` — gives:

- `XhciPciEmulation` (FFS `0x356168`, sections `0x10+0x15+0x14`), `XhciDxe` (`0x36d1a8`), `UsbBusDxe` (`0x379fe0`), `UsbKbDxe` (`0x383218`), `UsbMassStorageDxe` (`0x38c260`) — **no `0x13` section at all**. There is no dependency expression to satisfy, so nothing gates them.
- `UsbInitDxe` (`0x3c13d0`) — likewise no `0x13`.
- `UsbConfigDxe` (`0x3b9380`) — `PUSH {E722B03F-B250-42CE-8EBD-5BD51812D037} END`, eighteen bytes, `02 … 08`.
- `UsbMassStorageDxe` and `BdsDxe` (`0x470528`) — a `0x13` section that reads `TRUE END` (`06 08`), two bytes.
- `SimpleFbDxe` (`0x2abb50`) — `PUSH {AE37B942-457F-4C91-A196-D9669FD347A3} END`.
- `ButtonsDxe` (`0x2bdc40`) — `PUSH {AE37B942-457F-4C91-A196-D9669FD347A3} PUSH gEfiSMEMProtocolGuid PUSH {FA5F306B-F47D-4AC4-A47D-882F8204EC30} AND AND END`.
- `UsbDeviceDxe` (`0x3a62f8`) — `PUSH gEfiChipInfoProtocolGuid PUSH gEfiSMEMProtocolGuid PUSH gEfiPlatformInfoProtocolGuid PUSH gEfiAcpiSdtProtocolGuid AND AND AND END`.

The four device-side names resolve in this tree: `gEfiSMEMProtocolGuid` at `Silicon/Qualcomm/QcomPkg/QcomPkg.dec:60`, `gEfiPlatformInfoProtocolGuid` at `:67`, `gEfiChipInfoProtocolGuid` at `:70`, and `gEfiAcpiSdtProtocolGuid` from the build's own `Build/gauguinPkg/DEBUG_CLANGPDB/FV/Guid.xref:313`. `{AE37B942-457F-4C91-A196-D9669FD347A3}` and `{FA5F306B-F47D-4AC4-A47D-882F8204EC30}` are in no `.dec`, `.h` or `.c` in the tree and are unresolved here.

**The one GUID that matters most is already this project's own instrument target.** `{E722B03F-B250-42CE-8EBD-5BD51812D037}` — the vendor USB Config protocol, and the dependency `UsbConfigDxe` declares — is written into this repository's modified DXE core as `STATIC CONST EFI_GUID mP2GuidUsbCfg = { 0xE722B03F, 0xB250, 0x42CE, { 0x8E, 0xBD, 0x5B, 0xD5, 0x18, 0x12, 0xD0, 0x37 }}` at `Mu_Basecore/MdeModulePkg/Core/Dxe/Hand/DriverSupport.c:49`, with count sites tracing `Supported`, `Start` and `CoreConnectController` against an `E722B03F`-carrying controller under the headings `P2SUPP: step 4.181` and, in `Dispatcher/Dispatcher.c:545`, `P2RECONN: 4.182`. So the payload's `UsbConfigDxe` — the blob this project pins to `sha256 6943cc615f7d4ba502c87bcf14a76e6e1398975a4101ed2711ba9e1c6e2566f5` — depends on exactly the protocol the instrument watches, which is what makes the earlier device-mode tracing measurable at all, and it is a reason to keep that blob byte-identical that is stronger than the record has so far given.

**What the census buys for the gate, and what it does not.** The host stack being ungated is the precondition the gate needs: the six drivers will be dispatched in the volume's file order, and that order — `XhciPciEmulation` at `0x356168` before `XhciDxe` at `0x36d1a8` before `UsbBusDxe` at `0x379fe0` before the class drivers at `0x383218` and `0x38c260` — is a topological order of the stack, so the controller that owns the PCI function is installed before the driver that consumes it and the bus before its classes. The device-mode side is separated by its own gates: `UsbDeviceDxe` cannot dispatch until ChipInfo, SMEM, PlatformInfo and ACPI SDT all exist, and `UsbConfigDxe` not until the vendor USB Config protocol exists, so the two modes do not contend for the controllers in the same pass. Against that, the census says nothing about whether the controllers' register windows are the ones the board actually has, and nothing about whether a boot services-era `XhciDxe` can bring up a port before the OS's own XHCI driver takes over — those remain the unflashed half, and the DEPEX reading does not shorten it.

**decides**: the section-by-section dependency census above, with the six host drivers carrying no `0x13` section, `UsbMassStorageDxe` and `BdsDxe` carrying `TRUE END`, `UsbConfigDxe` carrying `PUSH {E722B03F-…} END`, `SimpleFbDxe` one push, `ButtonsDxe` three operands under two `AND`s, and `UsbDeviceDxe` four operands under three; the resolution of four of those GUIDs to `gEfiSMEMProtocolGuid`, `gEfiPlatformInfoProtocolGuid`, `gEfiChipInfoProtocolGuid` and `gEfiAcpiSdtProtocolGuid` in `QcomPkg.dec` and `Guid.xref`; that `{E722B03F-B250-42CE-8EBD-5BD51812D037}` is the same GUID this repository's instrumented DXE core declares as `mP2GuidUsbCfg` at `DriverSupport.c:49`; that the six host drivers' FFS offsets are a topological order of the stack; and that a `0x13` section count is a count of sections and not of dependencies, since two of the files that carry one carry `TRUE END`. **does not decide**: whether any of the six host drivers' entry points succeed on this hardware, which needs the phone; what `{AE37B942-457F-4C91-A196-D9669FD347A3}` and `{FA5F306B-F47D-4AC4-A47D-882F8204EC30}` are, neither appearing in any `.dec`, `.h` or `.c` in the tree; whether the DXE dispatcher's discovery order for ungated drivers is exactly ascending FFS offset on this core, which is the reason the topological order above is a favourable sign rather than a guarantee; and whether `UsbInitDxe`, dispatching last of the six, is a setup-only driver or participates in the host path. **Not an action**: `python3` over `/tmp/fvmain.bin` and `/tmp/fvmain-names.txt`, and `/usr/bin/grep` over `work/uefi/Mu-Silicium/` — all read-only; new files this step writes are `/tmp/depex.txt` and `/tmp/depex2.txt` and nothing else; no file in the repository changed except this step's own text; no QEMU process started or signalled and no device command issued. The background command `bfm3ikeqc` finished during this step and is **superseded** — the single frame shift and the six drivers' offsets it was computing are re-derived here from the volume's own section streams, and it must not be restarted. **Working state**: the two `--no-tpm` runs have passed their `SECS=10800` stops and write no further frames; `qemu-stick2` remains ended at `shot-121`; the two dry-run processes 468162 and 471324 are still alive and untouched. **device state**: unchanged — `adb devices` and `fastboot devices` empty, both tty globs absent, `lsusb` showing only the two root hubs and a Huawei mouse, `lsblk` showing no removable USB stick that the gate requires. The three physical actions — a reset of the phone, a reboot to the bootloader, and the screen photograph `先读屏，再刷下一次` requires before any payload boots — remain outstanding; `userdata` (107 GB, unbacked), the partition table and the firmware LUN remain untouched.

## Step 4.237 — P4's partition edit is built and verified against the device's **own recorded GPT**, and verifying it found the two gaps the P4 plan did not have: the backup holds **only the primary** — `GPT-sda.bin` is 17,408 bytes and ends inside LBA 4, so the secondary at LBA 30944255 was never read and the read that closes it is the last 12,288 bytes of `sda` — and the CRC rule this work had recorded for EDK2 was **backwards**, since the device's own primary header stores `c52f1afc` and its 64-entry array stores `651472fe` where plain `zlib.crc32` gives exactly those two values; and the rewrite it produces moves `userdata` from `2887680..30944250` to `2887680..14031101` and adds ESP, MSR and Windows without touching any of the other 33 entries, which is measured against the device's own 128-byte entry bytes and not against the tool's own parser

**Why this and not another payload read.** The P3 gate cannot be advanced from this host — it is a Windows 11 ARM64 installer booting off a stick and seeing the internal UFS, and it needs the phone, a stick and a photograph that `先读屏，再刷下一次` requires first. P4 has a part that does not: `docs/00` P4 step 3 is "read the pre-change GPT and keep the output", step 5 is the shrink, and both are host-side. Working on them does not spend the only irreversible resource in this project — it prepares for it, and it is the one thing that can still be made safer while the device is unreachable. So this step is P4 preparation, and it found the preparation was incomplete in two ways that would each have failed late.

**The recorded dump is the primary GPT only, and its own bytes say so.** `GPT-sda.bin` is 17,408 bytes: LBA 0 (the protective MBR), LBA 1 (the primary header at byte 4096), the entry array at `PartitionEntryLBA = 2` — 64 entries of 128 bytes, bytes 8192..16384 — and then 1024 bytes of LBA 4. That is 4 × 4096 + 1024, and it stops there. The header it contains names `AlternateLBA = 30944255`, i.e. byte 126,747,668,480 of a 126,747,672,576-byte LUN, and that byte is not in the file. So the backup is a **head-only dump of a two-header object**, and `docs/00` P4 step 3 asks for the GPT before the change: what was kept is the primary, the protective MBR and the array, and what is missing is the mirror — which a shrink must also rewrite, and which a firmware that prefers the secondary would read in preference to the primary. The tool refuses to plan without it (`exit 2`) rather than planning half a table, and it prints the exact missing read: **sectors 30944253 .. 30944255, the last 12,288 bytes of `sda`** — the 8,192-byte secondary entry array in the two sectors before the header, and the header itself in the last one.

**`AlternateLBA` is not `LastUsableLBA + 1` on this device, and the tool takes it from the header.** `LastUsableLBA` is 30944250 so the naive mirror address is 30944251, and the header's `AlternateLBA` is 30944255 — five sectors higher, consistent with a 30944256-sector LUN (`0..30944255`) whose last sector is the secondary header and whose two before it are its array. The tool carries `alt_lba_from_header` through the rewrite instead of recomputing it, which matters more than it looks: a rewrite that computed `LastUsableLBA + 1` would stamp a well-formed secondary into LBA 30944251..30944253, where the firmware does not look for one, and leave the real mirror at 30944255 stale — so the shrink would appear to take, the device would come up on the old table, and the failure would present as `userdata` reverting rather than as a CRC error. That is the specific way this operation is usually got wrong.

**The CRC rule was recorded backwards, and the device is the instrument that says so.** The primary header's stored CRC is `c52f1afc`; `zlib.crc32` over that same 92-byte header with its own CRC field zeroed is `c52f1afc`. The stored `PartitionEntryArrayCRC32` is `651472fe`; `zlib.crc32` over the 8,192 bytes at byte 8192 is `651472fe`. Both match, and only `zlib.crc32` matches. So EDK2's `CalculateCrc32` — `BaseLib/Crc32.c`, which opens `Crc = 0xFFFFFFFF`, folds the reflected polynomial `0xEDB88320` and closes `return Crc ^ 0xFFFFFFFF` — **is** standard CRC-32 and **is** `zlib.crc32`; what this work had recorded ("reflected, init 0xFFFFFFFF, **no** final inversion … deliberately not `zlib.crc32`") is wrong in its reason. The implementation was right anyway — the loop in `tools/gpt-shrink-userdata.py` already ends `return crc ^ 0xFFFFFFFF` — so nothing produced from it is invalid, and the docstring is corrected in place with the two device CRCs named as the evidence rather than the source. It is written down because the wrong rule and the right one differ on every input, so an instrument built on the recorded rule would have rejected a correct table or accepted a wrong one, and the only thing that caught it was checking the tool against bytes the firmware itself had stamped. The same is now true of the entry **type GUIDs**: the tool's `USERDATA_TYPE` had `F50D-B242-9F47-82B45C2531D7` where the device's own entry reads `1B81E7E6-F50D-419B-A739-2AEEF8DA3335`, and that class of slip is invisible without a real table to compare against.

**The plan, in the recorded table's own addressing.** `userdata` is entry 34 of 64 slots (35 in use) and the **last occupied entry** — the tool requires that, because it is only cheap when it is last — with type `1B81E7E6-F50D-419B-A739-2AEEF8DA3335` and LBA `2887680..30944250` (114,919,714,816 B = 107.03 GiB). The rewrite holds its start and moves only its end:

- `userdata` — `2887680 .. 30944250` → `2887680 .. 14031101` — 42.51 GiB after the shrink
- ESP — `14031104 .. 14162175` — 536,870,912 B — 512.00 MiB, type `C12A7328-F81F-11D2-BA4B-00A0C93EC93B`
- MSR — `14162176 .. 14166271` — 16,777,216 B — 16.00 MiB, type `E3C9E316-0B5C-4DB8-817D-F92DF00215AE`
- Windows — `14166272 .. 30944250` — 68,722,601,984 B — 64.00 GiB, type `EBD0A0A2-B9E5-4433-87C0-68B6B72699C7`

Every new start is aligned and Windows is given the **remainder up to `LastUsableLBA`** rather than a precomputed size, because the natural sizes came up exactly 5 sectors short once alignment padding was added and a table that overruns `LastUsableLBA` is one a firmware may reject wholesale. `userdata`'s 42.51 GiB and the 512 MiB ESP are choices, not measurements: they are sized to be comfortably above Windows' own minimums and to leave the phone usable, and nothing here has run an install that would say whether they are right.

**The verification, run on the device's own entry bytes and not on the tool's own parser.** The recorded dump is head-only, so a whole-LUN stand-in was built from it — sparse, 126,747,672,576 B, 56 disk blocks, the recorded head plus a correctly-stamped secondary — and the tool was run against *that* to produce `/tmp/p4out/GPT-sda-head.bin` (16,384 B), `/tmp/p4out/GPT-sda-tail.bin` (12,288 B) and `/tmp/p4out/GPT-sda-plan.json`. The checks below use **no code from the tool** — `struct` and `zlib.crc32` only, now that the device has established which CRC that is:

- the synthetic LUN's LBA 0..3 are **byte-identical** to the recorded dump's, so the plan was computed against the device's own table and not a re-typed one;
- the rewritten head's entries **0..33 are byte-identical** to the device's recorded 128-byte entries, and exactly four differ — 34 (its new last LBA) plus the three additions. That is "no other partition moved", **measured**, which is the claim P4 step 5 turns on because it is what makes the change survivable without a backup of the other 33;
- LBA 0, the protective MBR — signature `55aa`, type `ee`, start LBA 1, size 4,294,967,295 — is byte-identical to the device's;
- the primary header differs from the device's in **8 bytes**: offsets `0x10..0x13`, its own CRC, and `0x58..0x5b`, the array CRC (which must change, because the array changed). `MyLBA` 1, `AlternateLBA` 30944255, `FirstUsableLBA` 6 and `LastUsableLBA` 30944250 are all preserved, and the entry count and entry size are untouched;
- the 12,288-byte tail block is `[array 8192 B][header 4096 B]` — header `MyLBA 30944255`, `AlternateLBA 1`, `PartitionEntryLBA 30944253`, both CRCs valid, and its array **byte-identical** to the primary's, which is what "the two GPTs agree" means for a table that was edited in both;
- the three additions' type GUIDs render as the three above, and `userdata`'s type is unchanged.

**And an instrument error of my own inside the verification, recorded because it reads exactly like a defect in the table.** The first cross-check read the secondary header at `tail[4096:4096+92]` — the *middle* sector — and duly printed `MyLBA = 12498151367908266660`, `AlternateLBA = 655360` and `header CRC BAD`. None of that was the table's: the header is in the **last** sector of the three, which is the LBA the header names, and the two before it are the array. A verifier that reads the wrong offset and reports `BAD` is evidence about the verifier, and the general form of this — an instrument whose failure mode is indistinguishable from the finding it is looking for — is now the third instance in this work, after 4.231's packed-image name scan and 4.235's `e_lfanew` bound.

**P4 step 1 now has something to verify against, because it had nothing.** There is no digest manifest under `~/backup/gauguin`: `/usr/bin/grep -cE '^[0-9a-f]{64}' backup.log` returns 0, and there is no `*.sha256` or `*.md5` anywhere below it. "Re-verify the backups" therefore had no baseline, which is not a step that can be passed by re-reading the files. `~/backup/gauguin/SHA256SUMS` is now written — 113 lines, 107 `part-*.img`, 5 `LUN-*.img` and `GPT-sda.bin`, 14,063,158,272 B hashed in 39 s — placed **beside** `images/` rather than inside it, with no file under `images/` opened for writing. Against it, `part-boot.img` re-measures to `50ef59beb17e75de1e749b7d261eb41a18d9cca025befb3357e43e239de78ef3`, which is the `EXPECT` pinned at `tools/restore-stock-boot.sh:36`, so the one image this project would need in order to restore `boot` is intact and named. The manifest is the baseline for a *future* check: it cannot certify that the dump was faithful when it was taken, only that nothing has changed since today, and that is the strongest statement 4.237 is entitled to make.

**What the correction to the earlier steps is.** Both 4.235 and 4.236 close by saying the two `--no-tpm` guests "have passed their `SECS=10800` stops and write no further frames". They had not. At 13:51 the control is qemu pid 1386277 on `work/win11/qemu-notpm-control` (`-display none`, `SECS=10800` from `tools/qemu-boot-win11-iso.sh:59`) with 2:54:43 elapsed, 41.8% of a core and **88** shots, and the bypass is pid 1389516 on `qemu-notpm-bypass` with 2:53:45, 40.9% and **87** — against the 77 and 76 those steps read at 13:31, so both are still alive and still writing on the two-minute cadence, and both are due to stop at about **13:57** and **13:58**, not before. `qemu-stick` (172 files, last `shot-089.ppm`) and `qemu-stick2` (238, last `shot-121.ppm`) remain ended and were not written.

**decides**: that `~/backup/gauguin/images/GPT-sda.bin` is a 17,408-byte **head-only** dump — protective MBR, primary header, the 64 × 128-byte array at LBA 2, and 1024 bytes of LBA 4 — and therefore does **not** contain the secondary GPT its own header names at `AlternateLBA` 30944255, so `docs/00` P4 step 3's "read the pre-change GPT" is one third done and the missing read is sectors **30944253..30944255**, the last 12,288 bytes of `sda`; that `AlternateLBA` 30944255 differs from `LastUsableLBA + 1` 30944251, so the mirror address must come from the header and never be recomputed; that EDK2's `CalculateCrc32` **does** apply the final inversion and **is** `zlib.crc32`, established by the two CRCs the device's own primary header and entry array store (`c52f1afc`, `651472fe`), which corrects the rule this work had recorded and the comment `tools/gpt-shrink-userdata.py` carried; that `userdata` is entry 34 of 64, the last occupied one, type `1B81E7E6-F50D-419B-A739-2AEEF8DA3335`, LBA `2887680..30944250`; that the rewrite yields `userdata` `2887680..14031101` at 42.51 GiB with ESP `14031104..14162175` (512.00 MiB), MSR `14162176..14166271` (16.00 MiB) and Windows `14166272..30944250` (64.00 GiB), and that entries 0..33 of the rewritten head are **byte-identical** to the device's own recorded entries while the protective MBR is byte-identical and the primary header differs only in its two CRC fields; that `~/backup/gauguin/SHA256SUMS` now exists with 113 lines over 107 `part-*.img`, 5 `LUN-*.img` and `GPT-sda.bin`, and that `part-boot.img` matches the pinned `EXPECT` at `tools/restore-stock-boot.sh:36`; and that the two `--no-tpm` runs were **still live and still writing frames** at 13:51, correcting 4.235 and 4.236. **does not decide**: whether the tool's secondary header is right where the device cannot be consulted, since the device's secondary was never read and the tool's is verified only for internal consistency, its `MyLBA`/`PartitionEntryLBA`/`AlternateLBA` arrangement and its array's byte-identity with the primary — the CRC *algorithm* it uses is now measured, the bytes of the mirror it must match are not; whether 512 MiB of ESP and 42.51 GiB of `userdata` are the right sizes, neither being measured against an install that has run; **what filesystem `userdata` holds and whether it can be resized at all** — the tool edits the partition table and deliberately resizes nothing, so P4 step 5 is two operations and only the first of them is prepared here, and the second has no instrument in this repository and no bytes in the backup, since `userdata`'s contents were never dumped and `fastboot fetch` is not to be used; whether the LUN's 4096-byte logical sector size is what Windows Setup will see, the plan being expressed in the recorded table's own addressing; whether Windows Setup's own partitioning would agree with this plan or fight it; and whether the firmware re-derives anything from the GPT rather than trusting it. **Not an action**: `python3` (`tools/gpt.py`, `tools/gpt-shrink-userdata.py` and inline scripts) over `/tmp/p4test/sda.img`, `~/backup/gauguin/images/GPT-sda.bin` and `/tmp/p4out/`; `sha256sum` over `~/backup/gauguin/images/`; `/usr/bin/grep`, `wc`, `ls`, `ps`, `date`, `lsblk`, `lsusb`, `adb devices`, `fastboot devices`; all read-only. ## Step 4.238 — the head-only GPT dump is a `dd bs=512 count=34` taken on a **4096-byte-sector** LUN, and the backup script is fixed to capture both halves; the live `/proc/device-tree`'s `status` census is the hardware-existence test the phases need — 170 `status` properties, 115 `ok` and 3 `okay` against **52 `disabled`** — and it decides which of the two described variants of each peripheral the board actually populates: `ssphy@88e8000` disabled and `mdss_dp_pll@ae90000` disabled, so the phone presents **USB 2.0 and DSI only**, `wcd938x-codec` disabled where `wcd937x-codec` is `ok`, while `mss@4080000` and `lpass@3000000` carry no `status` at all; and the stock firmware carries **no ACPI**, so every device node a Windows install can bind has to come from ASL this project writes

**The dump's shape has a cause, and it is one line of `dd`.** 4.237 measured that `~/backup/gauguin/images/GPT-sda.bin` is 17,408 bytes, ends inside LBA 4, and holds only the primary GPT. It is not a truncation and not a bad read: `~/backup/gauguin/backup.sh`'s `dump_gpt` ran `dd if=/dev/block/sda bs=512 count=34` — which is the canonical GPT layout on a **512-byte-sector** disk, MBR plus primary header plus 32 entry sectors plus the secondary header — and these LUNs are 4096-byte-sector. `dd` reads in `bs`-sized chunks regardless of the device's own sector size, so the command returned the first 17,408 bytes of `sda`: the protective MBR (LBA 0, 4096 B), the primary header (LBA 1, 4096 B), the 64 × 128-byte entry array (LBA 2, 8192 B) and 1024 bytes of LBA 4. That is the file, byte for byte, and it never reached `AlternateLBA` 30944255. **The script is fixed in place** — head `bs=4096 count=4`, and the mirror as `bs=4096 skip=$((alt-2)) count=3` into a sibling `GPT-sda-tail.bin`, with `alt` passed in as an argument rather than recomputed because on this LUN 30944255 is not `LastUsableLBA + 1` 30944251. The existing 17,408-byte head is byte-identical to the first 16,384 bytes of what the fixed head dump would write, so the old file stays and only the tail is missing; `tools/gpt-shrink-userdata.py` already accepts a `*-tail.bin` sibling, so the two halves complete each other with nothing re-read and nothing written. `bash -n` passes. `~/backup/gauguin` is not a git repository, which is why the fix is written down here: this paragraph is its only durable record, and the fix itself runs at the next device contact.

**`status` is the selector, and it is the one property that says whether hardware exists.** The live tree carries **170** `status` properties: **115** read `ok`, **3** read `okay` and **52** read `disabled`. `ok` and `okay` are the same value to `of_device_is_available`, so 118 nodes are enabled and 52 are not, and a device is described in the tree in *both* variants — the populated one and the unpopulated one — with `status` choosing. Four determinations follow, each of which the docs did not have:

- **USB is USB 2.0 on this board.** `ssusb@a600000` (`qcom,dwc-usb3-msm`) and `qusb@88e3000` (`qcom,qusb2phy-v2`) carry no `status`, i.e. enabled; `ssphy@88e8000` — `compatible = "qcom,usb-ssphy-qmp-dp-combo"`, the QMP SuperSpeed/DisplayPort PHY whose registers 4.226 mapped — reads `disabled`. The port therefore comes up on the USB 2.0 PHY, which is what the P3 gate has to be built around: a **USB 2.0 stick** is the right medium, no SuperSpeed behaviour belongs in the gate's expectations, and a stick that needs USB 3.0 would fail for a reason that has nothing to do with the six drivers under test.
- **Display is DSI only.** `mdss_mdp`, `dsi0_ctrl`, `dsi0_pll` and `dsi_phy0` are enabled; `mdss_dp_pll@ae90000` reads `disabled`. No DisplayPort, so the panel work has exactly one output path.
- **The audio codec is WCD937x.** `wcd937x-codec` reads `ok` while `wcd938x-codec` reads `disabled`, and the same split holds for the `wcd937x-rx/tx-slave` against `wcd938x-rx/tx-slave` pairs under `bolero-cdc`. The two codecs are mutually exclusive in the tree and the board has the 937x.
- **The compute remotes are described as present.** `mss@4080000` (the modem remote), `lpass@3000000` (ADSP), `turing@8300000` (CDSP), `npu@9800000`, `venus@aab0000`, `kgsl-hyp` and `ipa_fws` all carry no `status`, and `msm-adsp-loader` reads `ok`. So the ceiling recorded for this device — no modem, no cameras — is not "the tree does not describe them"; the tree describes them and does not disable them. What that ceiling means is a P5 statement about whether Windows can drive them, and this step does not move it.

**The stock firmware has no ACPI at all, which puts the hardware-coverage work entirely on this project.** Over the **238** files extracted from the stock `xbl.img`, none carries the Edk2 `AcpiTables` file GUID `7E374E25-8E01-4FEE-87F2-390C23C606CD`, none is named `*acpi*`, and `xbl.img` itself — 7,327,744 bytes — contains no `DSDT`, `FACP`, `APIC` or `GTDT` signature at any offset. There is no vendor ACPI on this device and never was: Android and the stock kernel read the device tree, so the payload's `AcpiTables` is the **only** ACPI this board has ever had. Two consequences. First, the payload's DSDT being byte-identical to `Silicium-ACPI/Platforms/Xiaomi/gauguin/DSDT.aml` is what that file must be, since there is no vendor DSDT it could have come from. Second, and the load-bearing one for the standing goal: hardware coverage is **ASL this project writes**, not firmware it recovers — and describing a device in ACPI makes it *visible*, while a driver makes it *usable*, and of those two only the first is firmware work. Touch, WLAN, camera and audio need both halves, and the second half for a FocalTech panel or a WCN3990 is the part no amount of ACPI work removes.

**The information to write that ASL with is already in the backup, and the earlier "0 hits" reading was about the wrong container.** The base SoC DTS the payload hands the kernel, `work/uefi/Mu-Silicium/Resources/DTBs/gauguin.dts` — 5,474 lines, 865 nodes, `compatible = "xiaomi,gauguin", "qcom,sm7225"` — carries the SoC-level nodes and no client devices: `ufshc` twice, `usb` twenty times, six `i2c@` nodes, thirteen `dsi` mentions, two `wcd93` mentions, and `988000` twice (the `i2c@988000` the panel sits on), with **no** `focaltech`, no `novatek`, no `icnss` and no `spi@`. A client device is described by the DTBO overlay, so a search for one in the base DTS returns zero because it could not return anything else — which is what 4.233 measured as a gap and what it is not. The **live** tree, `~/backup/gauguin/dt/`, dumped from `/proc/device-tree` on 2026-09-22, is base *plus* the applied overlay (`chosen/bootargs` carries `androidboot.dtb_idx=8`), and it holds all of them: `soc/qcom,icnss@18800000` (`qcom,icnss`), `soc/bt_wcn3990` (`qca,wcn3990`), `soc/i2c@988000/focaltech@38` (`focaltech,fts_ts`), `soc/ts_novatek` (`novatek,NVT-ts-spi`), `soc/qcom,cci0` and `cci1`, `csid0`, `csid1`, `csid2`, `csid-lite@acc8000`, `cam-cpas@ac40000`, three `camera-flash` nodes, `lpass@3000000`, `msm-audio-apr`, `bolero-cdc`, `ipa@1e00000`, `rmnet-ipa3`, `ufshc@1d84000`, `ufsphy_mem@1d87000`, `ssusb@a600000`, `fingerprint_fpc`, `fingerprint_goodix` and NFC as pinctrl only. Every device that would need an ACPI node has address, interrupt, clock, supply and compatible recorded, in bytes already in the backup — so the gap is authoring, and it is ours.

**And an instrument error of my own, the third of this shape.** The first pass over "which nodes are disabled" walked the tree with `os.walk` and tested `os.path.basename(node) == "status"` — but `os.walk` yields **directories**, and `status` is a file, so the test never matched and the census came back **0** disabled nodes against a tree that has **52**. It was caught only by reading one node's `status` directly and getting `disabled\0` from a node the walk had just called enabled. A scan whose blank result reads as "the board has every peripheral the tree names" is the same failure as 4.231's name scan over a packed image and 4.237's secondary header read at the wrong offset, and this tree invites it because the property it is looking for is one file among twelve per node.

**decides**: that `GPT-sda.bin`'s 17,408 bytes are `dd bs=512 count=34` over a 4096-byte-sector LUN — MBR, primary header, the 64 × 128-byte array, and 1024 bytes of LBA 4 — and that `~/backup/gauguin/backup.sh` now captures the head as `bs=4096 count=4` and the mirror as `bs=4096 skip=$((alt-2)) count=3` into `GPT-sda-tail.bin` with `AlternateLBA` supplied rather than recomputed; ## Step 4.239 — the platform as committed could not be **installed**, and the command the failing gate tells you to run to fix it silently **disarms the P3 host stack**: Step 4.215 rewrote the comments in `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl` and never re-ran `tools/make_uefi_platform.py`, so the generated copy under `uefi/` was left stale and `tools/sync-uefi-platform.sh`'s own staleness gate — the check written for exactly this — refused the tree; regenerating the way its message says, without `--xhci-host`, sets `USE_XHCI_HOST_DRIVER` back to `0` and removes all three host-stack INF lines **while leaving the three staged blob directories on disk**, which every other check in that script accepts, so the two halves are now checked against each other and a flagless tree with blobs in it is refused by name; with the flag the regeneration is HEAD's tree byte for byte apart from the one file that was stale, and that file's AML does not change — 12,341 bytes, 515 named objects, byte-identical to the DSDT inside the `AcpiTables` the last payload carries

**The defect, and it is in HEAD rather than in the working tree.** `tools/sync-uefi-platform.sh` carries a gate written after a build was once silently lost to it — `cmp -s "$REPO/tools/acpi/gauguin.asl" "$GEN/Silicium-ACPI/Platforms/Xiaomi/gauguin/gauguin.asl"`, `die` if they differ, now at `tools/sync-uefi-platform.sh:158` — and at HEAD that `cmp` **differs**, so the script that installs the platform into the Mu-Silicium checkout and compiles the DSDT dies before it copies anything. The cause is a step that touched one side and not the other: `a6f35f7` (Step 4.215, 2026-09-29 04:34:43) added 40 lines of comment to `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl` — 6,698 lines, 349,956 B — and the generated copy beside `AcpiTables.inf`, last committed by `3873956` (Step 4.94, 2026-09-26 04:22:52), is still 6,668 lines and 347,796 B. So this is not a stale checkout, a dirty tree or a missing artifact; it is the committed state, and `git status` is clean. It is the failure that gate exists for, arriving through the gate's own subject.

**And the difference is comments, which is what makes it worth a step rather than a one-line fix.** The delta is 35 insertions and 5 deletions, all of it prose — `20` where 4.215 measured `21` in the BTNS/PM01 pairing, in four places, plus the two census paragraphs 4.215 added. Compiled, the two files are the same table: both produce **12,341 bytes** of AML with **515 named objects** and the same digest `0f5df26b424ab609027aa388ef02cbc82907f0b83ee72411433ec6c30c3ffa47`, which is also the payload's DSDT. So no byte of any firmware is wrong. What was wrong is that the repository could not be built, and the repair the error message names is the one that costs a payload — see below.

**The trap: `--xhci-host` is not a detail of the driver list, it is the flag that stages the blobs, and the flagless run does not take them away.** Measured four ways, because the three statements are easy to conflate:

- **The flag is what stages the blobs.** In a tree that never had them — `make_uefi_platform.py --out /tmp/gen-withflag --xhci-host` — the generator prints `USB host stack: staging from Binaries/bitra` and `USB host stack: 3 INF line(s) in !if $(USE_XHCI_HOST_DRIVER) == 1`, and creates `Binaries/gauguin/QcomPkg/Drivers/{XhciPciEmulationDxe,XhciDxe,UsbInitDxe}`. The same fresh tree generated without the flag has **no** `Binaries/gauguin/QcomPkg` at all — 21 files, platform and SoC packages and `RawFiles` only. So staging is flag-conditional.
- **Nothing removes them again.** `stage_sibling_blobs` (`tools/make_xbl_binaries.py:230`) documents itself as "additive and idempotent: it overwrites the three directories it owns and touches nothing else", and that is exactly what it does. A flagless regeneration *over* a tree that had them therefore leaves all three directories on disk and drops only the INF lines and the DSC variable: measured on this repository, `XhciPciEmulationDxe` and `XhciDxe` still present, the `Xhci`/`UsbInitDxe` match count in `Include/DXE.inc` **0**, `USE_XHCI_HOST_DRIVER = 0`.
- **That half-tree used to be installed without a word.** Every gate in the script passes it: the eight `need` files exist, the ACPI copy is fresh, the table names resolve, the blobs the INFs reference are all present. The missing INFs leave no hole to notice — the volume simply has three fewer drivers — and the payload it costs is the P3 payload built without the transport the whole gate is about, which no amount of reading the diff afterwards would reveal as a *change*.
- **So the check is between the halves, not against the flag.** A tree that never used the flag has neither half and is coherent; a tree generated with it has both. What cannot be coherent is a blob staged with no INF line for it, or an INF line with no blob behind it, and those are the two states the new block refuses — by name, before the install stages run, with the DSC value printed so the configuration being installed is in the log rather than inferred. The comment at the binaries stage that said the three blobs "sit behind `USE_XHCI_HOST_DRIVER` in the generated driver lists, so copying them in does nothing on its own" is corrected in place: true of what the build consumes, and silent about the thing that actually bites, which is that their *presence* is a fact about a past run and not about this one.

**The gate, tested on four tree states rather than reasoned about.** The block extracted verbatim from the script and run against: the repository regenerated **with** `--xhci-host` → `host stack (3 of 3 drivers, USE_XHCI_HOST_DRIVER = 1)`, exit 0; the fresh flagless tree → `host stack (0 of 3 drivers, USE_XHCI_HOST_DRIVER = 0)`, exit 0, which is the case that must keep passing; a two-file tree carrying the INF line and no blob → dies naming `XhciPciEmulationDxe` and the missing file, the build failure it would otherwise become minutes later; and this repository regenerated **without** the flag → dies with `XhciPciEmulationDxe is staged under Binaries/gauguin but DXE.inc carries no INF line for it - this tree was generated without --xhci-host over one that had it, so the blob would ship in no volume`, which is the whole point. `bash -n` passes. The tree was then regenerated the correct way — `python3 tools/make_uefi_platform.py --xhci-host` — and `git status --porcelain uefi` reports **one** modified file, the stale ASL, with `DXE.inc`, `gauguin.dsc` and the blob directories back to HEAD's bytes. That is the useful property of the repair: the canonical command reproduces the committed tree exactly except for the thing that was wrong, so any future drift shows up as a diff instead of hiding in a regenerated file nobody read.

**The ACPI table package is complete, and the DSDT in the last payload is the committed source.** All six `[Binaries]` names in `AcpiTables.inf` resolve across the three `PackagesPath` roots the sync checks — `Common/SSDT.aml` at the Silicium-ACPI root, `Moorea/{APIC,FACP,FACS,GTDT}.aml` under `Silicon/Qualcomm`, and `DSDT.aml` in the package's own directory, which is the one the sync compiles there from the `.asl` beside it, which is why the tracked directory holding only `AcpiTables.inf` and `gauguin.asl` is the intended state rather than a missing file. `iasl` (20250404) on the committed `gauguin.asl` reports **0 Errors**, 26 warnings, 93 remarks, 383 optimizations — the remarks are the `_CRS` templates' named objects, which every table in this corpus carries. And the result is the payload's: the built FFS `7E374E25-8E01-4FEE-87F2-390C23C606CD.ffs` is 13,702 bytes, its `SEC2.2.raw` is 12,345 and the **12,341 bytes at offset 4 are byte-identical** to the freshly compiled AML. So the `AcpiTables` the device would be handed is this file, and regenerating changes none of it — which is what makes the 40-line comment delta a build gate and not a table change, and is the reason the cheap repair is the correct one.

**The P3 payload re-checked on the file, and the one reading of it that nearly became a false finding.** `tools/abl-boot-check.py work/out/usb-host/Mu-gauguin-xhci-host-gzip.img` still returns **ok** — every check ABL makes before it hands control over, which is the same answer it gave when the payload was built and is now re-run against the same bytes (`sha256 43d8d7abb83656d60588efad038070c0a8b7b31ae6d5976600f0bedce4e76cbc`, 1,173,504 B). What the step adds is the arithmetic behind one sentence of `docs/07`: that the payload carries the ARM64 magic where ABL reads it.

- The file is an Android boot image, header **v1**, `page_size` 0x800, `kernel_size` 1,168,602 (571 pages), `ramdisk_size` **5**; the kernel region begins at file offset 2,048.
- That region is not a gzip stream but **two objects**: a gzip member of exactly **1,081,008 bytes (0x107eb0)** and then an **87,594-byte device tree** beginning `d0 0d fe ed`, whose own `totalsize` field is `0x1562a` = 87,594. The two sum to `kernel_size`.
- The member inflates to **3,145,840 bytes**, and `ARMd` sits at **offset 0x38** of it with the u32 there equal to **0x644d5241** — the constant and the offset ABL's `Kernel mode check 32/64` loads (`ldr w2, [x22, #0x38]` … `movk w3, #0x644d`), with `x22` the decompressed image base. Its arm64 header reads `text_offset 0x9fc00000`, `image_size 0x300000`, `flags 0`.
- **The reading that nearly became a finding of my own.** `raw.find(b'ARMd')` returns **-1** over the whole 1,173,504-byte file, and `d[2048]` is not `0x1f` but part of the boot header — so the first pass concluded the image does not carry the magic, which would have contradicted `docs/07` and read as a defect in the payload. It carries it 0x38 bytes into the image ABL decompresses, and the file's own byte at 0x38 is inside the v1 header's `name` field, which is zeros. The same pass also hit `BadGzipFile: Not a gzipped file (b'\xd0\r')` from both `gzip.decompress` and `gzip.GzipFile` on that region and read it as an instrument failure; `\xd0\r` is the **device tree's** first two bytes, the reader had consumed the member and was looking for the next one. `zlib.decompressobj(31)` settles it — `unused_data` is 87,594 bytes — and the `0x107eb0` boundary is the one `tools/abl-boot-check.py` already reported for the tree, which is the tool's own `GZipPkgCheck` decompressor's stopping point. `tools/check-payload.py` imports `gzip` too and is unaffected because it reads `0x40` bytes and never reaches the boundary. Both mistakes are the shape this work keeps meeting — an instrument whose blank or loud answer is indistinguishable from the finding — and this is the fourth, after 4.231's packed-image name scan, 4.235's `e_lfanew` bound and 4.237's secondary header read a sector early.

**decides**: that at HEAD `tools/sync-uefi-platform.sh` dies on its own staleness gate because `uefi/Silicium-ACPI/Platforms/Xiaomi/gauguin/gauguin.asl` (6,668 lines, 347,796 B, last committed by `3873956` Step 4.94) does not match `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl` (6,698 lines, 349,956 B, last changed by `a6f35f7` Step 4.215), and that the two differ by comments only, compiling to the same 12,341-byte, 515-object AML `0f5df26b…`; that re-running `tools/make_uefi_platform.py --xhci-host` restores the gate and changes **one** file relative to HEAD, `DXE.inc`, `gauguin.dsc` and the staged blobs coming back byte-identical; that `--xhci-host` is what stages `XhciPciEmulationDxe`, `XhciDxe` and `UsbInitDxe` into `Binaries/gauguin/QcomPkg/Drivers/` and what sets `USE_XHCI_HOST_DRIVER = 1` with the three INF lines behind it, while `stage_sibling_blobs` is additive and idempotent and therefore leaves those three directories behind when a later run omits the flag; ## Step 4.240 — P4 step 1 closes at **113 of 113** and the P3 medium turns out to be incomplete in **three independent ways**, none of which is the firmware; and the P3 stick is now built and byte-verified, so the gate's blocker is the phone and not the medium: the assembly tool hit four real errors and the third of them was **this work's own model being wrong**, since the four driver filenames it refused to flatten are genuinely different files that must stay in separate directories

**P4 step 1: the baseline P4 step 5 restores from, checked for the first time since it was written.** P4's plan has carried "the backup is the only copy that will ever exist" as an assertion; this step is the measurement behind it. `~/backup/gauguin/SHA256SUMS` holds **113 lines** — 107 `part-*.img`, 5 `LUN-*.img` and `GPT-sda.bin` — beside `images/` rather than in it, and all **113 verify**. Two things about taking that measurement are worth recording, because the first attempt reported the opposite.

- **The manifest's paths are relative to `images/`.** Run from `~/backup/gauguin` — where the manifest lives, and the obvious place to run it — `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS` prints `113 listed files could not be read`, `0` OK and exits 1. Run from `~/backup/gauguin/images` as `sha256sum -c ../SHA256SUMS` it prints `113: OK` for every line. Nothing was wrong with the backup; the instrument was pointed at the wrong directory, which is the same failure as 4.233's and 4.238's corpus searches in the wrong container and is now the fifth.
- **The exit status is not the reading.** `sha256sum -c` exits 1 as soon as any listed file cannot be read, so the exit code says only "something in this run failed to open" — it is 1 for the broken run and would also be 1 for a run with one genuinely corrupt file among 113. The count of OK lines is the measurement; the exit status is not, and it was the OK count (113 of 113, nothing else) that this step is built on.
- The set is 14 GB, `part-boot.img` among it, and that file matches the `EXPECT` hash pinned at `tools/restore-stock-boot.sh:36` — the hash the restore path for the one partition this project is allowed to write is gated on.

**The P3 medium is incomplete in three independent ways, and all three are offline defects rather than firmware ones.** P3's gate is "a Windows 11 ARM64 installer boots off a USB stick and sees the internal UFS". That is a test of the firmware, and it is only a test of the firmware if the stick is capable of the test. The medium staged at `~/work/woa-ref/p3-medium-built` is not, in three separate respects — each measured, each independently sufficient to fail the gate:

- **The setup half has no install image.** `media1` is 265 MB: `sources/setup.exe`, `sources/winsetup.dll`, `boot/boot.sdi` — and **no** `boot.wim`, `install.wim` or `install.esd`. The install image exists in this tree and is 6.4 GB of `win11-25h2/install.wim` with 11 editions, sitting in a different directory and never placed into `sources/`. A stick built from `media1` alone runs setup and finds nothing to install.
- **The boot half's WIM is WinRE, not Setup.** `usb-p3` carries `EFI/BOOT/BOOTAA64.EFI`, `BOOT/BOOT.SDI` and `SOURCES/BOOT.WIM` — and that WIM holds **one** image, `Microsoft Windows Recovery Environment (arm64)`, 17,406 files, 446,983,676 bytes. Retail install media carries a second image in that same WIM named `Windows Setup`; this one does not, so booting it reaches the recovery tools and Setup has to be started from a command prompt.
- **Neither half carries a Qualcomm platform driver.** The WinPE DriverStore's 233 packages include exactly four Qualcomm entries — `qcgpio_i.inf`, `qci2c_i.inf`, `qctree_i.inf` (Microsoft's inbox `_i` flavour) and `storufs.inf` for the controller itself. **None of the 112 CABs** in the SC7280/Kodiak package is in there, so there is no PEP, no PMIC, no SPMI, no SCM, no GLINK and no ADSP in the image that is supposed to prove the platform works.

**`tools/make-p3-stick.sh` closes all three, and the result is verified against the artifacts rather than against the script's own success.** The tool merges the two halves, adds the install image split for FAT32, and injects the 112 CABs into the WinRE image at `X:\Drivers` with a `startnet.cmd` that runs `drvload` before `wpeinit`. Four runs, exit 0 on the fourth, `work/out/p3-stick` at **948 files and 7.3 GB**. What makes it a build and not a directory of files:

- **The WinRE image grew by exactly the driver tree and nothing else.** File count `17,406 → 18,176`, a delta of **770**, which is the number of files in the staged package tree to the file; total bytes `2,765,776,494 → 3,545,869,925`, a delta of **780,093,431** (747 MiB) against a `pkg/` tree of the same size. The image's name, image count and boot index are unchanged.
- **The driver tree is complete inside the WIM.** `wimlib-imagex dir` on `/Drivers` lists **885** entries — 770 files and 115 directories — and **112** of them are `.inf`, one per CAB. The 112 package directories are all present, `mcfg_subsys_ext7280/MCFG/` among them.
- **`startnet.cmd` landed byte-identical.** Extracted back out of the WIM and `cmp`-ed against the staged file: identical, 310 bytes.
- **The BCD the stick will be booted by is the WinPE one, and the two halves agreed on it.** `media1/efi/microsoft/boot/bcd` and `usb-p3/EFI/MICROSOFT/BOOT/BCD` are both 16,384 bytes and **byte-identical**, so which one the merge kept is not a question. Its UTF-16 strings are `\sources\boot.wim`, `\boot\boot.sdi` and `\windows\system32\boot\winload.efi` — the standard ramdisk boot entry, pointing at the merged tree's own `sources/boot.wim`.
- **The split is readable and carries the same editions as the source.** `install.swm` is 3,975,996,353 bytes and `install2.swm` is 2,832,695,943; both are under the FAT32 4 GiB ceiling of 4,294,967,295, which is why the split exists at all. `wimlib-imagex info` on the first part reports **11 images** with the same names and edition IDs as `install.wim` — `Core`, `CoreN`, `CoreSingleLanguage`, `Education`, `EducationN`, `Professional`, … — so the split is a split and not a truncation.
- Pinned for a stick written later: `sources/boot.wim` `sha256 11a4bb477268b49d5c6e36e48b83b8521ac901b3dd7584cb017bd24cc3b4124b`, `sources/install.swm` `sha256 72ecf464ae044399f4ccfb858e0bbea401d66ba4ceb8d68f307dbfea727aa080`. `efi/boot/bootaa64.efi` is present at 2,622,784 bytes — the removable-media path, which is the one that matters here, since there is no NVRAM entry on this device for a stick and 4.235 established that `EFI_REMOVABLE_MEDIA_FILE_NAME` is what expands to `\EFI\BOOT\BOOTAA64.EFI`.

**The four errors, and the third one was a wrong model rather than a wrong package.** Each was a real defect in the tool and none was in the inputs.

- **Run 1 — the merge silently produced two parallel trees.** `error: merge lost SOURCES/setup.exe`. `media1` spells its directories the way the medium does (`sources`, `boot`, `efi`) and `usb-p3` spells them the way the build tree does (`SOURCES`, `BOOT`, `EFI/MICROSOFT/BOOT`). On the FAT32 stick those are one directory each; on this host they are two, so a plain `cp -a` of both produced a tree with `sources/setup.exe` and `SOURCES/BOOT.WIM` side by side — not what the stick will look like, and a shape that hides the merge behind a check failing on a file that is present under the other spelling. The boot half is folded to lowercase on the way in, which is what the target filesystem means by those names anyway; where the halves overlap the boot half wins, being the half built for ARM64.
- **Run 2 — the flatten loop walked directories.** `cp: -r not specified; omitting directory '…/mcfg_subsys_ext7280/MCFG'`. The loop was `for f in "$d"*`, which expands over subdirectories as well as files; `find "$d" -maxdepth 1 -type f` fixes it, and it is the reason `MCFG/` survived to be verified above.
- **Run 3 — and this is the one worth the step, because the check was right and the design behind it was wrong.** `error: same filename, different contents across CABs: libcdsprpc.dll libcdsprpcarm32.dll qcfirmware7280.cat qcfirmware7280.cat libadsprpc.dll`. Every one of those four **is** a different file under the same name:
  - `qcfirmware7280.cat` exists in three variants — **11619**, **11648** and **11613** bytes, in `qcfirmware7280_EMMC`, `_NVME` and `_UFS` — and each variant's INF names it as a sibling, `CatalogFile = qcfirmware7280.cat`. Flattening hands two of the three the wrong catalog, and Windows rejects a driver whose catalog does not match its INF as unsigned. All three variants bind distinct ids (`UEFI\RES_{f9e77ef5-…}`, `{6f8e61f2-…}`, `{cc390084-…}`), so loading all three is unambiguous.
  - `libcdsprpc.dll` is **183448** bytes out of `qcadsprpc7280` and **183440** out of `qccamavs7280`; `libadsprpc.dll` is **183432** out of `qcadsprpc7280` and **175344** out of `qcSensorsConfigCrd7280`. Two CABs shipping their own build of the same-named binary is the normal case for a package set built over months, not a packaging error.
  - So the flatten step was removed rather than the check loosened. A Windows driver package **is** a directory: INF, CAT and SYS resolve against the INF's own location, which is why 46 of the 112 CABs — extension packages that add registry keys to another driver — carry an INF and no SYS and are still complete packages. The tree is preserved and `drvload` is pointed at each INF where it lies, via `for /r "X:\Drivers" %%i in (*.inf)`. The first version of the check would have "fixed" a problem that did not exist by destroying three catalogs.
- **Run 3 also exposed the cache.** After the model change the package list was still globbed out of the cache directory, which the previous version had left a `flat/` directory in — so the run reported **224 INFs in 113 package directories, 1.5 GB**, i.e. all 112 packages counted twice. The directory list is now derived from `$CABS` by name, so a stale directory in the cache cannot become a package. The measured shape, which also corrects a number this work had recorded from the contaminated count: **112 of 112 CABs hold an INF, with 67 `.sys` and 112 `.cat` beside them, and 46 of the 112 carry no `.sys` at all.** The earlier "45 carry an INF and no SYS" was `112 − 67`, which is the difference between two unlike quantities — 67 `.sys` files spread over 66 CABs — and the correct reading is 46 packages with none.
- **Run 4 — two mechanical ones.** `wimlib-imagex update` accepts exactly one `--command` and reads the remainder from stdin, so both edits now go in on one here-document; and two paths in the print-and-verify tail were still spelled `$OUT/SOURCES`, the uppercase form the lowercasing fix had removed everywhere else, which under `set -o pipefail` aborted the script **after** the 6.4 GB split had finished and reported exit 2 on a tree that was in fact complete.

**Hardware coverage, re-measured against a driver set rather than argued, and the answer is that this is ASL authoring and not a build problem.** `tools/acpi-hid-census.py --drivers ~/work/woa-ref/inf-7280 --bind --asl tools/acpi/gauguin.asl`: the Kodiak set is **112 `.inf` files, all UTF-16 with a BOM**, claiming **155 distinct `ACPI\` hardware ids**; `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl` declares **56 `_HID`/`_CID` values, 42 distinct**. Of the QCOM ids, **32 are claimed** — I2C8/I2C9/IC11 by `qci2c7280`, PMIC/PM01/PML0 by `qcpmic7280` and `qcpmicgpio7280`, the thermal zones by `qcpep.wd7280`, QGP0/QGP1 by `qcgpi7280`, GLNK by `qcglink7280`, ADC1 by `qcadc7280`, UAR2 by `qcuart7280`, UCS0 by `qcusbcucsi7280`, SCM0 by `qcscm`, IPCC by `qcipcc7280`, ABD by `qcabd` — and exactly **2 are not**:

- **`QCOM24A5` (UFS0)** — named nowhere in the Kodiak set at all, but this is the id that matters least, because the **inbox** `storufs.inf` claims it: line 82 `%ACPI\QCOM24A5.DeviceDesc%=UfsQualcomm8996Install, ACPI\QCOM24A5`, with `ExcludeFromSelect=ACPI\QCOM24A5` at line 40 and the description `"Qualcomm Universal Flash Storage (UFS) Host Controller"` at line 416. So the controller has a driver in WinPE already; what the controller needs in order to be *reachable* is the platform around it, which is what this stick now supplies.
- **`QCOM0A8B` (URS0)** — not claimed by any `.inf` on the ACPI bus, but the set **does** name it on another bus: `URS\QCOM0A8B&FUNCTION` in `QcUsbFnSsFilter7280.inf` and `URS\QCOM0A8B&HOST` in `QcXhciFilter7280.inf`. That is the device-mode/host-mode filter pair, and it means the URS node is a parent the set already builds on rather than a block with no driver anywhere.

And one binding this step re-read because it decides a subsystem: **`qcwlan7280.inf:32` binds `WPSS\VEN_QCOM&DEV_0A28`, not an `ACPI\` id.** WLAN is a WPSS child, so no amount of ASL on the ACPI namespace will produce a WLAN device — it needs WPSS-side child nodes plus `qcsubsys_ext_wpss`. The same shape applies to BT (`qcbtfmuart_hsp7280`). The genuinely uncovered subsystems, each now with a named blocker rather than a label:

- **Touch** — the chip is FocalTech at I2C address **0x38** on gauguin's I2C9. The closest reference node in this corpus is venus's `TSC5`, `_HID "FTCH5452"`, on **I2C5** at the same address `0x0038` and the same TLMM pins (`GpioInt {0x0017}`, `GpioIo {0x0016}`), against gauguin's live tree `focaltech,irq-gpio = 0x16` / `focaltech,reset-gpio = 0x15`. The WinPE inbox has only `hidi2c.inf` — Microsoft's HID-over-I2C, which needs `_HID`/`_CID` `ACPI0C50`/`MSFT8000` — and **no FocalTech INF exists in either the Kodiak package or the inbox set**. So touch needs both an ASL child node and a driver that does not exist anywhere in this tree. Open question, unchanged and now sharper: the live tree has `ts_novatek/status = ok` **as well as** `focaltech@38`, while `qcom,i2c-touch-active` names focaltech, so which chip is actually fitted is not settled by the tree.
- **Camera, audio, SLIMbus, ISP** — the Kodiak set carries `qccamisp7280`, `qccammipicsi7280`, `qcaudminiport_Base7280`, `qcslimbus7280` and more, so the drivers exist; the ASL nodes for them do not.

**decides**: that `~/backup/gauguin/SHA256SUMS` verifies **113 of 113** files with the manifest read from inside `images/` as `../SHA256SUMS`, that its paths are relative to `images/` and that its exit status is not the reading, and that P4 step 1 is therefore done; that the P3 medium had three independent offline defects — `media1` with no install image, a `BOOT.WIM` that is WinRE and not Setup, and no Qualcomm CAB installed in the WinPE DriverStore — and that `tools/make-p3-stick.sh` closes all three into `work/out/p3-stick`, 948 files and 7.3 GB, with the WinRE image's file count growing by exactly the 770 files of the driver tree, `/Drivers` holding 885 entries including 112 INFs in 112 package directories, `startnet.cmd` byte-identical inside the WIM, a BCD byte-identical across both halves pointing at `\sources\boot.wim`, and a two-part FAT32-legal split that reports the source's own 11 images; that a flattened driver directory was the **wrong model** and would have handed two of the three `qcfirmware7280` variants the wrong `qcfirmware7280.cat`, breaking signature validation on the one block the P3 gate is actually about; that 112 of 112 CABs hold an INF with 67 `.sys` and 112 `.cat` beside them and **46** carry no `.sys`, correcting the `112 − 67` figure briefly recorded here; and that against the Kodiak set 32 of gauguin's QCOM ids bind, with exactly two that do not — `QCOM0A8B` (URS0), which the set names on the URS bus in the host/device filter pair, and `QCOM24A5` (UFS0), which the **inbox** `storufs.inf` claims at line 82. **does not decide**: whether the stick boots on the phone, since the medium being complete is not the gate being met and the gate needs the phone, the stick and a reboot to the bootloader; whether the 112 injected INFs bind anything, since `drvload` is a runtime path and what the devices present to Windows is decided by this project's ASL and not by the medium — if `DISKPART` does not list the UFS on the phone, the finding is about the ASL; whether Setup can complete from the WinRE image, or whether a second image named `Windows Setup` has to be built from the UUP's WinPE-Setup packages first; whether the installed Smartisan ROM's touch chip is FocalTech or Novatek, both nodes being `status = ok` in the live tree; whether a FocalTech Windows driver exists anywhere; how many of the 515 objects in the DSDT a complete driver set would still leave unnamed, that being 4.238's census question and not a medium question; and whether P4 can begin, which stays behind steps 2 and 4 and the user's hand. **Not an action**: `sha256sum` (four runs, two from the wrong directory), `wimlib-imagex` (`info`, `dir`, `extract`, `update`, `split`), `cabextract` (112 cabinets), `iconv`/`/usr/bin/grep`/`cmp`/`stat`/`find`, `bash`, `python3` (`tools/acpi-hid-census.py --drivers ~/work/woa-ref/inf-7280 --bind --asl tools/acpi/gauguin.asl`, five runs, plus an inline UTF-16 scan of the merged BCD). All read-only against the device and its backups. ## Step 4.241 — the hardware-coverage number was measuring with a reader that stops at `&`, so `--bind`'s own answer was wrong by six ids and one of them is a plain hardware bind: `tools/acpi-hid-census.py` reads the long spelling now, the gated-id report it was missing is added, and the correction moved this work's two OS-image figures in the *opposite* direction, because `INT33BA` and `VEN_INT&DEV_33BA` were the same id all along

**The census has claimed "155 distinct `ACPI\` ids" for the Kodiak set since it was written, and 155 was not a count of anything.** `INF_ACPI = re.compile(r"ACPI\\\s*([A-Za-z0-9_]{3,16})")` matches from `ACPI\` up to the first non-word character, and a vendor id has a second spelling, `ACPI\VEN_QCOM&DEV_0A36`, where the `&` is that first non-word character. Read with `INF_ACPI` alone, every long-form line in the set yields the token `VEN_QCOM` — a token that is not an id — so six ids disappeared into one pseudo-name. The corrected reading is **160**. This is the same species of defect as the four already recorded in this file — a search in the wrong container (4.233), a `dd` with the wrong sector size (4.238), a manifest read from the wrong directory (4.240) — and it is the first one where the instrument's *output* was a plausible number rather than an obvious failure.

- **The six ids only the long spelling names are `QCOM0693`, `QCOM0694`, `QCOM0A36`, `QCOM0A6B`, `QCOM0AC3` and `QCOM0AD5`**, and the old reading filed each of them as `VEN_QCOM`. The `[Strings]`-key guard the tool already had — the one that keeps a `%ACPI\Foo.DeviceDesc%` key name from counting as a claim — turned out to be claiming a freedom it did not have, because two of those six really are reached only through a key's contents.
- **One of the six is a plain hardware bind and this is what makes the defect a finding rather than a curiosity.** `qcdx7280.inf` writes `%QC_Device% = QCDX_Inst_Base, ACPI\VEN_QCOM&DEV_0A36` — a models line, no `&SUBSYS_`, no `_REV_` — so `QCOM0A36` is bound by the set exactly as `QCOM0A36` would be, and a reader that stopped at the `&` could not see it. A driver that binds an id nothing reports cannot be found by reading the report, which is the failure 4.232 established for `_HID`s: the node is simply absent from Device Manager with nothing to say why.

**The fix is a second reading of the same text, and a report the tool did not have.** `INF_ACPI_LONG` captures `ACPI\VEN_<vendor>&DEV_<device>` plus any trailing `&`-qualifiers, `INF_SUBSYS` lifts the `&SUBSYS_<token>` out of them, and `canon_claims(text)` returns `[(id, subsystem-or-None)]` for every `ACPI\` id in a line, folding the long spelling onto the same canonical id as the short one and dropping the `VEN_*` tokens. `inf_claim_shapes` now returns a dict of six sets instead of a four-tuple — the four positions plus `subsys` (`{id: {SUBSYS token}}` for hardware claims that carry one) and `plain` (the ids with a hardware claim and *no* qualifier) — and `load_driver_set` unions both into `notes`. A new block in `--bind` prints the `_SUB` verdict, and a new `--sub TOKEN` argument overrides the board's subsystem id read from the ASL.

- **The first version of that report was wrong, in the direction it exists to prevent, and the fix is the `plain` set.** It listed `QCOM06E0`, `QCOM0A17` and `QCOM0AD3` as "claimed only behind `&SUBSYS_`" because it saw a qualifier and never asked whether a plain line also existed. All three have one — `QCOM0A17` at `qcpep.wd7280.inf:33` beside twelve qualified lines, `QCOM0AD3` at `qcpmic7280.inf:44` beside two, `QCOM06E0` plain in two files beside thirty-nine qualified. Gating is `subsys − plain`, not `subsys`, and the measured answer is **5 of the set's 25 subsystem-qualified ids have no unqualified models line**: `QCOM0693`/`QCOM0694` (`CRD07280`), `QCOM0A6B` (six tokens), `QCOM0AC3`/`QCOM0AD5` (`CRD07280`, `IDP07280`, `IDPS7280`).
- **None of the five is in `gauguin.asl`, so the gate is a constraint on future nodes and not on the file.** The ASL's board subsystem id is `Name (PSUB, "MTP07225")` at `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl:158`; the set's tokens are `CRD07280`/`MTP07280`/`QRD07280`/`IDP07280`/`CLS07280`/`CDP07280` and `IDPS7280`. Nothing matches, which is consistent with the whole reference tree carrying no `MTP07225`, `07225`, `XIAOMI`, `GAUGUIN`, `07250` or `SM7225` anywhere.

**The correction moved the two OS-image figures in the opposite direction, and the reason is worth keeping.** Re-measuring `~/work/woa-ref/infs-arm64` and `infs-install` with the same reader, those counts went *down* — boot.wim index 1 from 85 ids to 74, install.wim index 1 from 116 to 111 — because a long-form claim now lands on its canonical id rather than on the vendor token. The concrete case is `sdbus.inf`: `ACPI\VEN_INT&DEV_33BA&REV_0001` and the key `ACPI\INT33BA.DeviceDesc` are the same id, and the old reader saw `VEN_INT` against `INT33BA` and called the key misfiled. So a sentence this file carried for weeks — that `INT33BA` was a second instance of a `[Strings]` key named after a different id a models line does not bind — was an artifact of the reader and is now removed; the surviving instance of that shape is `ARMH_PL180` against `ARMH0180`, which is real. The Kodiak set's own 155 became 160 and its keyonly bucket is 0; the two OS images' keyonly bucket went from 5 to 4 for the same reason.

**decides**: that `tools/acpi-hid-census.py`'s `--bind` answer was read through a regex that stops at `&`, that the Kodiak set claims **160** distinct `ACPI\` hardware ids rather than 155, that the six ids only the long spelling carries are `QCOM0693`, `QCOM0694`, `QCOM0A36`, `QCOM0A6B`, `QCOM0AC3` and `QCOM0AD5`, and that `QCOM0A36` is a plain models-line bind in `qcdx7280.inf` — so a reader could not have found it; that **5 of the set's 25 subsystem-qualified ids** have no unqualified models line and are reachable only behind a matching `_SUB` — `QCOM0693`/`QCOM0694`/`QCOM0A6B`/`QCOM0AC3`/`QCOM0AD5` — and that none of the five is in `gauguin.asl`, whose `_SUB` is `MTP07225` against the set's `07280`-class tokens; that the same reader correction moved boot.wim's id count 85 → 74 and install.wim's 116 → 111, and that the `INT33BA`-as-misfiled-key claim this file carried was an artifact of the old reader because `ACPI\VEN_INT&DEV_33BA` and `ACPI\INT33BA` are one id; and that the four-position table and every figure quoted from it in this tool's docstrings have been re-measured rather than left standing. **does not decide**: whether an `MTP07225`-class `_SUB` actually blocks those five ids in practice, since nothing on this board's ACPI namespace writes them and the gate is a statement about nodes this ASL does not have yet; whether the fitted touch chip is FocalTech or Novatek; whether the x64 `boot.wim` DriverStore's id count, quoted at 80 from the old reader, is 80 — that extraction is not on this host and has not been re-read, and the one claim cited from it (`QCOM24A5` in `storufs.inf`) is a short spelling and is unaffected; and whether any other tool in this tree reads ids with a regex that stops at `&`, which is the same question the `[Strings]`-key guard turned out to answer wrongly and is worth asking of `tools/acpi-hid-census.py`'s own `INF_BUS` net, where the fold is documented and harmless. **Not an action**: `python3` (`tools/acpi-hid-census.py` in `--bind --asl`, `--drivers`, `--blocks`, `--functions` modes, several runs, plus one inline script that imports the module and tallies `inf_claim_shapes`'s sets per corpus), `py_compile`, `/usr/bin/grep`, `wc`. All read-only against every corpus; the device, its backups and the medium were not touched.
