## Step 4.242 — the touch panel question is closed by a kernel command line and not by the tree: **Novatek NT36672C**, `0x46`/`0x36`, chosen by OTP bytes, and the `focaltech@38` node is live in every overlay because one merged base DTS carries it while the overlay only *adds* the Novatek node — and the WLAN/BT block the census calls unreachable turns out to be one `_SUB` string, not five devices

**This step began as a documentation check and found a wrong conclusion of this project's own, in a file that records it as fact.** `docs/05-hardware-map.md`'s touch section ends by leaving the chip open: "the live tree has `ts_novatek/status = ok` **as well as** `focaltech@38`, while `qcom,i2c-touch-active` names focaltech, so which chip is actually fitted is not settled by the tree." That sentence is right about the tree and wrong about the question: the tree cannot settle it, and something else does.

**Both vendor nodes are live in every overlay, because the FocalTech node is in the base and the overlays only add.** The nineteen overlays were extracted from `~/backup/gauguin/images/part-dtbo.img` (Android DTBO header `0xd7b7ab1e`, 19 entries of 32 bytes at offset 32) and decompiled. **Every one of the nineteen declares `focaltech@38` at `0x38` with `focaltech,irq-gpio` 0x16 and `focaltech,reset-gpio` 0x15, and every one sets `qcom,i2c-touch-active = "focaltech,fts_ts"`** — including entry 13. Only entry 13 declares `ts_novatek`, `touch_spi@0` and `xiaomi_touch`. So `qcom,i2c-touch-active` is not evidence about this board: it is the same string in all nineteen overlays, which is a statement about the shared base rather than about a SKU. The overlay is a *delta*; it can add a node but it does not remove one that the base carries.

**What settles it is the panel OTP, and the two numbers are identical at both ends.** `/proc/device-tree/chosen/bootargs` carries

```
msm_drm.panel_otp=0x46,0x36,0x32,0x01,0x4a,0x14,0x31,0x00,WpAndMaxlum:0x89,0x84,0x6e
```

and overlay 13's `novatek,cfg_0` — the Novatek driver's own per-supplier configuration array, `novatek,config-array-size = 2` — reads

```
novatek,cfg_0 { novatek,tp-vendor = <0x46>; novatek,display-maker = <0x36>;
                novatek,fw-name = "novatek_nt36672c_j17_fw01.bin";
                novatek,mp-name = "novatek_nt36672c_j17_mp01.bin";
                novatek,clicknum-file-name = "nvt+tianma"; }
novatek,cfg_1 { novatek,tp-vendor = <0x53>; novatek,display-maker = <0x42>; … "nvt+csot" }
```

`0x46` and `0x36` are the first two bytes of the OTP, in order, and they select `cfg_0` and not `cfg_1`. The part is **Novatek NT36672C**, the display is Tianma, and the J17 in both firmware filenames is the gauge board's own panel codename, which `docs/05` records independently as `Panel_J17_36_02_0a_lcd_dsc_vid.xml`.

**The identification is corroborated from four independent directions, and the one that was expected to be the closest is the weakest.** (1) The OTP match above, which is a runtime measurement rather than a declaration. (2) The mode name: overlay 13's `cfg_0`/`cfg_1` and `docs/05`'s panel node all carry `j17_36_02_0a`, and `androidboot.product.hardware.sku=pro` matches that node's `pro` variant. (3) The DTBO selection is unambiguous and mechanical — `androidboot.dtbo_idx=13` from ABL, and entry 13's `qcom,board-id = <0x23 0x00>` is the only one of the nineteen that equals the live tree's `/qcom,board-id` (0x23); entry 0's is `0x1000b`. (4) The part configuration is a full one: two named firmware images, an 18×36 channel map, and a criteria node, i.e. the node the vendor driver actually consumes. The `.dts` that ships inside the payload (`work/uefi/Mu-Silicium/Resources/DTBs/gauguin.dts`) is a **soc-level** base tree — 5474 lines, and `grep` finds no `focaltech`, `novatek`, `ts_novatek` or `touch_spi` in it at all — so it carries neither vendor's node and is not evidence about the fitted part either way. That is worth recording because 4.240's driver census was built on `inf-7280` while an earlier search of this file returned "0 hits" and was read as absence.

**The consequence for P5 is exact and does not depend on that corroboration.** Touch is **Novatek NT36672C on SE0 (SPI 0x880000) with the IRQ on TLMM 22 and the reset on TLMM 21**, speaking Novatek's protocol over SPI. It is not FocalTech over I2C at 0x38, and it is not HID-over-I2C. Windows has no such driver: `hidi2c.inf` binds `ACPI\PNP0C50`, a HID-over-I2C controller, and neither `novatek`, `focaltech`, `nt36672` nor `MSFT8000` occurs anywhere in the WinPE image's 446,983,676 bytes (`grep -a` — `grep -i` prints nothing at all for a binary file, which is how one of the two hits this step first saw was a false positive: the alternation `nt36672\|nt36\|novatek\|focaltech` matched the literal bytes `hNt36` inside a compressed section). So touch is a driver this port would have to write, or a chip left undriven; it is not a binding problem and no `_HID` choice changes it. `docs/05`'s open sentence is now closed in place.

**The second finding is about the census's own reporting, and it is a correction to the framing of the last two steps.** After 4.241's fix, `--bind` reported that 5 of the Kodiak set's 25 subsystem-qualified ids are reachable only behind a matching `_SUB`, and neither 4.240 nor 4.241 says the thing that decides what that costs. The intersection over those five sets is **`CRD07280`**, and it is in all five: `QCOM0693`, `QCOM0694` (`CRD07280`), `QCOM0A6B` (six tokens, all containing it), `QCOM0AC3` and `QCOM0AD5` (`CRD07280`, `IDP07280`, `IDPS7280`). So a board whose `_SUB` is `CRD07280` opens the *entire* gated set at once. That is a one-string answer where the five-row table reads like five.

- **`QCOM0AE2` is not one of them and is not gated at all.** `qcsubsys7280.inf:52` binds `%WPSS.DeviceDesc%=SUBSYS_Device, ACPI\QCOM0AE2` with no qualifier — a plain hardware claim, and the census's own gated list does not contain it. `qcsubsys_ext_wpss7280` and `qcwlan_ext_wpss7280` add `CRD07280`/`IDPS7280`/`IDP07280` variants, but the plain claim is there, so `QCOM0AE2` binds on this board as written. This matters because `QCOM0AE2` is the WPSS device the WLAN trouble in 4.240 was traced to, and 4.240's unclaimed count of 2 is correct while the framing of WLAN as unreachable-by-ASL is too strong.
- **WPSS and its `QWLN` child have a reference node after all, in `lisa`.** `work/uefi/Mu-Silicium/Silicium-ACPI/Platforms/Xiaomi/lisa/Decompiled/DSDT.dsl:15139` is `Device (WPSS)` with `_HID "QCOM0AE2"`, `_DEP` of eight `\_SB` nodes including PEP0, GLNK, IPC0 and TFTP, an interrupt at GSI 0x26B, and a `Device (QWLN)` child — that child being the WLAN node, with `_ADR` Zero, `_DEP` of PEP0/MMU0/IPC0, `_PRW`, `_S0W`/`_S4W`, a `_PRR` pointing at `WPSS.QWLN.WRST`, and a `_CRS` of `0x17A10040+0x10`, `0x80C00000+0xC00000` and 21 GIC interrupts at 0x320–0x334. Gauguin's own DT carries `soc/qcom,icnss@18800000` with `reg 0x18800000+0x800000`, a second window `0xB0000000+0x10000`, twelve interrupts at GSI 0x19E–0x1A9, an iommu and five supply rails, plus `soc/bt_wcn3990`. **Those are the values to rewrite rather than the node to invent** — lisa's structure transfers and gauguin's addressing replaces lisa's — which is the same shape 4.238 established for the `_CRS` windows generally. Whether `qcwlan7280.inf`'s `WPSS\VEN_QCOM&DEV_0A28` ever comes up is a question about the WLAN driver's own expectation of the `QWLN` child's device path, and this step does not settle it.
- **`MTP07225` is this project's own invention, not a recovered board token.** `PSUB` is compared in exactly one place, the `_SUB` method at `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl:1834`, which returns `"MTP07225"` when `\_SB.PSUB == "MTP07225"` — a branch that returns the string it matched. Twenty-five nodes then `Alias (^PSUB, _SUB)`. A search of the whole reference tree for `MTP07225` returns **three hits, all of them this project's own generated files** (`tools/acpi/gauguin.asl` and its two build copies under `work/uefi/…/Silicium-ACPI/Platforms/Xiaomi/gauguin/`), and `SM7225`'s twelve hits are the same three files plus the ACPI table header. Nothing in the Kodiak driver package, the Kodiak platform repository, the Rennell repository or the 66-table ACPI corpus carries either token.

**decides**: that the fitted touch panel is a **Novatek NT36672C** on SE0 at `spi@880000`, IRQ TLMM 22, reset TLMM 21, speaking Novatek's protocol over SPI — settled by `msm_drm.panel_otp=0x46,0x36,…` matching overlay 13's `novatek,cfg_0` `tp-vendor = 0x46` / `display-maker = 0x36`, with the other supplier `cfg_1` being `0x53`/`0x42`; that the `focaltech@38` node and `qcom,i2c-touch-active = "focaltech,fts_ts"` are live in **all nineteen** overlays because they are in the shared base rather than in the selected overlay, so neither is evidence about this board, and entry 13 is uniquely selected by `qcom,board-id = <0x23 0x00>` matching the live tree (`androidboot.dtbo_idx=13`); that no touch driver exists in this tree for either chip — `hidi2c.inf` binds `ACPI\PNP0C50`, HID-over-I2C, and no `novatek`/`focaltech`/`nt36672`/`MSFT8000` string is in the WinPE image — so P5's touch is a driver to be written and not a binding to be chosen; that **`CRD07280` is in all five** of the set's subsystem-gated ids, and that `_SUB` is a single string compared in exactly one place in this ASL, so the gated set is opened or closed as one; that `QCOM0AE2` is a plain, ungated claim in `qcsubsys7280.inf:52` and the WPSS/`QWLN` structure exists in `lisa` with `_HID QCOM0AE2` to be re-addressed from gauguin's `qcom,icnss@18800000`; and that `MTP07225` and `SM7225` occur nowhere in the reference corpora and only in this project's own files, so `PSUB` is a value this port chose. **does not decide**: whether the Novatek node's own declaration is *sufficient* now that the OTP evidence is stronger than it — the OTP is read by the display driver and the DT stores which of two suppliers the display belongs to, so a unit whose panel is Tianma could still be fitted with a FocalTech touch part, and this step has not measured one; ## Step 4.243 — the picture of what is left, measured from the device tree's own `ok` blocks against the ASL's windows: **39 devices against 58 live `ok` SoC blocks, 13 register windows against 12 blocks that need one, and the reason the gap is not gap-shaped — every remaining block is first its *module*, which is another ACPI node not yet written

**Everything before this step measured a corner of the work. This measures its shape**, because "硬件覆盖仍是写作工作" is a statement that stays true however many steps are taken and therefore never tells the next step whether it moved anything. The two sides are both on disk and both cheap to read: the live tree's `/proc/device-tree` dump at `~/backup/gauguin/dt/` records which blocks this board has (`status = ok`), and `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl` records which ones Windows will be told about.

**The count, measured:** 58 nodes under `soc/` are `status = ok` and carry a `reg` base. `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl` holds **39 `Device` blocks** and **13 `Memory32Fixed` windows**, whose owning devices are `QGP0`, `UAR2`, `QGP1`, `I2C8`, `I2C9`, `IC11`, `UFS0`, `BAM1`, `MMU1`, `URS0`, `SPMI`, `GIO0` and `MMU0`. Twelve of those blocks are covered as *devices* rather than as addresses: SE0's `spi@880000` and SEQ's `spi@98c000` are deliberately withheld (4.57), SE3/SE5/SE7's amplifiers, NFC controller and charger cluster are buses-written-but-slaves-unwritten (the file says so at `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl:2887`), and `pinctrl@f100000` and `spmi@c440000` are the two whose windows *are* written — `GIO0` at `0x0F100000` and `SPMI` at `0x0C400000`.

**What is genuinely missing is divisible into four kinds, and the division is what makes it writable.** Confirmed against the driver set with `tools/acpi-hid-census.py --drivers ~/work/woa-ref/inf-7280 --bind`:

- **Writable now, driver present, node absent** — the SSD block: `sdhci@7c4000` (`QCOM0A6F`) and `sdhci@8804000` (`QCOM0A70`), both claimed as plain hardware ids by the set's `qcsdcc7280.inf`/`qcsdcc0x7280.inf`. These are the closest to mechanical of anything left: a `_CRS` of one window and one GSI, a `_HID` from the set, and no parent to build first. **(Retracted by 4.244: there is no `qcsdcc7280.inf` in the set and no INF in it mentions SD at all; `QCOM0A6F` is claimed by nothing and `QCOM0A70` is `DPLB`, the DisplayPort bridge. The block is still writable now, with `QCOM24BF` and `QCOM2466` read off `renoir` at byte-identical base addresses and claimed by the inbox `sdbus.inf`.)**
- **Writable now, but the node is a *child* of a module that has to exist first** — this is the structural finding and it is why the gap is not gap-shaped:
  - **Audio** — the set binds `AUCD\QCOM0A29` (`qcaudminiport_Base7280.inf`) and `ADSP\QCOM0A0F` on `SLM1\CHLD` (`qcslimbus7280.inf`), and gauguin's own tree carries `soc/slim@3ac0000` as a live `ok` block. So the SLIMbus controller, the ADSP child and the audio device are three levels, of which the ASL has none. Bare audios appear as `ADSP\` children and not as ACPI devices, exactly as WLAN does under WPSS.
  - **Camera** — `qccamisp7280.inf` binds `ACPI\QCOM0A25`, `qccammipicsi7280.inf` `ACPI\QCOM0A98`, `qccamjpege7280.inf` `ACPI\QCOM0A33`, `qcccidbridge7280.inf` `ACPI\QCOM0AA2` — and those are the *top-level* CAMSS/ISP/MIPI-CSI/JPEG nodes the devices under `qcom,cam-cpas@ac40000` hang from, none of which is written.
  - **WLAN/BT** — 4.242 already established `QCOM0AE2` is a plain claim and `lisa` has the `WPSS`/`QWLN` structure to re-address from `soc/qcom,icnss@18800000`. The ASL declares `\_SB.WPSS` as an `External` and reads its `_STA` in the PEP0 `_DSM` (`tools/acpi/gauguin.asl:153`, `:2011`), i.e. the file is already written as though the node will exist.
  - **Display** — `qcdx7280.inf`'s plain `ACPI\QCOM0A36` (the id 4.241 recovered from the long spelling) is one of the nodes a display path needs, and this ASL has no display block at all.
- **Not writable at all, and correctly absent** — the 20 `qcom,gdsc@*` power-collapse nodes, `qcom,gpi-dma@800000`/`@900000` (the QUP serial engines' DMA, reached through the SEs and not an ACPI device of its own), `qcom,msm-eud@88e0000`, and `qcom,a5@ac00000` with the MSA/SMMU child tree under it. No `_HID` in the set binds a GDSC and one should not be invented: these are reached through PEP0's `_DSM` and the parent module's power sequences, which is a further argument for doing the modules first.
- **Not representable, measured rather than assumed** — `spi@880000` and the two `thermal-sensor@*` blocks. The set's QUP pool is `QCOM0A10` (I2C), `QCOM0A16` (UART), `QCOM0A88` (GPI) and no SPI id at all: `--bind` prints "SE0 nothing in this set claims index `0E`". And a scan of all 151 `.dsl` tables under `Silicium-ACPI` finds **zero** reference windows enclosing `0x0C263000`, `0x0C265000` or `0x00880000` — so TSENS has neither a name nor a window anywhere in the corpus, and the SPI engine has no name. That is why 4.57 could not write them, restated as a measurement over the whole corpus rather than over one file.

**The prioritisation that follows, and why it is not the obvious one.** The obvious order is address order or block order. The order the measurement supports is: **SDCC first** (two self-contained nodes, a driver, a low-risk first exercise of the whole add-a-node loop), **then WPSS** (a plain claim, a reference structure in `lisa`, and an `External` already waiting for it), **then the audio module chain**, **then CAMSS**. Every one of those is *reachable from this host* and none needs the phone — so the hardware-coverage half of the goal can keep advancing while the P3 gate waits on a stick and a reboot. **Not on this list, and the reason is not priority:** touch. 4.242 settled that no Windows driver exists for the Novatek NT36672C, so no `_HID` choice reaches it, and writing the node would register a device that nothing binds — the exact silent failure this file's header warns against.

**decides**: that this board has **58 live `ok` SoC blocks with a register base** and the ASL describes **39 devices across 13 windows**, of which 12 blocks are covered as devices and the two withheld engines and the three unwritten slave clusters account for the rest; that the remaining work divides into four kinds — writable-now (`sdhci@7c4000`, `sdhci@8804000`, both with a driver in the set), writable-but-child-first (the SLIMbus/ADSP audio chain, the CAMSS/ISP/CSI/JPEG top nodes, WPSS/`QWLN`, display), not writable by design (the GDSC cluster, the GPI DMAs, EUD), and not representable (the SPI engine, whose TYP index `0E` **no id in the set claims**, and TSENS, for which no window exists in any of the 151 corpus tables); that the `Kodiak` platform's own ACPI is a **CPU-only 354-byte `DSDT_Minimal` named `SM7325`** which carries no peripheral block at all, so the SC7280/Kodiak board's own tables contribute no device names and this port's names can only come from the driver package; and that the next node should be an SDCC, because it is the shortest path from "measure" to "hardware coverage moved". **does not decide**: whether the SLIMbus/ADSP audio chain is reachable at all on this board, the DSPs being firmware rather than ACPI nodes and `mss@4080000`/`lpass@3000000`/turing/npu/venus carrying no `status` (4.238), so the audio path may be blocked exactly where 4.57 said the others were; whether `QCOM0A25`/`QCOM0A98`/`QCOM0A33`/`QCOM0AA2` bind with the windows and GSIs the device tree gives rather than the ones the set's own board gives; the exact `_HID` for `sdhci@8804000` where the set carries two SDCC ids and only the board says which is which; and whether any of this reaches a driver *at runtime*, which only the P3 gate can answer. **Not an action**: `python3` (three inline scripts: the `ok`-block/`Memory32Fixed` comparison, the ASL window-to-device map, the corpus-wide window scan; plus `tools/acpi-hid-census.py` in default, `--blocks` and `--bind` modes), `iasl -d` on a **copy** of `Silicon/Qualcomm/Kodiak/DSDT_Minimal.aml` written to `/tmp/kodiak/` — the tree's own files were not touched — `/usr/bin/grep`, `find`, `wc`. All read-only against the device's backups; no device was contacted. Files written: this entry. **No device command was issued**, no partition, seed, `boot` or storage was written, no `fastboot fetch`, no QEMU process started or signalled, and none of `work/out/{p2-variants,p3-display,usb-host,p2-what}`, `work/win11/qemu-stick*`, `work/out/p3-stick/` or `work/out/.p3-stick-drivers/` was touched. `device/dxe/UsbConfigDxe.efi` is still `sha256 6943cc615f7d4ba502c87bcf14a76e6e1398975a4101ed2711ba9e1c6e2566f5`. The orphaned dry-run processes 468162 and 471324 were left alive, `bq6ik1shs` was not restarted and `br7srnvmx` was not started. **Working state**: unchanged from 4.242 — `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl` at 39 devices and 13 windows, `work/out/p3-stick` built and verified and written to nothing, no build run. **device state**: unchanged — no `adb` or `fastboot` device, both tty globs absent, `ssphy@88e8000` disabled so the board presents USB 2.0, and `lsblk` shows no removable medium. ## Step 4.243 (addendum) — the Kodiak table set is measured rather than assumed to be empty

4.243's last clause said the `Kodiak` platform's own ACPI carries no peripheral block *because the DSDT is CPU-only*. That is one table. Read across all ten:

| Table | Bytes | Device-name content |
|---|---|---|
| `DSDT_Minimal.aml` | 354 | 8 × `Name (_HID, "ACPI0007")` — the CPUs, nothing else |
| `CSRT.aml` | 69,258 | 2 resource groups, both placeholder |
| `IORT.aml` | 4,954 | 5 `QCOM`-token hits, all of them the OEM ID |
| `DBG2`, `APIC`, `PPTT`, `FACP`, `GTDT`, `MCFG`, `SPCR` | 80–816 | OEM ID only |

Measured by searching each `.aml` with `/usr/bin/grep -a` for `QCOM`, `_HID` and `_CID`: **only `DSDT_Minimal` contains any `_HID`, and all eight are `ACPI0007`.** Plain `grep` would have printed nothing at all for every one of these files, which is the trap the host-grep memory records — the counts above come from the `-a` form.

The CSRT is the only table that could have carried device names, and it is a template. Decompiling it gives two resource groups, `[030h] Device ID 100B` and `[068h] Device ID 100C`, both `Vendor ID 4D4F4351` — that DWORD's bytes are `51 43 4F 4D`, ASCII `QCOM`, so the vendor field is the string rather than a number. Group 1's `MMIO Base Address Low`/`High` read `00000002`/`00000001` and its `UID` is `00000001`. Group 2's read `00010004`/`DEADF00D` and its `UID` is `DEADF00D`, the poison value, i.e. unwritten. Its `ResourceInfo` buffer at `[090h]` begins

```
51 43 4F 4D 45 44 4B 32 25 73 00 00 51 43 4F 4D   QCOMEDK2%s..QCOM
```

which is the generator's own OEM Table ID (`Oem Table ID : "QCOMEDK2"` at `[010h]`) followed by a literal `%s` — a **format placeholder that was never substituted**. A table whose `UID` is `DEADF00D` and whose payload still holds an unexpanded `printf` directive has not been filled in for this board, and no reading of it yields a block this port can name.

**decides**: that 4.243's last clause survives being widened from one table to ten — the `Kodiak` platform's ACPI set contributes **no device name at all**, the eight `ACPI0007` CPUs in `DSDT_Minimal` being the whole of it and the CSRT being an unfilled `QCOMEDK2` template rather than a resource description, so "names can only come from the driver package" is a measurement over the set and not an inference from its smallest member; and it retires the CSRT as an open question, which 4.243 had left standing. **does not decide**: whether `100B`/`100C` were ever meant to name anything on a real board, since nothing in the set or the driver package consumes the CSRT either way. **Not an action**: `/usr/bin/grep -a` over ten files, `iasl -d` on the already-existing `Decompiled/CSRT.dsl`, `stat`, `sed -n`. Read-only against the tree; no device was contacted and nothing was written but this entry. Device state and every standing constraint are as recorded in 4.243.

## Step 4.244 — the SDCC pair, and a correction to 4.243's own reading of them

4.243 said the two SDCC nodes were "writable now, driver present, node absent", and named the driver as "the set's `qcsdcc7280.inf`/`qcsdcc0x7280.inf`". **No such file exists.** The Kodiak set is 112 `.inf` files and not one of them mentions SD in any encoding: searched for `sdcc`, `sdhci` and `secure digital`, all 112 return nothing. The two ids 4.243 gave are wrong in the same way — `QCOM0A6F` is **claimed by no INF in any corpus on this host**, and `QCOM0A70` is not an SDCC id at all. It is `DPLB`, the DisplayPort bridge: `qcdplbridge7280.inf:36` reads

```
%DPLBRG.DeviceDesc%=DPLBRG_Device, ACPI\QCOM0A70
```

and both reference DSDTs that carry it name the device `DPLB` (`lisa/Decompiled/DSDT.dsl:22924`, `a52sxq/Decompiled/DSDT.dsl:17833`). So 4.243 had applied the header's own family-byte reasoning to the storage class, where it does not hold — `QCOM2465` on 8974, `QCOM24BF` on 8994 and `QCOM24A5` for UFS on this SoC are all in one `24xx` class that appears not to move with the SoC family the way the PMIC's `xx2D` and TLMM's `xx0C` do.

**What the two blocks are, measured from this device's tree.** `sdhci@7c4000` calls itself `sdhc1` in `qcom,msm-bus,name`, carries `qcom,nonremovable`, runs 8-bit at `HS400_1p8v`/`HS200_1p8v`/`DDR_1p8v`, and has three windows — `hc_mem` `0x7C4000`, `cqhci_mem` `0x7C5000`, `cqhci_ice` `0x7C8000` — the last an inline crypto engine. `sdhci@8804000` calls itself `sdhc2`, carries `cd-gpios = <193 94 0>`, runs 4-bit at `SDR12`…`SDR104`, and has one window, `hc_mem` `0x8804000`. Non-removable + 8-bit + HS400 + CQHCI-with-ICE is the internal eMMC shape; card detect + SDR104 is the removable slot. Phandle 193 resolves to `soc/pinctrl@f100000`, so the card-detect pin is TLMM 94.

The unit's own storage is neither of them: `chosen/bootargs` reads `androidboot.bootdevice=1d84000.ufshc` and `androidboot.boot_devices=soc/1d84000.ufshc`.

**The ids, and why the check was run against a different set than usual.** `renoir` — the corpus's only other Xiaomi board of this generation, and the table this file's own `UFS0` was already patterned on — declares its SDCC pair as

- `Device (SDC1)` `_HID "QCOM24BF"`, `Memory32Fixed 0x007C4000, 0x1000`, `_UID Zero`, with a `Device (EMMC)` child and `_RMV` returning `Zero`;
- `Device (SDC2)` `_HID "QCOM2466"`, `Memory32Fixed 0x08804000, 0x1000`, `_UID One`, with a card-detect `GpioInt` on `\_SB.GIO0` pin `0xC0`.

**Both base addresses are byte-identical to gauguin's** (`0x7C4000`, `0x8804000`), and the split matches `qcom,nonremovable`/`cd-gpios` one for one, so the pairing is read off a same-family table at the same addresses rather than derived. Neither id is in the Kodiak set; both are claimed by `sdbus.inf` **in the install image's own driver store**, at

```
%ACPI\QCOM2466.DeviceDesc%=SDHostQualcomm8974Std, ACPI\QCOM2466
%ACPI\QCOM24BF.DeviceDesc%=SDHostQualcomm8994Std, ACPI\QCOM24BF
```

with all three of its SDCC ids (`QCOM2465`, `QCOM2466`, `QCOM24BF`) also in its `ExcludeFromSelect` list — which suppresses an id in the Update Driver list but does not stop PnP matching a models line. Measured both ways: `--drivers ~/work/woa-ref/infs-arm64/pro --bind QCOM24BF QCOM2466` reports "claimed by sdbus.inf" for each, and the same command against `inf-7280` reports "NOT CLAIMED" for each. This is not the file's first inbox id — `UFS0` is `QCOM24A5`, which the set also does not claim and `storufs.inf:82` does (4.240).

**Written.** `Device (SDC2)` at `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl:308` and `Device (SDC1)` at `:342`, taking the file from 39 devices to 41. SDC2 is present (`_STA` inherited, i.e. 0x0F) with `_DEP` of PEP0 and GIO0, one `Interrupt` at `0xEC`, and the card-detect `GpioInt` on GIO0 pin `0x5E`. SDC1 is written **inert**, its `_STA` returning `Zero`, because renoir's presence gate is `STOR == 0x02`, a board variable gauguin's tables do not carry, and an eMMC controller reporting present on a UFS unit is the device-that-does-not-start the header warns about; renoir does exactly this to its own SDC2, whose `_STA` returns `Zero` unconditionally. Withheld: renoir's SDC2 also carries a `GpioIo` on GIO0 pin `0x5C` (a card-power pin) — gauguin declares `cd-gpios` and no power pin, so none is invented. Also withheld, on a diagnostic budget rather than a hardware one: renoir's pair carries an empty `_DIS` that iasl answers with `Warning 3141 - Missing dependency (Device has a _DIS, missing a _SRS, required)`, so including it would take this file from 26 warnings to 28 for a method Windows does not need.

**The GSI rule is measured, not assumed.** ACPI GSI = the device tree's SPI number + 32, verified on four nodes already in the file: UFS0 DT 265 → `0x129` = 297; I2C8 DT 354 → `0x182`; I2C9 DT 355 → `0x183`; IC11 DT 357 → `0x185`. So SDC2's `hc_irq` at DT 204 is `0xEC` = 236 and SDC1's at DT 641 is `0x2A1` = 673. Both controllers also declare a `pwr_irq` (DT 222 → 254, DT 644 → 676) which is not declared, for the same reason it is not declared on UFS0 or on renoir's pair.

**decides**: that 4.243's SDCC paragraph is retracted on all three of its facts — there is no `qcsdcc7280.inf` in the set, `QCOM0A6F` is claimed by nothing anywhere on this host, and `QCOM0A70` is `DPLB` the DisplayPort bridge — and that the two SDCC controllers are nevertheless writable now, with `QCOM24BF` for `sdhci@7c4000` and `QCOM2466` for `sdhci@8804000` read off renoir at **byte-identical base addresses**, both claimed by the inbox `sdbus.inf` that is in the install image's driver store; that the ACPI GSI is the device tree's SPI + 32, now measured on four independent nodes; and that the file is at 41 devices across 13 windows, compiling to `0 Errors, 26 Warnings, 97 Remarks` — the warning count deliberately unchanged. **does not decide**: whether an eMMC part is fitted on this unit, which is why SDC1 is inert rather than present; whether `ExcludeFromSelect` leaves the inbox `sdbus.inf` genuinely free to bind at first boot on a device it has never seen, which only the P3 gate can answer; whether the removable slot's card-detect `GpioInt` transfers to Windows through a GIO0 whose `_CRS` here declares the TLMM window and nine interrupts but has never had a GpioInt on it before — this is the first `GpioInt` in the file; and whether renoir's `STOR` variable has any counterpart in gauguin's firmware that a later step could read instead of hardcoding `Zero`. **Not an action**: `python3` (the phandle/`reg`/`interrupts` decode, the `_HID`-by-device scan over the corpus, the SD-in-any-encoding search over the 112 INFs), `tools/acpi-hid-census.py --bind` in six invocations, `/usr/bin/grep -a` (the `.inf` searches needed `-a`; `sdbus.inf` is UTF-16, so a plain grep for its models lines returns nothing and the reading came through `iconv`), `iasl -tc` and `iasl -d`, `cmp`, `stat`. Read-only against the device's backups; no device was contacted. Files written: `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl` and its generated twin `uefi/Silicium-ACPI/Platforms/Xiaomi/gauguin/gauguin.asl`, regenerated with `tools/make_uefi_platform.py --xhci-host` — **the flag matters and the first regeneration omitted it**, producing a tree whose `USE_XHCI_HOST_DRIVER` had gone back to `0` and whose `DXE.inc` had lost the three host-stack INF lines, which is precisely the state `tools/sync-uefi-platform.sh:57-88` exists to catch; the flag restored, the diff against HEAD is the ASL alone, and `cmp` confirms source and generated copy are identical. **No device command was issued**, no partition, seed, `boot` or storage written, no `fastboot fetch`, no QEMU process started or signalled, and none of `work/out/{p2-variants,p3-display,usb-host,p2-what}`, `work/win11/qemu-stick*`, `work/out/p3-stick/` or `work/out/.p3-stick-drivers/` was touched. `device/dxe/UsbConfigDxe.efi` is still `sha256 6943cc615f7d4ba502c87bcf14a76e6e1398975a4101ed2711ba9e1c6e2566f5`. The orphaned dry-run processes 468162 and 471324 were left alive, `bq6ik1shs` was not restarted and `br7srnvmx` was not started. **device state**: unchanged — no `adb` or `fastboot` device, both tty globs absent, `lsblk` shows no removable medium, and the P3 gate has still never been run.

## Step 4.245 — WPSS is written, and it closes a hole PEP0 has been answering through

The `_HID` is a plain claim, not a derived one. `qcsubsys7280.inf:52` reads

```
%WPSS.DeviceDesc%=SUBSYS_Device, ACPI\QCOM0AE2
```

with no `&SUBSYS_` qualifier, and the two extension INFs that also name the id — `qcsubsys_ext_wpss7280.inf` and `qcwlan_ext_wpss7280.inf` — qualify theirs with `CRD07280`, `IDPS7280` and `IDP07280`, which this board's `_SUB` is not. `--bind QCOM0AE2 --drivers ~/work/woa-ref/inf-7280` reports all three files and the plain claim is the one that binds. This is also the id 4.242 recovered from the long spelling.

**What it closes.** `\_SB.WPSS` has been declared `External` at `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl:153` and its `_STA` read at PEP0's `_DSM` revision-7 branch (`:2184-2195`) since the PEP0 block landed. That branch is `If (CondRefOf (\_SB.WPSS)) { If (CondRefOf (\_SB.WPSS._STA)) { Return (..._STA ()) } Else { Return (0x0F) } } Else { Return (Zero) }` — so while no `WPSS` device exists, the reference fails and the `_DSM` answers **Zero for every consumer that asks revision 7 what the wireless subsystem is**. The node now exists and that answer becomes `0x0F`. The hardware behind it is real: `soc/qcom,icnss@18800000` is `status ok` with twelve interrupts, `soc/bt_wcn3990` is present, and `vendor.qcom.bluetooth.soc = cherokee` is in the Android properties (`docs/05`).

**Written as** `Device (WPSS)` at `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl:439`, taking the file from 41 devices to 42. `_HID QCOM0AE2`, `_UID Zero`, `_STA` returning `0x0F`, `_DEP` of PEP0 and PILC — this file's PILC is the PIL proxy already present, and `qcsubsys` is the driver that needs it. One window, `0x18800000 + 0x800000`, from `reg-names = "membase"`; the node's second `reg` entry (`0xB0000000 + 0x10000`, `"smmu_iova_ipa"`) is the SMMU's I/O virtual address pool rather than a window the processor touches, and is not written. Twelve interrupts, device tree SPIs 414–425 in order, all level-high: **414 + 32 = 446 = 0x1BE**, the first GSI below, so the node obeys the number → GIC-SPI rule 4.244 confirmed on the four nodes already in the file.

**QWLN is not written, and why that costs nothing is the finding.** The corpus's WPSS nodes carry a `Device (QWLN)` child — renoir and lisa both, at `Memory32Fixed 0x17A10040` with a 12 MB window at `0x80C00000` and thirty-two GSIs from `0x320`. None of it is measurable on gauguin: `0x17A10040` is not a translation-service page here, it falls inside this board's own GIC frame (`soc/interrupt-controller@17a00000`, `reg` `0x17A00000+0x10000` and `0x17A60000+0x100000`), and gauguin's icnss declares 12 interrupts where lisa's QWLN declares 32. The reason a missing child costs nothing is that **lisa's QWLN has no `_HID` at all** — `_ADR Zero`, `_DEP` of PEP0/MMU0/IPC0, `_PRW`, `_S0W`/`_S4W`, `_PRR` pointing at its own `WRST` power resource, and the `_CRS` above. What binds the wireless device is a driver registry value, not a firmware node: `qcsubsys_ext_wpss7280.inf`'s `[WPSS_Children]` section is

```
HKR,Desktop\0,"DeviceObjectName",%REG_SZ%,"QWLN"
HKR,Desktop\0,"_HID",%REG_SZ%,"QCOM0A28"
```

which is why `qcwlan7280.inf:32` binds `WPSS\VEN_QCOM&DEV_0A28` and why no INF in the set claims an `ACPI\` id for WLAN anywhere. So 4.240's clause that "WLAN is a WPSS child that no amount of ACPI namespace will produce" is confirmed from the other side as well: the child's `_HID` is supplied by the qcsubsys driver, and the firmware's whole obligation is the parent, its window and its interrupts — all three now written. If the P3 gate shows no WLAN device, QWLN is the structure to add and the open question is which of its resources are gauguin's.

**decides**: that the wireless subsystem node is `QCOM0AE2` as a plain claim in `qcsubsys7280.inf:52` with the two `&SUBSYS_`-gated extension INFs not binding this board; that it is written at `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl:439` with the device tree's own window and twelve interrupts, obeying the SPI + 32 rule; that PEP0's revision-7 `_DSM` answer changes from `Zero` to `0x0F` for every caller, which was the file's own `External` waiting since the PEP0 block; and that the WLAN child is a `WPSS\` child the qcsubsys driver creates from its registry, so no ACPI node can or should supply `QCOM0A28`. **does not decide**: what QWLN's real resources are on this board, since the corpus's are impossible here and the device tree does not describe the child at all; whether `_PRR`/`WRST`/`_PRW` are needed for the WLAN child to reach D0 once qcsubsys creates it, which is the P3 gate's question; and whether the twelve-interrupt set is complete, the device tree's own list being the only source and `pwr_irq`-style second interrupts having been withheld on every other node in this file. **Not an action**: `/usr/bin/grep -a` over the 112 INFs, `iconv` (every `.inf` is UTF-16, so a plain grep for these lines prints nothing), a Python pass decoding each INF and listing its `WPSS`/`wlan` lines, a brace-matching Python extractor over `lisa/Decompiled/DSDT.dsl` read twice (the second time to confirm QWLN has no `_HID` after the first reading showed the interrupts but not the device list), `iasl -tc`, `cmp`, `sed`, `stat`. Read-only against the device's backups; no device contacted. Files written: `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl`, its generated twin under `uefi/Silicium-ACPI/Platforms/Xiaomi/gauguin/` (regenerated with `tools/make_uefi_platform.py --xhci-host`, `cmp`-identical to the source), `docs/05-hardware-map.md` and this entry. The file is at 42 devices across 13 windows, compiling to `0 Errors, 26 Warnings, 99 Remarks`. **No device command was issued**, no partition, seed, `boot` or storage written, no `fastboot fetch`, no QEMU process started or signalled, and none of `work/out/{p2-variants,p3-display,usb-host,p2-what}`, `work/win11/qemu-stick*`, `work/out/p3-stick/` or `work/out/.p3-stick-drivers/` was touched. `device/dxe/UsbConfigDxe.efi` is still `sha256 6943cc615f7d4ba502c87bcf14a76e6e1398975a4101ed2711ba9e1c6e2566f5`. ## Step 4.246 — the camera top nodes bind the same-way family as WPSS, and the blocks behind them are gauguin's own

4.243 listed the camera top nodes as "writable but child-first". Reading the id forms rather than only the bind results changes that, and the change is the whole content of this step.

**The ids are in the block-name family, not the board-gated one.** Each camera INF's models line is

```
qccamisp7280.inf:42        %ISP.DeviceDesc%=CameraISP_Device, ACPI\QCOM0A25
qccammipicsi7280.inf:42    %CameraMipiCsi.DeviceDesc%=CameraMipiCsi_Device, ACPI\QCOM0A98
qccamjpege7280.inf:70      %JpegE.DeviceDesc%=CameraJpegE_Device, ACPI\QCOM0A33
qccidbridge7280.inf:32     %CCIDBridge.DeviceDesc%=ccidbridge_Device, ACPI\QCOM0AA2
qccamplatform7280.inf:44   %CameraPlatform.DeviceDesc%=CameraPlatform_Device, ACPI\QCOM0A32
qccamflash7280.inf:38      %Flash.DeviceDesc% = CameraFlash_Device, ACPI\QCOM0A27
```

all plain. What *is* gated is the sensors — `qccamfrontsensor7280.inf:61-62` and `qccamauxsensor7280.inf:63-64` write each id twice, short and long, both plain, but the QRD extension gated. So the top nodes sit in the same class as WPSS (`QCOM0AE2`) and the BCL (`QCOM0A77`): **claimed by a plain models line, outside the set's five gated ids**. That is a different class from `BTH0`'s `QCOM0A6B`, `CSW0`'s `QCOM0AC3` and `WLTM`'s `QCOM0AD5`, which 4.241 measured as unreachable on this board.

**The nodes are siblings, not a parent chain.** lisa's `JPGE` is `_HID QCOM0A33`, `_UID 0x17`, with `_DEP` of CAMP and MMU0 and two interrupts; `CAMP` is `QCOM0A32`, `_UID 0x1B`, `_DEP` of PEP0/PMIC/PML0/ARPC/NSP0; `VFE0` is `QCOM0A25`, `_UID 0x16`, `_DEP` of MMU0/PEP0/CAMP; `MPCS` is `QCOM0A98`, `_UID 0x18`, `_DEP` of CAMP; `FLSH` is `QCOM0A27`, `_UID 0x19`; and `CCID` is `QCOM0AA2` with neither `_UID` nor `_STA` and a `_DEP` of PSUB alone. The dependency is on the platform node, not on each other. lisa's `CAMP` carries **no window and no interrupt** — its three GSIs (0x1EC, 0x12F, 0x1EB) are its children's CSPR/CAMNOC lines, and `0x12F` is this file's BAM1 interrupt. The corpus's top camera nodes are deliberately thin.

**The VFE0 template is measurable on gauguin, and half of it matches.** lisa's `VFE0` carries eleven `Memory32Fixed` windows; seven are camera-shaped and four are not. **The one node that is fully measured is `JPGE`, and it is still not written this step.** lisa's `JPGE` (`QCOM0A33`, `_UID 0x17`, `_DEP` of CAMP and MMU0) carries two windows and two interrupts:

**`CAMP` is where the chain actually starts, and it is where the unverified part is.** lisa's `CAMP` is `_HID QCOM0A32`, `_UID 0x1B`, `_DEP` of PEP0, PMIC, PML0, ARPC and NSP0, with three GSIs (`0x1EC`, `0x12F`, `0x1EB`) and — on lisa — **no window at all**, its top window living inside `VFE0` instead. That `0x1EB` is lisa's third `CAMP` GSI, which is the closest thing to a positive identification available, but the other two have no gauguin counterpart and the window is a composite the corpus's node does not model. So the camera chain's entry point is written next, not now, and the shape of the work is: `CAMP` with gauguin's own windows and the `_DEP` trimmed to what exists, then `JPGE` verbatim, then decide `MPCS` and `VFE0` from the device tree's eight blocks rather than from lisa's eleven windows.

## Step 4.247 — the camera chain gets its entry point, and the engine that transfers byte for byte

`Device (CAMP)` at `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl:556` and `Device (JPGE)` at `:621`, taking the file from 42 devices to 44.

**`CAMP` is lisa's id and dependency shape with gauguin's resources, and that combination is the whole node.** `_HID QCOM0A32` (`qccamplatform7280.inf:44`, a plain models line), `_UID 0x1B` kept from lisa. `_DEP` of PEP0, PMIC and PML0 — three of lisa's five dependencies, and all three exist in this file with the ids lisa gives them (`QCOM0A2B` at `:751`, `QCOM0AD3` at `:940`). lisa's other two, ARPC and NSP0, are left out even though `QCOM0A5C`/`QCOM0A82`/`QCOM0AB0` are all bindable in the set, because the reason `JPGE` waited a step applies to them too: a `_DEP` naming a device that does not exist is a namespace violation. The `_CRS` is the device tree's three windows in `reg-names` order — `cam_cpas_top 0xAC40000+0x1000`, `cam_camnoc 0xAC42000+0x4600`, `core_top_csr_tcsr 0x1FC0000+0x40000` — and one interrupt at DT SPI 459 = `0x1EB`, written Level/ActiveHigh/Shared as lisa writes it. That GSI is the identification: it is the third of lisa's CAMP interrupts (`0x1EC`, `0x12F`, `0x1EB`), and the other two are not written because `0x12F` is **this file's own BAM1 line** — the corpus's platform node reaches other blocks' interrupts on lisa's hardware split, and only `0x1EB` has a counterpart here.

Where the two boards differ is worth stating plainly: on lisa `CAMP` has **no window at all**, and on gauguin it has three. That is not a portability failure, it is the same blocks placed differently — and it is why the node could not be copied and had to be built from this board's own node.

**`JPGE` is the one node in the chain that transfers unchanged.** `_HID QCOM0A33` (`qccamjpege7280.inf:70`, plain), `_UID 0x17`, `_DEP` of CAMP and MMU0, windows `0x0AC4E000+0x4000` and `0x0AC52000+0x4000`, interrupts `0x1FA`/`0x1FB`. gauguin's `qcom,jpegenc@ac4e000` and `qcom,jpegdma@0xac52000` are at those same two addresses with those same two lengths at DT SPI 474 and 475 — which the SPI + 32 rule turns into those same two GSIs. Windows, lengths and interrupts are all identical, so the only judgement in the node is the id. Its interrupts are Edge/ActiveHigh/Exclusive where CAMP's are Level/Shared: the corpus is not uniform and the difference belongs to the block.

## Step 4.249 — lisa's VFE0 is the whole camera cluster, and gauguin's camera region is now mapped

Three things fall out of mapping every node in `0x0AC00000..0x0AD80000`, and the first is a correction to 4.246.

**4.246 mislabelled three of lisa's `VFE0` windows.** It called `0x0AC6B000+0x1000`, `0x0AC6F000+0x8000` and `0x0AC87000+0xA000` "not on this board at all". They are gauguin's `qcom,lrme@ac6b000` (`0xAC6B000+0xA00`), `qcom,bps` (`0xAC6F000+0x8000`, **exact**) and `qcom,ipe0` (`0xAC87000+0xA000`, **exact**) — three live `ok` blocks of the image-processing pipeline, two of them at their exact lengths. Only `0x84300000+0x500000` has no counterpart, and that is the camera SMMU, which gauguin describes as a phandle-only node with no `reg`. So the corrected count of lisa's eleven windows is **eight** matching gauguin bases, not four.

**And that changes what lisa's `VFE0` is.** A node carrying an IFE, the CPAS/CDM, both CCIs, LRME, BPS, IPE, a `csid-lite`, a `csiphy` and the camera SMMU is not the IFE — it is the **whole CAMSS/IFE cluster node**, the same role lisa's `CAMP` plays for the platform, one layer up. gauguin splits what lisa merges: its `qcom,vfe0@acaf000`/`vfe1`/`vfe2`/`vfe-lite` are four separate `ok` blocks at `0xACAF000`, `0xACB6000`, `0xACBD000`, `0xACC4000`, each `+0x4000`, and its three CSIDs and four CSIPHYs are separate too. So the mapping from corpus to board is:

|---|---|
| `VFE0` cluster node `QCOM0A25`, eleven windows | four `vfe@*` blocks — one node, or four re-addressed ones |
| `MPCS` `QCOM0A98`, five 8 KB windows at `0x0ACE0000…0x0ACE8000` | four `csiphy0..3` at `0xAC65000/66000/67000/68000`, `+0x1000` — **different block and different addresses** |
| `CAMP` `QCOM0A32`, no window | `cam-cpas@ac40000`, three windows |
| `JPGE` `QCOM0A33`, two windows | **identical** (`jpegenc@ac4e000`, `jpegdma@0xac52000`) |
| `CCID` `QCOM0AA2`, no window | `csid0..2` and `csid-lite`, four `+0x1000` blocks |
| `FLSH` `QCOM0A27`, `_CRS` of one byte `0x79` | `qcom,camera-flash@0/@5/@6`, no `reg` |
