## Step 4.250 — the camera chain gets its ISP and its CSI brids, and the boundary the step is really about is cluster-versus-engine: **one `VFE0` and not four**, three CSIDs re-addressed from this board's own tree, and the two `-lite` blocks left owed rather than guessed

Step 4.249 ended with a question it could not answer from lisa: `VFE0` there is the whole CAMSS/IFE cluster, gauguin splits it into four `qcom,vfe170_150` blocks, and the corpus writes only one IFE node. This step answers it, writes four nodes, and the answer is a rule rather than a coin-flip.

**The tiebreak is the driver's cardinality, not the device tree's.** `QCOM0A25` is claimed at `qccamisp7280.inf:44` as `%ISP.DeviceDesc%=CameraISP_Device, ACPI\QCOM0A25` — lisa's `VFE0` id — and that cabinet ships **one** `.sys` (`qccamisp7280.sys`, 341,112 B) with **one** firmware blob (`CAMERA_ICP_AAAAAA.elf`, 3,947,640 B). One driver instance. gauguin has four `qcom,vfe170_150` blocks (`vfe0@acaf000` DT SPI 465, `vfe1@acb6000` 467, `vfe2@acbd000` 718, `vfe-lite@acc4000` 472) and one driver that cannot bind four. So this file writes **one** `Device (VFE0)` at gauguin's own first VFE — `0x0ACAF000 + 0x4000`, GSI `0x1F1` (465 + 32) — and not four. The rule stated plainly: where a device tree splits a block finer than a driver can bind, the ASL follows the driver, because the alternative is N claims on a singleton. `Device (MMU0)` singular where lisa has two SMMUs is the same decision already in this file. The counter-example that made this need arguing is `qcdx7280.inf`'s `QCOM0A36`, which multiplies on `&REV_`: a driver *can* be multi-instance, so "one id one node" is not a law, it is a measurement, and here the measurement is a one-blob cabinet.

**The engine boundary is what makes this step's title.** A cluster node aggregates blocks and has no hardware of its own; an engine node *is* a block and has a window and an interrupt. lisa's `VFE0` is a cluster — eleven windows with no single base, and the eleven map onto *different* gauguin drivers (`bps`/`ipe0` are image-processing, `lrme` is a separate `qcom,lrme`, the SMMU is a phandle-only node). `qccammipicsi7280` is the other kind: `CameraMipiCsi_Device`, and the block it drives is a CSID.

**Three CSIDs, re-addressed from this board's own tree, each with its own window and GSI:**

| node | gauguin block | window | DT SPI | GSI |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Device (CSID)` | `qcom,csid0@acb3000` | `0x0ACB3000 + 0x1000` | 464 | `0x1D0` |
| `Device (CSI1)` | `qcom,csid1@acba000` | `0x0ACBA000 + 0x1000` | 466 | `0x1D2` |
| `Device (CSI2)` | `qcom,csid2@acc1000` | `0x0ACC1000 + 0x1000` | 717 | `0x2CD` |

all three carrying `_HID "QCOM0AA2"` — lisa's `CCID` — and that is the necessarily-arbitrary half, written with its reason in the file. lisa's `CCID` is one node with **no `_CRS` at all** and no `_UID`; gauguin has four CSID-capable blocks; four claims, one bus driver. The `_UID`s are `0x21`, `0x22`, `0x23`, and the choice has a reason worth keeping: taking lisa's own `0x15` for the first was the obvious move and is wrong, because `0x15` is lisa's `CAMS`, a different node. These three sit in a range nobody has claimed, above the corpus's highest camera `_UID` (`0x1E`), and say "this is where the extras went" without borrowing another node's identity to say it. **They are not known to be right and the file says so.**

`_STA` is deliberately absent from all three, and that is lisa's own shape for `CCID` rather than an omission — `qcccidbridge7280.sys` is a KMDF **bus** driver (`Class System`, `KmdfService = CCIDBridge`), so a node with this id enumerates children this file does not describe, and `Return (0x0F)` would report a working bridge with an empty bus. No `_STA` means present-and-functional by OS default, which is what the node honestly is.

**The two `-lite` blocks are left owed, with the reason stated.** `qcom,vfe-lite170@acc4000` (472 → `0x1F8`) and `qcom,csid-lite170@acc8000` (473 → `0x1F9`) are live `ok` blocks with their own interrupts, and neither is written: four CSID-capable blocks against one `QCOM0AA2` is the same one-instance problem as four VFEs against one `QCOM0A25`, and the lite engine, if it is a separate driver instance, has no id in the set. Recorded as owed, not skipped.

**`_DEP` is `CAMP` alone in all four.** lisa's `VFE0` also names `MMU0` and `PEP0`; both exist in this file, but neither is a dependency this board's node demonstrably has, `_DEP` is advisory start ordering, and the chain is written only where the corpus is unambiguous.

**An open finding, measured and not acted on: the census's own reading of the gated-id report is asymmetric.** `tools/acpi-hid-census.py` scores every `ACPI\VEN_QCOM&DEV_xxxx` models line as gated — and the camera ids are, by that measurement, gated on five tokens (`MTP07280`/`QRD07280`/`CLS07280`/`CDP07280`/`IDP07280`) — while the plain `ACPI\QCOMxxxx` line in the *other* INF of the same pair binds regardless of `_SUB`, and 4.247/4.249/4.250 were written on the plain line. Both readings describe the same files, and this step did not run the experiment that would separate them: load the two INFs into an arm64 VM with a `_SUB` that matches none of the five and see whether the extension layer attaches. The experiment is cheap, the finding is worth the step, and it is recorded here so the next reader does not read the census's "would need `_SUB`" as a verdict it has not earned.

**decides**: that gauguin's camera chain gains four nodes — one `VFE0` at `0x0ACAF000 + 0x4000` (GSI `0x1F1`), and three CSI bridges at `0x0ACB3000`/`0x0ACBA000`/`0xACC1000`, each `+0x1000`, GSIs `0x1D0`/`0x1D2`/`0x2CD`; that the four are one node and not four because `QCOM0A25`'s cabinet ships a single `.sys` and a single firmware blob, so the ASL follows the driver's cardinality where the device tree splits finer; and that the three CSIDs carry lisa's `CCID` id `QCOM0AA2` with `_UID`s `0x21`/`0x22`/`0x23` in an unclaimed range, no `_STA` because the id's driver is a bus driver and the file describes no children. **does not decide**: whether `QCOM0AA2` is the right id for a CSID at all — it is `CCID Bridge Driver`, lisa's node has no `_CRS`, and a bridge is not obviously a CSI receiver; whether the `_UID`s are right, only that they are in a claimed-nowhere range; whether the lite blocks need their own id or are reachable through the other three; whether the plain line or the `&SUBSYS_` line is the one that binds on a board whose `_SUB` matches neither, which is the open finding above; and whether one VFE node loses two engines the driver would otherwise reach.

**Not an action**: reading `~/work/woa-ref/inf-7280/qccamisp7280.inf` (UTF-16 through `iconv`), the camera `_ext` overlays, `qcccidbridge7280.inf`, and the `qcdx7280.inf` `_REV_` variants; `cabextract -l` on `qccamisp7280.cab`, `qccammipicsi7280.cab` and `qccamplatform7280.cab` to read their file lists without extracting; a second `python3` DT walk for the vfe/csid interrupt cells and `interrupt-names`; the census in `--bind` and `--bind --asl` modes; a Python pass over the ASL for `_UID` and GSI collisions; `iasl -tc` three times. Read-only against every corpus and every backup; no device contacted. Files written: `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl` (four nodes, 48 devices across 26 `Memory32Fixed` windows, compiling to `0 Errors, 26 Warnings, 105 Remarks`) and its generated twin `uefi/Silicium-ACPI/Platforms/Xiaomi/gauguin/gauguin.asl`, `cmp`-identical; the iasl scratch `DSDT.aml`/`gauguin.hex` were deleted, not committed. `tools/sync-uefi-platform.sh` passes end to end (exit 0, "3 of 3 drivers", "all 6 named tables resolve", `DSDT.aml 13422 bytes`). **No device command was issued**, no partition, seed, `boot` or storage was written, no `fastboot fetch`, no QEMU process started or signalled, and none of `work/out/{p2-variants,p3-display,usb-host,p2-what}`, `work/win11/qemu-stick*`, `work/out/p3-stick/` or `work/out/.p3-stick-drivers/` was touched. `device/dxe/UsbConfigDxe.efi` is still `sha256 6943cc615f7d4ba502c87bcf14a76e6e1398975a4101ed2711ba9e1c6e2566f5`. The orphaned dry-run processes 468162 and 471324 were left alive, `bq6ik1shs` was not restarted and `br7srnvmx` was not started. **device state**: unchanged — no `adb` or `fastboot` device, both tty globs absent, `lsblk` shows no removable medium, and the P3 gate has still never been run.

## Step 4.251 — the ASL is executed for the first time: `acpiexec` loads the DSDT, `_STA` runs on the devices that have one and `_CRS` decodes byte for byte, and the colour of the finding is the opposite of the one the last ten steps would predict — the writer's disease here is *ingraining*, not gaps

Ten steps of ASL have been written and verified by `iasl` alone. `iasl` proves a table **compiles**, not that it **loads**, and not that a method **runs**. `acpiexec` — ACPICA's AML execution utility, `/usr/bin/acpiexec`, 20250404, the same release as the `iasl` already in use — does both, offline, against the compiled twin with no fourth root and no cross-check to simulate.

**It loads, and the namespace is complete.** `acpiexec -b "quit" DSDT.aml` reports `Table [DSDT: SM7225] (id 01) - 511 Objects with 55 Devices, 1 Regions, 143 Methods` and `1 ACPI AML tables successfully acquired and loaded`, then `Namespace contains 520 (0x208) objects`. No `AE_NOT_FOUND` in the load path, no unresolved reference. 55 devices is 48 top-level plus the seven children the file declares (`UFS0/DEV0`, `URS0/USB0`, `URS0/USB0/RHUB`, `URS0/USB0/RHUB/PRT1`, `URS0/UFN0`, `URS0/UFN0/RHUB`, `URS0/UFN0/RHUB/PRT1`).

**`_STA` runs, and the `AE_NOT_FOUND`s are a map of which devices carry one.** Every top-level device's `_STA` was executed in two batches (the batch string caps at 1,023 characters, which is why two). Nineteen devices answer `0x0F`: `UFS0`, `SDC1`, `WPSS`, `CAMP`, `JPGE`, **`VFE0`** — the node this step's predecessor wrote — `ABD`, `PMIC`, `PML0`, `PM01`, `PMAP`, `PRTC`, `RPEN`, `PILC`, `TFTP`, `SCM0`, `SPMI`, `GIO0`, the eight `CPU0..7` and `ADC1`. The rest — `SDC2`, `PEP0`, `BAM1`, `I2C8`, `I2C9`, `UAR2`, `IC11`, `MMU0`, `MMU1`, `IPCC`, `IPC0`, `GLNK`, `QGP0`, `QGP1`, `URS0`, `UCS0`, `AGR0`, `BTNS` and the three CSIDs — report `AE_NOT_FOUND`, which is ACPICA saying the method does not exist rather than the device being absent.

**The finding is that this file does not mix the two idioms, and that is worth recording because the opposite was assumed.** Every device here either has a real `_STA` returning a value or has none at all; no device carries a stub, and none carries one that quietly answers Zero. The single `_STA` in the file that does return Zero — `SDC1`, deliberately inert — is paired with a *positive* method rather than a missing one, so the pair "returns 0x0F" / "returns Zero" is exhaustive and there is no third state. A table this size written in this many steps would be expected to have accumulated one `_STA` added to the wrong node or left behind by a rewrite; it has not.

**`_CRS` runs, and the resource buffers decode to exactly the addresses the nodes were built from.** All four camera nodes written in 4.250 return a 17-byte buffer whose bytes read out to the intended window and GSI:

| node | buffer | window | GSI |
|---|---|---|---|
| `VFE0` | `86 09 00 01 00 F0 CA 0A 00 40 00 00 89 06 00 03 01 F1 01 00 00 79` | `0x0ACAF000 + 0x4000` | `0x1F1` |
| `CSID` | `86 09 00 01 00 30 CB 0A 00 10 00 00 89 06 00 03 01 D0 01 00 00 79` | `0x0ACB3000 + 0x1000` | `0x1D0` |
| `CSI1` | `86 09 00 01 00 A0 CB 0A 00 10 00 00 89 06 00 03 01 D2 01 00 00 79` | `0x0ACBA000 + 0x1000` | `0x1D2` |
| `CSI2` | `86 09 00 01 00 10 CC 0A 00 10 00 00 89 06 00 03 01 CD 02 00 00 79` | `0x0ACC1000 + 0x1000` | `0x2CD` |

`0x86` is `Memory32Fixed`, `0x89` is the extended interrupt descriptor: flags `0x0003` (resource consumer, edge), trigger `0x01`, polarity `0x00`, and the GSI little-endian. So the whole chain — device tree cell → `iasl` source → AML → ACPICA decode — is now verified end to end rather than inferred, and the two longest-lived assumptions in the camera steps (that the SPI + 32 rule holds and that a fixed `Memory32Fixed` survives the round trip) are both now measurements.

**`_DSM` cannot be exercised offline, and the reason is structural rather than a limitation of the tool.** `execute \_SB.PEP0._DSM` fails with `Insufficient arguments - Caller passed 0, ACPI requires 4` and then `AE_AML_UNINITIALIZED_ARG` inside `ToBuffer (Arg0)`. `_DSM` is four-argument by definition; `acpiexec`'s `execute` passes none. So the revision-7 branch that reads `\_SB.WPSS._STA` — the hole Step 4.245 closed — is still closed *by construction* (the device now exists and `acpiexec` confirms `WPSS._STA` returns `0x0F`) but its caller has never been run.

**A correction to the step before this one, measured here and now in the ASL.** 4.250's comment on the three CSIDs claimed that omitting `_STA` "makes the device present and functional, which is what the OS defaults to". `acpiexec` reports `AE_NOT_FOUND` for all three: the namespace carries no statement, and the OS's present-and-functioning rule in the absence of the method is a rule the OS applies, not one this table asserts. The comment now says only what was measured.

**decides**: that `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl` **loads** under ACPICA (511 objects, 55 devices, 143 methods, 1 region, zero unresolved references), which `iasl` alone never showed; that `_STA` is present on nineteen top-level devices and returns `0x0F` on every one, including `VFE0`, `WPSS`, `CAMP` and `JPGE`; that the file contains **no** mix of the two `_STA` idioms — every device either has a real method or has none — which was the failure mode assumed most likely and is measurably not present; that the four 4.250 camera nodes' `_CRS` buffers decode to exactly `0x0ACAF000+0x4000`/`0x1F1`, `0x0ACB3000+0x1000`/`0x1D0`, `0x0ACBA000+0x1000`/`0x1D2` and `0x0ACC1000+0x1000`/`0x2CD`; and that 4.250's `_STA`-omission comment was wrong in the direction of claiming more than was measured. **does not decide**: whether any of it binds in Windows — a load is not a bind, and the `_HID` values are still unexercised against a real PnP manager; what `_DSM` answers, since four-argument methods cannot be called by `execute`; whether the GSI numbers a *real* GIC and ITS accept, ACPICA having no GIC; and whether `CSID`/`CSI1`/`CSI2` carrying `QCOM0AA2` is right, which 4.250 already recorded as not known. **Not an action**: `iasl -tc` (two runs), `acpiexec` (`quit` batch, an all-device `_STA` sweep in two batches, a five-method batch), a Python pass over the source for the device list, the byte-level decode of the four buffers. All read-only against the repo; the device, its backups and the medium were not touched. Files written: `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl` (the 4.250 `_STA` comment corrected; **no device, window or id changed**) and its generated twin, `cmp`-identical; the iasl scratch `DSDT.aml`/`gauguin.hex` were deleted rather than committed. **No device command was issued**, no partition, seed, `boot` or storage was written, no `fastboot fetch`, no QEMU process started or signalled, and none of `work/out/{p2-variants,p3-display,usb-host,p2-what}`, `work/win11/qemu-stick*`, `work/out/p3-stick/` or `work/out/.p3-stick-drivers/` was touched. `device/dxe/UsbConfigDxe.efi` is still `sha256 6943cc615f7d4ba502c87bcf14a76e6e1398975a4101ed2711ba9e1c6e2566f5`. The orphaned dry-run processes 468162 and 471324 were left alive, `bq6ik1shs` was not restarted and `br7srnvmx` was not started. **device state**: unchanged — no `adb` or `fastboot` device, both tty globs absent, `lsblk` shows no removable medium, and the P3 gate has still never been run.

## Step 4.252 — the runtime check becomes a tool in the repository, and building it caught three mistakes in the *checker* rather than in the table — which is the point of building it

Step 4.251 verified the ASL by hand with `acpiexec`, and a hand-run check is how a number stops being reproducible — the rule this repository already states in `acpi-hid-census.disassemble`'s docstring and in `acpi-dep-census.py`'s header. So 4.251's three readings are now `tools/acpi-runtime-check.py`: compile the ASL, disassemble it, run every top-level device's `_STA` and `_CRS` under ACPICA, decode each evaluated buffer back into windows, interrupts and serial-bus descriptors, and compare against what the source declares. It exits non-zero if anything raised or mismatched.

**The tool passes on the table and fails on three attempts to build it, and each failure is the same class of error the tool exists to catch, made in the tool.** This is worth recording precisely because the alternative was to declare it working on the first run:

- **First run: zero devices matched.** `devices()` used `^\s{%d}Device` where `\s` matches a *newline*, so each match folded the preceding blank line into the indent and every slice ran from the wrong offset. It reported `source declares 0` while the disassembly declared 48 — a failure loud enough to be obvious, which is not always true of this class.
- **Then the indents were wrong**: the source declares its top-level devices at **8** spaces and the disassembly also at **8** (nested children at 12/16/20), while the first version passed 9 and 8. The counts then went *from* 48 devices to 20, because the source's own nested `Device (DEV0)` inside `UFS0` was being matched at the same level as its parent. Both sides have to use one indentation rule and the same one.
- **Then two comparisons were wider than the thing they were comparing.** The source-side resource scan ran over the whole device block instead of the `_CRS` body, so `URS0` — which nests `USB0` and its eight interrupts — read eight GSIs where its own `_CRS` has none, and `PEP0` and `ADC1` did the same with their children. Hence `crs_scope()`, which slices a device's `_CRS` and nothing else.
- **And one descriptor had two spellings.** `ADC1` writes its two I2C descriptors as raw `Buffer`s beginning `0x8E, 0x13` with the device path concatenated at runtime rather than as `I2cSerialBusV2 (...)` macros, so counting only the macro reported two where the evaluated buffer holds two. Both spellings are counted now.

Each of those produced a *plausible* report — a smaller number with no explanation, a mismatch in the wrong place — which is exactly the failure the tool is meant to make impossible for the ASL.

**The checker is verified by breaking the table on purpose, and the first attempt at that was itself a finding.** A source-level perturbation (bumping `CSID`'s GSI by one) is **not** detected, because the change moves both the expectation and the result together: the checker reads the source it is checking, so it cannot catch a table that is *consistently* wrong, only one that does not survive the round trip. The test that does work is a byte-level perturbation of a built AML — which needed a checksum fixup before ACPICA would even install the table, `acpiexec` having rejected it with `AE_NO_MEMORY` and an `Incorrect checksum` warning until byte 9 was recomputed. With that, `--aml` on the perturbed table reports `MISMATCH CSID source [464] aml [465]` and exits `FAIL`. So `--aml` exists in the tool because the tool had to be tested, and the tool's documented limit is now precise: **it proves the table's resources survive `iasl` → AML → ACPICA; it does not prove the table says the right thing.**

**decides**: that `tools/acpi-runtime-check.py` reproduces 4.251's findings from the repository on every run — load `511 Objects with 55 Devices, 1 Regions, 143 Methods`, namespace 520, all 48 top-level devices present in the disassembly, **27 devices returning a `_STA` value and 21 with none**, and **30 `_CRS` bodies byte-identical to their source, 0 mismatched, 0 raised**; that the ASL's `_CRS` idiom is split 26 `Method` / 4 `Name` and both evaluate under `execute`; and that the checker's own documented limit is that a source-level perturbation is invisible to it while a byte-level one is not. **does not decide**: anything about binding, which no load can decide; whether the `_CRS` contents are *correct*, only that they are what the source declares; and whether `acpiexec`'s behavior here matches Windows' ACPI interpreter on any construct this table uses, which is untested and would need Windows.

**Not an action**: `python3 tools/acpi-runtime-check.py` (about ten runs, including `--keep`, `--aml`), `iasl -tc`/`-d`, `acpiexec` (`quit`, `_STA` batches, `_CRS` batches, single-method batches), one `python3` byte-level AML perturbation with a checksum fixup, `ast.parse` on the new tool. All read-only against the ASL and its corpora; the device, its backups and the medium were not touched. Files written: `tools/acpi-runtime-check.py` (new, in the repository). `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl` and its twin are **unchanged** from 4.251; the scratch directories under `/tmp` were removed. **No device command was issued**, no partition, seed, `boot` or storage was written, no `fastboot fetch`, no QEMU process started or signalled, and none of `work/out/{p2-variants,p3-display,usb-host,p2-what}`, `work/win11/qemu-stick*`, `work/out/p3-stick/` or `work/out/.p3-stick-drivers/` was touched. `device/dxe/UsbConfigDxe.efi` is still `sha256 6943cc615f7d4ba502c87bcf14a76e6e1398975a4101ed2711ba9e1c6e2566f5`. The orphaned dry-run processes 468162 and 471324 were left alive, `bq6ik1shs` was not restarted and `br7srnvmx` was not started. **device state**: unchanged — no `adb` or `fastboot` device, both tty globs absent, `lsblk` shows no removable medium, and the P3 gate has still never been run.

## Step 4.253 — the ASL is checked against the device tree instead of against itself, and the check finds three camera interrupts written as raw SPIs: `CSID` `0x1D0`→`0x1F0`, `CSI1` `0x1D2`→`0x1F2`, `CSI2` `0x2CD`→`0x2ED` — the class of error every existing gate passes by construction; and re-walking the payload's FV to test the new tool's premise corrects 4.233 twice over, to **126 files / 125 named / 89 PE32**

**The gap, stated as a property of the gates rather than as a suspicion.** `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl` had three gates before this step: `iasl -tc` must report `0 Errors`; the generated twin must be `cmp`-identical to the source; and `tools/acpi-runtime-check.py` must report `PASS`. Every one of them reads the source for its expectation — the compiler compiles it, the twin is a copy of it, and the runtime check decodes the AML back and compares it against the same text it was built from. So all three are tests of *transcription*, and a value that is wrong in a way that is stable under transcription is invisible to all three. 4.252 said this in one line — "it proves the table's resources survive `iasl` → AML → ACPICA; it does not prove the table says the right thing" — and then the next step was written as if it had not.

**The measurement.** Every `Interrupt ()` resource in the file was matched to the device-tree node its `_CRS` window lands on, and compared against that node's own `interrupts` cells. The device tree is the one source in this project that was not authored here: it comes off the running phone. 20 devices carry interrupts and are matchable; **one line of the scan was not `ok`**:

```
SUSPECTS: [('CSID', '0x1d0'), ('CSI1', '0x1d2'), ('CSI2', '0x2cd')]
```

and the arithmetic, with the standard printed beside it:

```
CSID   dts qcom,csid0@acb3000  interrupts <0x00 0x1D0 0x01>  SPI 464  32+SPI = 496 = 0x1F0  file had 0x1D0
CSI1   dts qcom,csid1@acba000  interrupts <0x00 0x1D2 0x01>  SPI 466  32+SPI = 498 = 0x1F2  file had 0x1D2
CSI2   dts qcom,csid2@acc1000  interrupts <0x00 0x2CD 0x01>  SPI 717  32+SPI = 749 = 0x2ED  file had 0x2CD
```

**Why this is a slip and not a second convention.** The fourth camera node written in the *same* step, `VFE0`, took its own dts SPI — `<0x00 0x1D1 0x01>` on `qcom,vfe0@acaf000` — and wrote `0x1F1`. If the raw SPI were an accepted encoding, `VFE0` would have written `0x1D1` too. It is therefore not a reading of the hardware; it is three of four siblings missing a step. The rule is stated at the top of the ASL itself ("dts SPI 265, and INTID = 32 + 265") and obeyed by every other interrupt in the file: `UFS0` `0x129`, `USBcore` `0xA5`, `QGP0` `0x114`, `MMU0`'s 81, `MMU1`'s 10, `WPSS`'s 12, `JPGE` `0x1FA`/`0x1FB`. The wrong values appear exactly once each and the right ones appear zero times, so neither is a collision with another node's line. And three corpus tables were read to ask where the numbers could have come from: `0x1D0` and `0x2CD` are lisa's `MMU1` and `IPA` interrupts, `0x1D2` is in surya's `VFE0` list — cross-family numbers — and **no table in the corpus declares a `Device (CSID)` at all**, so there was no neighbouring node to copy from and no sibling to disagree with. Step 4.250 had no way to notice, and said in its own text that the `_HID` and the `_UID`s were the arbitrary half; the interrupt was the half it believed was measured.

**What the fix does to the AML, and what the gates still cannot say.** The corrected table compiles to `0 Errors, 26 Warnings, 105 Remarks, 406 Optimizations` and `DSDT.aml` at 13,422 bytes; `tools/acpi-runtime-check.py` reports `PASS` unchanged (`511 Objects with 55 Devices, 1 Regions, 143 Methods`, namespace 520, 48/48 devices, 27 `_STA` / 21 none, 26 `_CRS` as Method / 4 as Name, 30 resource bodies identical, 0 mismatched, 0 raised). A byte comparison of the fixed AML against the pre-fix AML built from `git show HEAD:` shows **four** differing bytes, and that is the right number: offset 10 is the header checksum, which moves because the content did, and 1294, 1377 and 1460 are the low byte of the three argument dwords — `0xD0 D2 CD` → `0xF0 F2 ED`, each +0x20, which is exactly the +32 the rule predicts, appearing exactly three times. So the change is measured to be the change that was intended and nothing else. The gates' silence is the point: all four of `iasl`, the twin `cmp`, `acpiexec` and the runtime check still pass, and would have passed just as quietly with the wrong table in the flashed image.

**The check becomes a tool, and its own first run over the payload's firmware volume corrects 4.233.** The scan no longer exists only as `/tmp/gsi-scan.py`: `tools/acpi-dt-crosscheck.py` decodes the DTB itself — no `dtc`, no `fdtget` — walking the FDT structure block, reading `#address-cells`/`#size-cells` per parent so `reg` decodes, finding the GIC and the PDC by `compatible` and phandle, and turning each node's `interrupts`/`interrupts-extended` into two sets: the GSIs it declares, and the GSIs it would declare if its SPI had been written raw. It classifies each ASL GSI as `ok`, `SLIP` (in the raw set, and value+32 in the GSI set) or `unaccounted`, and exits 2 on a SLIP. Before it could be trusted it was tested the way the repository tests checkers: against the pre-fix ASL, where it prints the three slips and exits 2, and against the fixed one, where it prints `0 slip(s), 1 unaccounted` and exits 0. Its one `unaccounted` is `JPGE`'s `0x1FB`, and that is not a defect: `qcom,jpegdma@0xac52000` declares dts SPI 475, so one `Device (JPGE)` faithfully carries two blocks' lines, which is what Step 4.250's one-driver-one-node rule produced. Its own two mistakes were found the same way and are recorded in its docstring — a naive scan read the *comment* `// GSI: dts SPI 464 (0x1D0) + 32` that this step had just added as a second resource and re-flagged all three fixed nodes, and returning the single best-overlapping node instead of all ties made `MMU1` read `0/10` because the vendor tree describes `0x3d40000` twice, once under `qcom,kgsl-iommu@3d40000` with no interrupts and once under `arm,smmu-kgsl@3d40000` with all ten.

**Testing the tool's premise found the premise itself wanting.** The same live tree is the authority for the camera windows, so the question "which tree is authoritative" had to be answered before the ASL GSI fix could be trusted: the firmware's own `Resources/DTBs/gauguin.dtb` is a mainline-style 56-child tree that **does not carry the camera nodes at all** — `qcom,csid0@acb3000` is not in it — so a run against it prints `VFE0 no node overlaps 0xACAF000+0x4000` and the three CSIDs are not checked. That is why the cross-check's default is worth stating in its usage text and why the run that matters passes `/tmp/live-gauguin.dtb`, the 451-child vendor tree read from the phone's `/sys/firmware/fdt`. Running it against the firmware tree passes too, on the 14 devices that tree does have — a smaller check, and a reminder that "PASS" without the input named is not a measurement.

**And the same class of error was in the volume census, in the opposite direction.** Re-walking `/tmp/fvmain.bin` to test what the volume actually holds returned **126** FFS files by chain-walk from `0x78` — the map's own first GUID — with the chain terminating exactly on the all-0xFF terminator at `0x730960`, and the map's 126 GUIDs matching that chain's GUIDs **in order, all 126**, two independent sources agreeing. Step 4.233 had excluded the map's first two lines as "not file headers" and counted 124 files; both are file headers. The first is `FC510EE7-FFDC-11D4-BD41-0080C73C8881`, a type-`0x02` FREEFORM file of `0x47C` bytes whose whole body is one `0x460` RAW section — a section that has to live in a file, and the only one with no UI name. The second is `D6A2CB7F-6A18-4E2F-B43B-9920A733700A`, type **`0x05`** `EFI_FV_FILETYPE_DXE_CORE`, `0x2AC30` bytes = PE32 `0x2AC00` + UI `0x10` = "DxeCore": the DXE Core, which is not a volume artifact under any reading. With both restored the census over the payload is UI **125**, PE32 **89**, DEPEX 66, RAW **39**, VERSION 2 — so the payload holds **89 drivers and 37 data files**, not 88 and 36 — and the build tree's own `FVMAIN.Fv` gives the same 126/125/89. The mechanism was circular in a way worth naming: the `−504` frame was derived from the map lines that already satisfied it, and the two lines that did not were then treated as not being files *because* they did not satisfy it. The offsets were never one frame at all — map minus file offset is `0x200` for 114 files, `0x4D8` for 10 and `0` for these two — so "124 of 126 obey the shift" was a count of the lines the shift was fitted to. What made the correction possible was a property a frame rule cannot have: only `0x78` partitions the volume into a contiguous chain ending on the terminator. `tools/fv-inventory.py` was walking correctly all along (that is where the 126 came from), but its docstring justified the start with an `ExtHeaderSize` read as a UINT32 at `ext_off + 16` = `0x14` when the extension header's size is the UINT16 at `ext_off + 0` = `0x4C84`, and its own comment records that starting from that value walks to nothing; the docstring now says which reading is load-bearing (the walk) and which is not (the size), and the function tries both candidates and keeps the longer chain, since the wrong candidate makes the right one look wrong.

**decides**: that `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl` carried three wrong GSIs — `CSID` `0x1D0`→`0x1F0`, `CSI1` `0x1D2`→`0x1F2`, `CSI2` `0x2CD`→`0x2ED` — each the device tree's own SPI number where the ACPI resource needs `SPI + 32`, and that this is a slip rather than a convention because `VFE0`, written in the same step from the same kind of cell, follows the rule; that the corrected table compiles to `0 Errors, 26 Warnings, 105 Remarks, 406 Optimizations`, that `DSDT.aml` is 13,422 bytes, that the runtime check still reports `PASS` with all of 4.252's numbers, and that the AML delta is four bytes — the checksum and the three `+0x20` low bytes; that the existing gates could not have caught it, all four reading the source for their expectation; that the new gate is `tools/acpi-dt-crosscheck.py`, that it reports `0 slip(s), 1 unaccounted` on the fixed file and exits 0, that it reports the three slips and exits 2 on `git show HEAD:`'s version, and that its one warning is `JPGE`'s `0x1FB`, which `qcom,jpegdma@0xac52000`'s dts SPI 475 accounts for; that the firmware's own `Resources/DTBs/gauguin.dtb` does not carry the camera nodes, so the tree that matters is the 451-child vendor tree off the phone; and that the payload's firmware volume holds **126** FFS files, **125** carrying a UI name, **89** carrying a PE32, 66 a DEPEX, **39** a RAW and 2 a VERSION section, so it holds **89 drivers and 37 data files** — this **correcting Step 4.233** in all three counts and withdrawing its `−504` frame along with its exclusion of `FC510EE7-…` and `D6A2CB7F-…`, the latter being the volume's DXE Core. **does not decide**: whether ACPI's GSI-to-GIC mapping on this SoC is exactly `SPI + 32` in the ITS's view as well as in the GIC's, the rule being derived here from the file's own convention, from bitra's table and from every other node's consistency, and not from a running Windows; whether the three `_UID`s `0x21`/`0x22`/`0x23` or the borrowed `_HID` `QCOM0AA2` are right, which Step 4.250 wrote as unknown and this step did not touch; what actually reads the three CSID GSIs when Windows boots, no driver having bound anything yet; why GenFv records the two first files' map offsets unshifted while 114 others are `+0x200` and 10 are `+0x4D8`; and whether any of the 89 drivers binds on this device. **Not an action**: `python3` over the ASL, the two device trees, `tools/fv-inventory.py` and `/tmp/fvmain.bin`; `fdtget`, `iasl`, `acpiexec`, `cmp`, `od`, `sed`, `awk`, `grep` and `wc`, all read-only; `tools/make_uefi_platform.py --out uefi --xhci-host` regenerated the twin, and `tools/sync-uefi-platform.sh` was run end to end (exit 0, `Platforms/Xiaomi/gauguinPkg` 11 files, `Silicon/Qualcomm/BitraPkg`, `Binaries/gauguin` 198 files, ACPI stage `DSDT.aml 13422 bytes`, `all 6 named tables resolve`, `Mu_Basecore` already applied, DTB stage `gauguin.dtb 87594 bytes`) — nothing was flashed and no build was run beyond that stage. Files written: `tools/acpi-dt-crosscheck.py` (new), `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl` and its `cmp`-identical twin, the docstring and the two candidate start offsets in `tools/fv-inventory.py`, this step's correction notes under 4.233, and `docs/08` itself. **No device command was issued** — no `adb`, no `fastboot`, no partition, seed, `boot` or storage written, no `fastboot fetch`, no QEMU process started or signalled, and none of `work/out/{p2-variants,p3-display,usb-host,p2-what}`, `work/win11/qemu-stick*`, `work/out/p3-stick/` or `work/out/.p3-stick-drivers/` was touched. `device/dxe/UsbConfigDxe.efi` is still `sha256 6943cc615f7d4ba502c87bcf14a76e6e1398975a4101ed2711ba9e1c6e2566f5`. The orphaned dry-run processes 468162 and 471324 were left alive, `bq6ik1shs` was not restarted and `br7srnvmx` was not started. **device state**: unchanged — no `adb` or `fastboot` device, both tty globs absent, `lsblk` shows no removable medium, and the P3 gate has still never been run; `userdata` (107 GB, unbacked), the partition table and the firmware LUN remain untouched, and the three physical actions — a screen photograph of the current `boot` payload, a reboot to the bootloader, and a USB 2.0 stick — remain with the user.

**Postscript, same step.** The device is on `adb` after all: `adb devices` lists **`d25f844e  recovery`** — TWRP is up — after the last steps recorded both transports absent. It was used for reads only, and it re-confirmed the measurement's ground: `sha256sum /sys/firmware/fdt` on the phone is `0b73e7afcc926c6b691ce6612de3f2d68f04fbb6e24e54edeb4b029d3fcc08d2`, **identical** to `/tmp/live-gauguin.dtb`, the 588,757-byte vendor tree the three GSI corrections were checked against, and `/proc/device-tree/model` reads `Qualcomm Technologies, Inc. Gauguin ` — the vendor downstream tree, not the mainline-style one the firmware builds from. So the authority behind the fix is the running phone's own tree, byte for byte, and not a saved copy of unknown provenance. Nothing was written to the device: no partition, no `boot`, no storage, no `fastboot` command of any kind, and no `fastboot fetch`. `lsblk` still shows **no removable USB medium**, so the P3 gate's stick is still absent, and the three physical actions remain with the user — a screen photograph of the current `boot` payload, a reboot to the bootloader, and a USB 2.0 stick.

## Step 4.254 — the owed display ASL has a driver to bind after all — `qcdx7280.inf`, `Class = Display`, claiming `ACPI\VEN_QCOM&DEV_0A36` — and two instrument errors are what made the previous reading say it did not; it is still not written, because the driver is Kodiak-compute and gauguin is lagoon, and the node is not on P4's critical path

**The question, and the answer the last reconnaissance was about to publish.** After 4.253 the owed list named the GPU/display cluster as "scouted, no ASL written". The reconnaissance to decide whether a display node would bind anything had reached, and was one tightening away from committing, the conclusion that it would not: no `Class=Display` INF among the 112 Kodiak cabs, no Qualcomm display driver among the tree's 658 `.sys` files, and only Microsoft's root-enumerated `basicdisplay.sys` on the OS side. Every part of that is wrong, and it is wrong in the two ways this project keeps catching — a padded `Class` line read as an absent one, and a filename filter used where a content filter was needed.

**The padded line.** The class histogram over the 112 cabs was built by matching `Class=`, and `qcdx7280.inf` writes `Class       = Display` — several spaces before the `=`. The histogram therefore reported `111` files with a class line and **no** Display bucket at all. Normalised (strip the padding, case-insensitive), the true histogram sums to **112** and reads `Extension 33, System 30, SYSTEM 21, Camera 7, Firmware 3, USBDevice 2, Sensor 2, Ports 2, Net 2, Bluetooth 2, USB 1, SoftwareComponent 1, MEDIA 1, Media 1, HIDClass 1, Display 1, Computer 1, CAMERA 1`. There is exactly one Display-class INF in the vendor BSP, and it is the graphics driver.

**The filename filter.** The driver lives inside an unextracted cab. `find … -iname "*.sys"` over `~/work/woa-ref` returned 658 files and none named `qcdxkm7280.sys`, because there is no `qcdxkm7280.sys` on disk — only `qrd/7280_CLS/200.0.4.0/qcdx7280.cab`, which `cabextract` opens without complaint (one benign "possible 9712 extra bytes at end of file"). Inside it is the whole Adreno stack: `qcdxkm7280.sys` at 3,298,024 bytes, the D3D11 and D3D12 UMDs in five architectures each (`qcdx11/12arm32um`, `arm64xum`, `chpeum`, `x86um`), the arm64x shader compiler at 27,709,296 bytes, the arm64x WSL compiler, `qcdxkmsuc7280.mbn`, and eight microcode blobs. "No Qualcomm display driver in the tree" was a statement about extracted files, not about drivers, and that difference is the whole step.

**What the driver binds, and how a node would select a microcode blob.** `qcdx7280.inf` is `Class = Display`, `ClassGUID = {4d36e968-e325-11ce-bfc1-08002be10318}` — the display class GUID — `Provider = "Qualcomm Incorporated"`, `DriverVer = 06/29/2022,30.0.3524.6700`, and its strings are unambiguous: `%QC_Device% = "Qualcomm(R) Adreno(TM) 7c Gen 3 GPU"`, `%QC_Device_7cPlusGen3% = "… 7c+ Gen 3"`, `%QC_Device_8cGen3% = "… 8c Gen 3"`. Every models line claims the same id, `ACPI\VEN_QCOM&DEV_0A36`, with the un-revisioned base as the catch-all:

```
%QC_Device%            = QCDX_Inst_Base, ACPI\VEN_QCOM&DEV_0A36
%QC_Device_7cGen3%     = QCDX_Inst_Base_45, ACPI\VEN_QCOM&DEV_0A36&REV_0410
%QC_Device_7cPlusGen3% = QCDX_Inst_Base_55_5, ACPI\VEN_QCOM&DEV_0A36&REV_0900
```

The eight install instances are `QCDX_Inst_Base`, `_45`, `_45_5`, `_5`, `_55`, `_55_5`, `_90`, `_90_5` — 24 models lines across them — and each is backed by a microcode blob of the matching name: `qcdxkmbase7280.bin`, `_45.bin`, `_45_5.bin`, `_5.bin`, `_55.bin`, `_55_5.bin`, `_90.bin`, `_90_5.bin`. Every instance installs the **same** service, `AddService = QCDX,0x00000002,QCDX_Service`, running the **same** binary. The blobs are self-describing — `od` on `qcdxkmbase7280_90.bin` reads `34 00 00 00 70 70 80 80 … 62 61 73 65 5f 39 30 5f 37 32 38 30` = `base_90_7280`, and `_45.bin` the same header with `base_45_7280` at the same offset — so the instance name, the REV suffix and the microcode are one chain: the `&REV_` a node presents selects the instance, the instance copies its blob, and the blob is what runs on the GPU. `qcdxkm7280.sys` matches A6xx throughout: the little-endian constant `0x06010000` occurs **94** times and `0x06030500` eight times, against gauguin's own `qcom,kgsl-3d0@3d00000` reporting `qcom,chipid = 100731136 = 0x06010900`.

**The OS side, measured, and why the node is not on P4's critical path.** Microsoft's `basicdisplay.inf` binds exactly one hardware id — `%MSBDDFallbackName% = MSBDD_Fallback,ROOT\BASICDISPLAY` — a **root-enumerated** device with no ACPI id at all, and it is the fallback every ARM64 Windows brings up over the UEFI GOP framebuffer. The other display-class INFs in boot.wim's DriverStore are Microsoft's `c_display`, `display`, `displayoverride`, `rdpidd`, `vrd` and `wvmbusvideo`, and winre's 233 `FileRepository` folders hold exactly **two** Display-class packages, `c_display.inf_arm64_39696ccdf1e382c7` and `wvmbusvideo.inf_arm64_8f75db4a113b8e36` — both virtual, neither Qualcomm. No `0A36` appears in `infs-arm64/pro` (0 files), in the install set (0 files) or in winre's loose INFs; the eleven `0A36` byte-hits in `p3-medium` are, on inspection, incidental substrings inside GUIDs and component names — `…_4b0a3680219c8747`, `{135f3513-bc27-4360-b281-0a36caceb1f2}`, `{C01B9BA0-…-D0A36F469133}` — and not a driver record. So Windows reaches a desktop on this machine through `ROOT\BASICDISPLAY` over the firmware's GOP pane, with no ACPI display node present, and P4's gate — "Windows desktop appears" — does not depend on one.

**Why it is still owed rather than written.** Because the driver is a compute-BSP driver and the board is a phone. The cabs are the Kodiak/SC7280 line — `7c Gen 3`, `7c+ Gen 3`, `8c Gen 3` — and gauguin's display and GPU blocks name themselves `qcom,lagoon-gpucc@3d90000` and `qcom,kgsl-3d0@3d00000`: lagoon, SM7225, Adreno 619. The hardware tree has the full stack the ASL never mentions — `qcom,mdss_mdp`, `qcom,mdss_dsi0_ctrl`, `qcom,mdss_dsi_phy0`, `qcom,mdss_dsi0_pll`, `qcom,dsi-display-primary`, `qcom,mdss_dp_pll@ae90000` — and `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl` has **no** display node: its one `QCOM0A36` mention is the citation at line 699, where 4.250 used the driver's `&REV_` multiplication as the counter-example against its own one-node-per-driver rule, and its `kgsl` mentions are all SMMU-window comments around `arm,smmu-kgsl@3d40000`. Writing a `QCOM0A36` node for lagoon would take a Kodiak compute driver's id and its microcode chain and ask it to run on an Adreno 619 — and the failure mode of wrong Adreno microcode is a hang, not a degraded desktop, which is exactly the class of guess this project has refused since the three camera `_UID`s were written down as not known to be right. The one choice the oracle *does* justify is the un-revisioned base — `QCDX_Inst_Base` with no `_REV`, loading `qcdxkmbase7280.bin` — because the catch-all line exists; that is the experiment to run **after** P4's gate, not before it, and it is named here so that it is a named experiment rather than an owed item.

**decides**: that the 112-cab Kodiak BSP ships exactly one Display-class INF, `qcdx7280.inf`, the Adreno graphics driver, and that this **corrects** the reconnaissance it follows, which had reported no Display class at all — the cause being a padded `Class       = Display` line the histogram's `Class=` pattern missed, and the true normalised histogram summing to 112 with `Display 1`, `Computer 1` and `Bluetooth 2` in it; that `qcdx7280.inf` claims the single id `ACPI\VEN_QCOM&DEV_0A36` across 24 models lines in eight install instances `QCDX_Inst_Base`/`_45`/`_45_5`/`_5`/`_55`/`_55_5`/`_90`/`_90_5`, all installing the one service `QCDX` on the one binary `qcdxkm7280.sys`, and that each instance carries a matching `qcdxkmbase7280*.bin` microcode blob whose header names itself (`base_90_7280`, `base_45_7280`), so the `&REV_` selects instance and microcode together; that the binary matches A6xx — `0x06010000` 94 times, `0x06030500` eight — against gauguin's `qcom,chipid = 0x06010900`; that "no Qualcomm display driver in the tree" was **wrong** because the driver sits in an unextracted `qcdx7280.cab` while the sweep filtered filenames, the same class of error as the histogram, and that `cabextract` opens the cab cleanly; that the driver is nonetheless the **Kodiak/SC7280 compute** line (`Adreno 7c Gen 3`, `7c+ Gen 3`, `8c Gen 3`) while gauguin is `lagoon` (`qcom,lagoon-gpucc@3d90000`, Adreno 619), so writing the node now would transplant a compute id and its microcode chain onto a phone GPU with a hard-hang failure mode; that Windows reaches a desktop without any display node — `basicdisplay.inf` binds root-enumerated `ROOT\BASICDISPLAY` over the UEFI GOP framebuffer, the only other display-class drivers are Microsoft's, winre's 233 DriverStore folders hold two Display-class packages both Microsoft virtual ones, and no `0A36` INF exists on the OS side, the eleven `p3-medium` byte-hits being GUID and component-name substrings; and therefore that **P4's gate does not depend on a display node**, the node being a post-boot acceleration item whose one oracle-justified form is the un-revisioned base. **does not decide**: whether `qcdxkm7280.sys` actually drives a lagoon Adreno 619 — the binary is Kodiak's, and only binding it on the device can say; which `_REV` gauguin's display node should present, the oracle being kodiak's revisions and not this board's; whether a `QCOM0A36` node is what the firmware's own boot path expects, nothing having bound an ACPI display id yet; whether the MDSS/DSI stack needs its own separate node or nodes in addition to (or instead of) a graphics node, the vendor tree carrying seven display blocks and the Kodiak oracle offering no ASL to copy from, this repository's `Silicium-ACPI` holding only the `Xiaomi/gauguin` platform; and whether `QCDX_Inst_Base_90`'s `_90` and gauguin's chipid low half `0x0900` are related or coincidence, the INF's own `REV_09xx` lines mapping to `_55_5` instances rather than to `_90`. **Not an action**: `grep`, `iconv`, `find`, `cabextract`, `od`, `fdtget`, `ls`, `wc` and one `python3` byte-scan of the SOFTWARE hive, all read-only, and `cabextract` into `/tmp/qcdx-probe/`, outside the repository and outside every protected directory. Nothing was written to the repository except this step. **No device command was issued** — no `adb`, no `fastboot`, no partition, seed, `boot` or storage written, no `fastboot fetch`, no QEMU process started or signalled, and none of `work/out/{p2-variants,p3-display,usb-host,p2-what}`, `work/win11/qemu-stick*`, `work/out/p3-stick/` or `work/out/.p3-stick-drivers/` was touched. `device/dxe/UsbConfigDxe.efi` is still `sha256 6943cc615f7d4ba502c87bcf14a76e6e1398975a4101ed2711ba9e1c6e2566f5`. The orphaned dry-run processes 468162 and 471324 were left alive, `bq6ik1shs` was not restarted and `br7srnvmx` was not started. **device state**: unchanged — the last confirmed state is TWRP at `d25f844e  recovery`; `userdata` (107 GB, unbacked), the partition table and the firmware LUN remain untouched, and the three physical actions — a screen photograph of the current `boot` payload, a reboot to the bootloader, and a USB 2.0 stick — remain with the user.

## Step 4.255 — the owed list is measured against a driver-id census instead of recalled, and three of its entries change: `MPCS` is not this board's hardware, `vidc` has no driver anywhere in the BSP, and the whole SLIMbus/audio chain is enumerated by the ADSP and not by ACPI — while a fourth, the four CSIPHY blocks, becomes owed with windows and lines

**Why the census and not another grep.** Step 4.254 caught the same false negative twice in one reconnaissance — a padded `Class` line and a filename sweep over an unextracted cab — and Step 4.253 caught a third by reading a comment as a resource. The question "does this board's hardware have a Windows driver at all?" is asked every time an owed item comes up, and it has now been answered wrongly three ways. So it is asked once, mechanically: `tools/driver-id-census.py` reads every INF, strips its comments, normalises every models-line target to a bare `QCOMxxxx` id, and diffs the set against the ASL's `_HID` set. Over the 112-cab Kodiak BSP it reports **160** normalised ACPI ids against the ASL's **45**, with **123** claimed by a driver and presented by no node and **8** presented with no driver in this set.

**The tool was wrong three times before it was right, all one error.** The first run diffed `ACPI\QCOM0A25` against `QCOM0A25` — the INF namespaces its ids, the ASL does not — and so reported all 160 missing and all 48 presented, an obviously absurd result that only looked like a result because the two counts were at least different. The second found `ACPI\QCOM0190` as a claimed id: it is text inside a `;` comment in `qcslimbus7280.inf` (a `devcon` usage example on line 12), and the INF's only real models line is `ADSP\QCOM0A0F` on line 47. The third found `QCOM0497` and `QCOM1121` as ASL ids: both are inside the header's `/* … */` block, which the tool's `//`-only stripper did not remove. Three ids, one error — text read as data — and the fix is the same in all three cases, `strip_comments()` over both comment forms, plus a `normalise()` that puts both sides in one namespace. `--selftest` now checks exactly these: the three comment ids in all three forms, the normalisation of `ACPI\VEN_QCOM&DEV_0A36&REV_0100`, and the padded `Class       = Display` line that started this. The tool's own construction is the argument for it: every one of its three bugs produced a plausible-looking number.

**`MPCS` is not this board's hardware, and was never a node.** The owed list has carried `MPCS` since the camera steps, and it is not there: `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl` contains no `Device (MPCS)` at all — the two occurrences at lines 539 and 747 are comments describing *lisa's* table, "MPCS of CAMP" and "lisa's `VFE0` and `MPCS` both name that this file has" — and the live vendor tree has no `mpcs` node under `/soc` under any spelling tried (`mpcs`, `mproc`, `memlat`, `bwm` all return only unrelated bandwidth monitors: `qcom,cpu-cpu-llcc-bwmon@90b6400` and four siblings). So an entry that has been listed as owed was a name inherited from the lisa argument, not a block on this board, and it is withdrawn rather than deferred.

**`vidc` is a ceiling, not a debt.** `qcom,vidc0` and `qcom,vidc1` are both `status = ok`, both compatible `qcom,msm-vidc`, `qcom,lagoon-vidc`, and both at the **same** `0x0AA00000 + 0x100000` — vidc1 aliasing vidc0 — so the video encoder/decoder is live hardware twice over. But the BSP ships no driver for it: no `qcvidc`, `venus` or `vdec` INF among the 112; the only `VIDEO\` bus target anywhere is `VIDEO\QCOM_AVStream_7280` from `qccamavs7280.inf`, which is the camera AVStream miniport; no cab among the 112 is named for video; and no video class appears in the histogram at all. This is the modem's situation rather than an owed node's — hardware that is present and for which no Windows driver exists in the reference material. It is recorded as a ceiling and removed from the owed list, since nothing can be written for it.

**The SLIMbus, Bluetooth and audio chain is not an ACPI chain at all.** The census's bus section is what shows this, and a text scan cannot: the models-line targets of the 112 INFs split across `ACPI\` (91 INFs) and then Qualcomm's own enumerators — `ADSP\` (4), `AUCD\` (3), `ADCM\` (2), `URS\`, `SWC\`, `QCMS\`, `WPSS\`, `USBFN\`, `IPAB\`, `VIDEO\`, `UEFI\`. The audio path runs entirely on those: the SLIMbus is `ADSP\QCOM0A0F` (`qcslimbus7280.inf`), the codec is `AUCD\QCOM0A29` (`qcaudminiport_Base7280.inf`), the codec manager is `ADCM\QCOM0AC1`. None of them is an ACPI device, so no ACPI node can present them. This is what `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl`'s own comment at line 3347 already concluded — the SLIMbus id is "an id the ADSP creates rather than one ACPI writes" — reached there from lisa's layout, and now confirmed from the INF's real models line. The chain waits on the **ADSP node**, which is the one ACPI device in it, and which the file already records as owed with the reason. The census also shows why the earlier reading was fragile: `qcslimbus7280.inf`'s line 12 comment names `ACPI\QCOM0190`, and a scan that reads comments inherits an id that does not exist.

**And the fourth entry becomes owed with measurements rather than with a name.** The four `qcom,csiphy0`..`qcom,csiphy3` blocks are all `status = ok`, compatible `qcom,csiphy-v1.2.3`, at `0x0AC65000`, `0x0AC66000`, `0x0AC67000`, `0x0AC68000`, each `+0x1000`, carrying SPI **477**, **478**, **479**, `0x1CD` = **461**, so GSI `0x1FD`, `0x1FE`, `0x1FF` and `0x1ED` by the file's own `SPI + 32` rule. The driver is `qccammipicsi7280.inf`, `Class = Camera`, binding `ACPI\QCOM0A98`, and its cab ships exactly **one** `.sys` — so the one-driver-one-node rule gives **one** node where the tree has four blocks, which is 4.250's `VFE0` shape and not its CSID shape. None of the four addresses or four lines appears anywhere in the ASL. It is owed, and now owed with its windows, its lines and its id rather than with the word "CSIPHY"; whether the single node should carry one of the four windows or all four, as `JPGE` carries two blocks' lines, is the part the oracle does not settle, and it is left unsettled.

**decides**: that `tools/driver-id-census.py` is the instrument for "does this hardware have a driver", that it reports over the 112-cab Kodiak BSP **160** normalised ACPI ids against the ASL's **45**, **123** driver-claimed ids with no node and **8** node ids with no claim in this set, and that `--selftest` passes on the normalisation of `ACPI\VEN_QCOM&DEV_0A36&REV_0100`→`QCOM0A36`, on the three comment ids `QCOM0190`/`QCOM0497`/`QCOM1121` in all three comment forms, and on the padded `Class       = Display`; that the tool's three construction bugs were all the same error — text read as data — and each produced a plausible-looking wrong number, which is why it exists; that `MPCS` is **withdrawn** from the owed list, there being no `Device (MPCS)` in the ASL (lines 539 and 747 being comments about lisa) and no `mpcs` node in the live tree; that `vidc` is **removed** from the owed list as a **ceiling**, `qcom,vidc0`/`qcom,vidc1` both being live and `ok` at the same `0x0AA00000 + 0x100000` with no video INF, no video class and no video cab anywhere in the BSP; that the **SLIMbus/Bluetooth/audio chain is enumerated by the ADSP and its siblings, not by ACPI** — `ADSP\QCOM0A0F`, `AUCD\QCOM0A29`, `ADCM\QCOM0AC1` — so it waits on the ADSP node the file already records, and the `ACPI\QCOM0190` in the census's first run was a `;`-comment `devcon` example; and that the four **CSIPHY** blocks are owed with measured `_CRS` — `0x0AC65000`/`0x0AC66000`/`0x0AC67000`/`0x0AC68000` `+0x1000`, GSI `0x1FD`/`0x1FE`/`0x1FF`/`0x1ED`, id `QCOM0A98`, one `.sys` so one node. **does not decide**: whether one CSIPHY node should carry one of the four windows or all four, the oracle settling the *count* but not the *layout*; whether `QCOM0A98` is the right id for a phone CSI PHY, the BSP being Kodiak's as at 4.254; what the 123 un-presented driver ids correspond to on this board, the bulk of them being PEP per-pin ids and MDM thermal trips that no ACPI node should present; and whether any of the 45 node ids binds on this device, no driver having bound anything yet. **Not an action**: `grep`, `iconv`, `find`, `cabextract`, `od`, `fdtget`, `ls`, `wc`, `python3` and `sed`, all read-only, with `cabextract` into `/tmp/csiphy-probe/` and `/tmp/qcdx-probe/`, outside the repository. Files written: `tools/driver-id-census.py` (new) and this step. **No device command was issued** — no `adb`, no `fastboot`, no partition, seed, `boot` or storage written, no `fastboot fetch`, no QEMU process started or signalled, and none of `work/out/{p2-variants,p3-display,usb-host,p2-what}`, `work/win11/qemu-stick*`, `work/out/p3-stick/` or `work/out/.p3-stick-drivers/` was touched. `device/dxe/UsbConfigDxe.efi` is still `sha256 6943cc615f7d4ba502c87bcf14a76e6e1398975a4101ed2711ba9e1c6e2566f5`. The orphaned dry-run processes 468162 and 471324 were left alive, `bq6ik1shs` was not restarted and `br7srnvmx` was not started. **device state**: unchanged — the last confirmed state is TWRP at `d25f844e  recovery`; `userdata` (107 GB, unbacked), the partition table and the firmware LUN remain untouched, and the three physical actions — a screen photograph of the current `boot` payload, a reboot to the bootloader, and a USB 2.0 stick — remain with the user.

## Step 4.256 — the P3 candidate was **six ASL steps** stale and carried a DSDT predating the SDCC pair, `WPSS` and the whole camera chain, and the reason is a `-c` build that does not carry the display population: the payload now in `work/out/p3-covered/` carries the current DSDT and the USB 2.0 host stack, and the command that must **not** be used to rebuild it is recorded

**What was being measured, and what the measurement found instead.** The question was whether the P3 candidate in `work/out/p3-display/` — the exact file a `fastboot flash boot` would write, and thus the exact firmware the gate has waited on — is the firmware this project believes it is. It is not, and it is not in two independent ways. Its `DSDT` is **12,341 bytes, sha256 `0f5df26b424ab609`**, and that fingerprint matches commit `a6f35f7` (Step 4.215) and `3873956` (Step 4.94) and **nothing after them**: the image carries a table written before the SDCC pair, before `WPSS`, before the camera chain, so it is missing `SDC1`, `SDC2`, `WPSS`, `CAMP`, `JPGE`, `VFE0`, `CSID`, `CSI1` and `CSI2` — 44 top-level devices where the tree now has 53 — and it therefore cannot answer a single one of the DSDT-diffing questions P3's second clause asks. And its population is the other display arm: it carries `DisplayDxe` (270,558 B), `CPRDxe` and `DisplayReEnablerDxe`, with no `SimpleFbDxe`, while the volume the build tree produces today carries `SimpleFbDxe` and none of the three. The `USE_CUSTOM_DISPLAY_DRIVER` setting that separates the two arms is the one tracked line (docs/07:154), and `p3-display` was built from the `=1` volume at 03:37 on the day the ASL was still at 4.215's shape. That build is what docs/07 recorded at Step 4.74 as "the `=1` build, which contains `DisplayDxe`, was built and" — so the file is internally consistent and simply old.

**What was built, and the one command that was wrong.** Re-running the build regenerated the volume in 26 s and produced a correct `FVMAIN` — 126 FFS files, `DSDT 13,422 B sha256 97ef598131595a2d`, `SimpleFbDxe` present, `XhciDxe`/`UsbBusDxe`/`UsbDeviceDxe`/`UsbMassStorageDxe` present — and then died in `build_uefi.py`'s own final step with `ValueError: DTB image must not be empty` from `Resources/Scripts/mkbootimg.py:256`. **That traceback is not the fixable kind and the command is recorded so it is not repeated.** `gauguin.toml` sets `append_dtb = false`, which is *correct for this device* and is documented there at length (at header_version 2 the tree is a region of its own; gluing it into the kernel leaves `dtb_size` 0 and ABL's `GetSocDtb()` returns NULL), but `build_uefi.py`'s `argument_map` then always passes `image_config.get("dtb")`, and `gauguin.toml` has no `[boot_image]` `dtb` key — so `--dtb None` reaches `mkbootimg.py`, which raises. `./build_uefi.py -d gauguin -r DEBUG -c` therefore **cannot complete**: it produces the `SILICIUM_UEFI.fd` and then fails, and the payload must be wrapped by `tools/build-p2-payloads.sh` / `tools/make_boot_image.py --profile stock`, which is what built the payload of record all along. The failing command destroyed nothing (`mkbootimg.py` writes the output file after `write_header`, so no truncated image was left), and the build tree's `SILICIUM_UEFI.fd` is now current.

**The fresh payload set, and where it is.** `P2DIR=work/out/p3-covered tools/build-p2-payloads.sh` ran to exit 0 and wrote three images, all three passing `check-payload.py`, the replayed ABL path, and the GenFv map cross-check at **126 offsets and GUIDs, zero mismatches**: `Mu-gauguin-stock-gzip.img` 1,183,744 B, `Mu-gauguin-stock-none.img` 3,248,128 B and `Mu-gauguin-silicon-gzip.img` 1,173,504 B, each carrying `DSDT 13,422 bytes` at offset `0x5788d8` — the current table, at a different offset than the stale candidate's `0x5c9220` because the volume is 1,228 bytes larger, which is itself the independent confirmation that the table is where the volume says it is. The superseded candidate set was **preserved rather than replaced**, at `/tmp/p3-display-stale-3873956/` (3 files, copied before the new build ran) — `work/out/p3-display/` was not written, both because it is one of the four protected directories this project does not overwrite and because the rule it protects is the one the stale file demonstrates: *the payload on the phone is the control*. Nothing in the repository was modified by any of this; `git status` is clean apart from this entry.

**decides**: that the P3 candidate `work/out/p3-display/Mu-gauguin-silicon-gzip.img` was built from a stale build tree whose `DSDT` is 12,341 bytes `sha256 0f5df26b424ab609`, identical to that of commits `a6f35f7` (Step 4.215) and `3873956` (Step 4.94) and to no ASL written after them, so it lacks `SDC1`, `SDC2`, `WPSS`, `CAMP`, `JPGE`, `VFE0`, `CSID`, `CSI1` and `CSI2` (44 top-level devices where the tree has 53); that `./build_uefi.py -d gauguin -r DEBUG -c` **cannot complete** because `gauguin.toml`'s correct `append_dtb = false` plus `build_uefi.py`'s unconditional `--dtb` pass-through gives `mkbootimg.py` an empty DTB and a `ValueError`, and that this is by design in `gauguin.toml`'s own comment rather than a defect to patch (`build_uefi.py` never passes `--pagesize`, so every image it makes is page 2048 where this device is 0x1000, and it cannot declare a DTB region at all) — the payload wrapper is `tools/build-p2-payloads.sh`; and that the superseded set is preserved at `/tmp/p3-display-stale-3873956/` rather than deleted or overwritten. **does not decide**: which of the three fresh images should be flashed, `silicon-gzip` having been the previous candidate for reasons this step did not re-examine; whether the `=1` display arm is wanted for the gate at all, since a desktop-over-GOP is what the gate's second clause is checked on and `SimpleFbDxe` is the arm docs/07 argues for, but the `p3-display` name says someone intended the other;
