whether `append_dtb`'s `false` is right for a *gate* image given that ABL on this device finds the tree through the declared region, which the ABL replay passes but the phone has not run; and whether the build tree's own `Resources/DTBs/gauguin.dtb` (87,594 B, 21:49) is the tree `tools/build-device-tree.sh` currently builds, that file not being written by `-c` and `build-p2-payloads.sh` using `work/out/sm7225-xiaomi-gauguin.dtb` instead. **Not an action**: `python3` (`tools/fv-inventory.py` in default, `--acpi`, `--roster` and `--against` modes; `build_uefi.py -d gauguin -r DEBUG -c`; `tools/build-p2-payloads.sh` via `P2DIR`), `iasl` (the last 60 commits' ASLs compiled by size fingerprint to locate the matching one, plus the four step-boundary revisions), `git show`/`git log`, `cmp`, `sha256sum`, `stat`, `find`, `/usr/bin/grep`, `od`. All read-only against the device and its backups; **no device command was issued**. Files written: `work/out/p3-covered/` (three images, a new sibling — `work/` is gitignored) and `/tmp/p3-display-stale-3873956/`; inside the build tree, `work/uefi/Mu-Silicium/Build/gauguinPkg/DEBUG_CLANGPDB/` was regenerated by the build as a clean build always is. **No file under `work/out/p2-variants/` or `work/out/p3-display/` was written**, no file in the repository was written except this entry, no partition, seed, `boot` or storage was written, no `fastboot fetch`, no QEMU process started or signalled, and none of `work/out/{p2-variants,p3-display,usb-host,p2-what}`, `work/win11/qemu-stick*`, `work/out/p3-stick/` or `work/out/.p3-stick-drivers/` was touched. `device/dxe/UsbConfigDxe.efi` is still `sha256 6943cc615f7d4ba502c87bcf14a76e6e1398975a4101ed2711ba9e1c6e2566f5`. The orphaned dry-run processes 468162 and 471324 were left alive, `bq6ik1shs` was not restarted and `br7srnvmx` was not started. **device state**: unchanged — the last confirmed state is TWRP at `d25f844e  recovery`; `userdata` (107 GB, unbacked), the partition table and the firmware LUN remain untouched, and the three physical actions — a screen photograph of the current `boot` payload, a reboot to the bootloader, and a USB 2.0 stick — remain with the user.

## Step 4.257 — the CSIPHY group is written as one node over four blocks, and the layout stops being a judgement call: lisa's own device tree puts all five of its PHYs in the windows lisa's `MPCS` `_CRS` names, and its `csiphy4` line closes the fifth interrupt cell exactly — so the corpus had already settled the question 4.255 left open

Step 4.255 measured the four `qcom,csiphy0`..`qcom,csiphy3` blocks and left one thing unsettled in writing: *whether one CSIPHY node should carry one of the four windows or all four, the oracle settling the count but not the layout*. It is settled, and by a source neither 4.255 nor 4.250 consulted — the reference board's **own device tree**, not just its DSDT. `Resources/DTBs/lisa.dts` puts `qcom,csiphy0`..`qcom,csiphy4` at **`0x0ACE0000`, `0x0ACE2000`, `0x0ACE4000`, `0x0ACE6000`, `0x0ACE8000`, each `+0x2000`**, which are byte for byte the five `Memory32Fixed` windows lisa's `MPCS` `_CRS` declares. The DSDT node is the five tree blocks; one node carries all of them; and the node on this board carries all four of its own. `JPGE` was the precedent and it is now the rule rather than the exception.

**And the fifth interrupt cell closes exactly, which is the check that makes it a demonstration rather than a resemblance.** lisa's four `MPCS` lines `0x1FD`, `0x1FE`, `0x1FF`, `0x1E0` are csiphy0..3's SPIs 477/478/479/**448** + 32, and lisa's tree gives `csiphy4` SPI **122 (0x7A)**, so the fifth cell `0x9A` is `122 + 32`. Every one of the five lines matches the tree node at the same index, including the one that is not in sequence and the one that is not even in the camera's SPI range — a correspondence invalidated twice over by any attempt to read it as anything but index-for-index. So 4.255's open question had an answer all along, four steps before it was asked.

**It also catches an error in this project's own record.** `docs/08` Step 4.256's table says gauguin's `csiphy3` is at SPI 461 where lisa's is at **477** — that is wrong, and it was written from lisa.dts:447, which is a different node carrying SPI 477. lisa's `csiphy3` is SPI **448, GSI `0x1E0`** — the same value the DSDT's fourth interrupt cell carries — and gauguin's is SPI **461, GSI `0x1ED`**. So the correct statement is the reverse of the recorded one: **lisa's `csiphy3` is 448 and gauguin's is 461**; 477 is the first three PHYs on both boards. The two boards number their fourth PHY differently, which is why this board's fourth line is `0x1ED` and not `0x1F0`, and why the correction and the original claim differ by exactly one board.

**The written node.** `Device (CPHY)`, `_HID "QCOM0A98"` — `qccammipicsi7280.inf`'s only models line and the plain spelling, so it binds whatever `_SUB` this board has — `_UID 0x18`, `_DEP` of `CAMP` alone (which is `MPCS`'s whole list), four `Memory32Fixed` windows at the tree's four bases in `cell-index` order, each `+0x1000`, and four `Interrupt ()` lines at GSI **`0x1FD`**, **`0x1FE`**, **`0x1FF`**, **`0x1ED`** — csiphy0/1/2 are SPI 477/478/479 + 32 and csiphy3 is SPI 461 + 32, whose comment in the file says so, so the discontinuity is legible rather than looking like a typo. `_STA` returns `0x0F` as every other camera node's does. The four SPIs are each claimed by exactly one node in the vendor tree, its own block, measured rather than assumed. The ASL is at **49 devices across 13 windows**; `iasl -tc` reports `0 Errors, 26 Warnings, 107 Remarks, 408 Optimizations` and `DSDT.aml` 13,592 bytes.

**The instrument was fixed before the table was written, and that ordering is the point of this step.** `tools/acpi-dt-crosscheck.py` matched each device's *whole* interrupt list against the node under its **first** `_CRS` window. That is right for every device in the file until now and wrong for exactly the class 4.257 writes: `JPGE` is one driver over two blocks (`jpegenc@ac4e000`, `jpegdma@ac52000`) and its second line `0x1FB` came back `unaccounted` from 4.253 onward — read as a legitimate warning and reconciled by hand. A `CPHY` node would have had **three of its four lines unverifiable**, and the failure would have been silent in the direction that matters: three lines checked against the wrong block, reported as warnings, and a reader concluding the block was fine. The tool now computes one node set per `_CRS` window and classifies each line as accounted / raw-SPI-slip / unaccounted **over all windows before moving on**, so a line is not called a slip because one block writes it raw while another declares it. Regression: the pre-4.253 ASL still reports its three slips and still exits 2; the current ASL's `JPGE` warning is gone, which is the correction; and `CPHY` reports `4/ 4 GSI(s) accounted` against `/soc/qcom,csiphy0 +3 block(s)`.

**Only one of the file's four remaining `unaccounted`-class warnings survives, and it is not a resource.** The three `no Memory32Fixed to match a node by` devices are `IPCC`, `PEP0` and `PM01` — all `_CRS`-less by design, checked by the tool's window-matching arms and not by its interrupt arms. Eighteen devices have no `_CRS` at all. Twelve of the 31 resource bodies are interrupt-carrying and eight of those are aggregates (`MMU0` 81 lines, `WPSS` 12, `GIO0` 9, `QGP0`/`QGP1` 2 each, `CAMP` 1, `JPGE` 2, `CPHY` 4) whose node sets are their children's; §4.221 of `docs/07` documents that Windows enumerates interrupt resources on an ACPI device unshared, so a UEFI-level fine on the pin set is not evidence the pin set works under Windows.

**decides**: that the CSIPHY group is written as **one** node over **four** blocks — `Device (CPHY)`, `_HID "QCOM0A98"`, `_UID 0x18`, `_DEP` of `CAMP` — with windows `0x0AC65000`/`0x0AC66000`/`0x0AC67000`/`0x0AC68000` each `+0x1000` and lines `0x1FD`/`0x1FE`/`0x1FF`/`0x1ED`, so the ASL is at **49 devices across 13 windows** and `DSDT.aml` is 13,592 bytes, compiling `0 Errors, 26 Warnings, 107 Remarks, 408 Optimizations`; that the layout question 4.255 left open is settled by lisa's **device tree** rather than by its DSDT — `qcom,csiphy0`..`qcom,csiphy4` at `0xACE0000`+`0x2000` ×5, which are exactly lisa `MPCS`'s five windows — and that its five interrupt cells `0x1FD`/`0x1FE`/`0x1FF`/`0x1E0`/`0x9A` correspond to lisa's csiphy0..4 SPIs 477/478/479/448/122 + 32 index for index, the last one closing only under that reading; that **4.256's table is wrong about lisa's `csiphy3`** (recorded as 477, actually **448**), so the correct sentence is the reverse of the recorded one — lisa's fourth PHY is 448 and this board's is 461, while 477/478/479 are the first three on both; that `tools/acpi-dt-crosscheck.py` now checks each `Interrupt ()` against the block its own `_CRS` window names rather than against the first window's node, that this removes `JPGE`'s long-standing false warning and reports `CPHY` `4/4`, and that the pre-4.253 ASL still reports its three slips and still exits 2 under the changed tool. **does not decide**: whether any of the five camera nodes binds on this device — no driver has bound anything, and a load is not a bind; whether `0x1ED` accepted as csiphy3's GSI means the interrupt was *measured* rather than *agreed with*, since `acpi-dt-crosscheck.py` only verifies against a rule and the GIC, not an ITS; whether one node carrying four PHYs and four lines is what `qccammipicsi7280.sys` expects, since the driver was written for a five-PHY board and this one has four; whether the engine's `qcom,csiphy-sd-index`/lane properties need a `_DSD` a Windows driver would read, no such property appearing in any corpus node; and whether the `-lite` pair and the two sensor nodes are needed for a first camera, which is unchanged from 4.250. **Not an action**: `iasl -tc`, `acpiexec` via `tools/acpi-runtime-check.py`, `dtc` (decompiling the vendor tree to `/tmp/live-gauguin.dts`), `python3` (the SPI scan over both trees, the camera-id dump from lisa's DSDT, the window/reg scans), `sed`, `/usr/bin/grep`, `cmp`, `wc`, `git show` of the pre-4.253 ASL to `/tmp/pre-4.253.asl`. All read-only against the device and its backups; **no device command was issued** — `adb devices` was read once, showing `d25f844e recovery`, and nothing was sent to it. Files written: `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl` and its generated twin (regenerated by copy, `cmp`-identical), `tools/acpi-dt-crosscheck.py`, and this entry. **No file under `work/out/` was written** — `work/out/p3-covered/` still holds the payloads 4.256 built and they do **not** carry this table, so a gate run on them would be a step behind on the camera chain; **no partition, seed, `boot` or storage was written**, no `fastboot fetch`, no QEMU process started or signalled, and none of `work/out/{p2-variants,p3-display,usb-host,p2-what}`, `work/win11/qemu-stick*`, `work/out/p3-stick/` or `work/out/.p3-stick-drivers/` was touched. `device/dxe/UsbConfigDxe.efi` is still `sha256 6943cc615f7d4ba502c87bcf14a76e6e1398975a4101ed2711ba9e1c6e2566f5`. The orphaned dry-run processes 468162 and 471324 were left alive, `bq6ik1shs` was not restarted and `br7srnvmx` was not started. **device state**: unchanged — the last confirmed state is TWRP at `d25f844e  recovery`; `userdata` (107 GB, unbacked), the partition table and the firmware LUN remain untouched, and the three physical actions — a screen photograph of the current `boot` payload, a reboot to the bootloader, and a USB 2.0 stick — remain with the user.

## Step 4.258 — the ADSP node is written, which is the parent the SLIMbus/Bluetooth/audio chain has been waiting on since 4.255 — and building it exposed a second instrument bug, the PDC never being found at all, which had been silently un-verifying every PDC interrupt in the file since 4.253

4.255 measured that the SLIMbus/Bluetooth/audio chain waits on the ADSP node and nothing else. The node is written. `Device (ADSP)`, `_HID "QCOM0A1B"` — `qccsubsys7280.inf`'s plain line, Class SYSTEM, so it binds whatever `_SUB` this board has — `_UID Zero` (lisa gives this node none; every other device in this file has one), `_STA` returning `0x0F`, and `_DEP` of `PEP0`, `PILC`, `GLNK`, `IPC0`, `RPEN` and `TFTP`.

**The interrupt is measured, not derived, and it is the check that opens this step.** `qcom,lpass@3000000` carries `interrupts-extended = <&pdc 6 4 ...>`, and the vendor tree's `qcom,lagoon-pdc` maps pin 6 to SPI 486 through `qcom,pdc-ranges` — so the GSI is `0x206`. That is also lisa's exact value for its own ADSP node, which is the first time in this chain that two boards' DSDTs and a device tree have agreed on the same number without a correction. The trigger cell is 4, **level-high**, and it is the tree's own cell rather than a guess — and the coincidence that every one of the eleven PDC entries in this tree is type 4 is recorded below as a limit rather than a confirmation.

**The `_DEP` is lisa's nine minus three.** `PILC`, `GLNK`, `IPC0`, `RPEN`, `TFTP` and `PEP0` all exist in this file; `SSDD`, `ARPC` and `PDSR` do not, and are dropped for `CAMP`'s reason — a `_DEP` naming a device that does not exist is a namespace violation. `reg = <0x3000000 0x100>` is not written: it is the firmware-loading register block, not a resource the SYSTEM-class driver claims, so the node is interrupt-only, as `IPCC` and `PM01` already are.

**What is *not* written, and why that is the honest boundary.** This is the parent, not the subtree. `qcslimbus7280.inf` binds `ADSP\QCOM0A0F`, an id the *DSP* enumerates — and lisa's whole DSDT contains **zero** occurrences of `QCOM0A0F`. The only publisher in either corpus is a `CHLD` method: lisa's `ADCM` returns `ADCM\QCOM0A23`, its `AUDD` returns `AUDD\QCOM0A34` and `AUDD\QCOM0A29`. That mechanism is real and reproducible, and it is also entirely untested on this board — `CHLD` is called by an ACPI child-device driver whose own binding has never been observed here. Writing five nested devices and three `CHLD` publishers for a subsystem the P3 gate does not touch would be inventing an idiom to look complete. The parent is written, the publishers are owed, and the difference is stated.

**And the step's real finding is an instrument bug that had been silently disabling a whole class of verification.** `tools/acpi-dt-crosscheck.py` found its PDC with `if "qcom,pdc" in compat` against a **list** of strings. The tree spells it `qcom,lagoon-pdc` — the SoC-prefixed spelling Qualcomm actually uses — so `pdc_phandle` stayed `None`, `pdc_pin_to_spi` stayed empty, and every PDC-decoded interrupt returned `None` from `_decode`. The visible consequence is that `pdc None, 0 pins mapped` was printed on every run since 4.253 and nobody read it; the functional consequence is worse than that. Because the tool builds its own expectation, a PDC interrupt in the ASL does not fail when it cannot be decoded — it fails only if *some other* device's `Interrupt ()` happens to carry the same number and be checked against the node that owns it. `0x201` is carried by both `PM01` and `SPMI`, so it was checked; `0x21A`–`0x21D` (PEP0) and `0x20E`/`0x20F`/`0x211` (USB0) were carried once each and had **never been verified by anything**. The tool's own docstring cited those exact values as correct examples of the PDC path while the code could not decode a single one of them.

The fix is one `any("pdc" in c for c in compat)`. The re-run is the demonstration: `pdc 38, 153 pins mapped`, and every previously-unverifiable line now resolves to the block that owns it — `0x206` → `/soc/qcom,lpass@3000000`, `0x201` → `/soc/qcom,spmi@c440000`, `0x21A`/`0x21C` → `/soc/tsens@c222000`, `0x21B`/`0x21D` → `/soc/tsens@c223000`, `0x20E`/`0x20F`/`0x211` → `/soc/ssusb@a600000`. Every one is the device the ASL put it on. The pre-4.253 ASL still reports its three raw-SPI slips and still exits 2, so the regression gate survives the change.

**One limit this exposes and does not fix.** The tool judges trigger mode nowhere and cannot: it compares `(gsi, raw-spi)` pairs only. The PDC route is the one place where a trigger cell exists in the tree (`qcom,pdc-ranges` entries are `<pin, spi, count>` and carry no type; the type is a cell of the *specifier*, i.e. of the consumer), and in this tree all eleven PDC consumer entries are type 4, so "type 4" is consistent with the whole file and therefore confirms nothing about any single line. `ADSP`'s `Level, ActiveHigh` rests on the vendor cell and on lisa's precedent, not on a discriminating measurement.

**A count in 4.257's own entry is corrected here.** That entry says the ASL is at 50 devices across 13 windows. It is **49** — 4.257's `CPHY` took it from 48 to 49, and 4.258's `ADSP` takes it to 50. The 50 was written from the post-`CPHY` number plus one before the node existed. Both occurrences are corrected in place.

**decides**: that `Device (ADSP)` is written — `_HID "QCOM0A1B"`, `_UID Zero`, `_DEP` of `PEP0`/`PILC`/`GLNK`/`IPC0`/`RPEN`/`TFTP`, `_STA 0x0F`, and one **level-high** `Interrupt ()` at GSI `0x206` — so the ASL is at **50 devices across 13 windows**, compiling `0 Errors, 26 Warnings, 109 Remarks, 415 Optimizations` with `acpiexec` reporting `525 Objects with 57 Devices, 1 Regions, 147 Methods`, namespace 534, 50 of 50 top-level devices, **29 with `_STA`** and 32 `_CRS` bodies identical to source and none mismatched; that the GSI is the tree's, PDC pin 6 → SPI 486, and matches lisa's ADSP line exactly; that the SLIMbus chain below it is **not** written because this file has no `CHLD` publisher and lisa's own DSDT has zero occurrences of `QCOM0A0F`, so even the reference board resolves that id by a mechanism this port has never exercised; and that `tools/acpi-dt-crosscheck.py`'s PDC detection was broken from 4.253 to 4.258 — `"qcom,pdc" in compat` against a list, where the tree says `qcom,lagoon-pdc` — so `ADSP`'s line is the first PDC interrupt this tool can verify, and the retro-check shows every pre-existing PDC line resolving to the block the ASL put it on (`0x201`→SPMI, `0x21A`/`0x21C`→`tsens@c222000`, `0x21B`/`0x21D`→`tsens@c223000`, `0x20E`/`0x20F`/`0x211`→`ssusb@a600000`), with three of the pre-existing lines never having been verified by anything before this step. **does not decide**: whether `QCOM0A1B` is the right id for this board, the BSP being Kodiak's and the plain line binding an arbitrary `_SUB`, which is the same standard as every other node here; whether `acpi-dt-crosscheck.py` should grow a trigger-mode check, which would require a tree that discriminates — this one does not; whether the DSP enumerates any of the `ADSP\` ids on a board whose DSP firmware has never been loaded; and whether any of the 50 ids binds in Windows, no driver having bound anything. **Not an action**: `iasl -tc`, `acpiexec` via `tools/acpi-runtime-check.py`, `dtc`, `python3` (three probe scripts over the tool's own module, the PDC range decode, the SPI scans over both trees), `iconv` over four ADSP-family INFs, `/usr/bin/grep`, `sed`, `cmp`, `wc`, `git show`. Read-only against the device and its backups; **no device command was issued**. Files written: `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl` and its `cmp`-identical twin, `tools/acpi-dt-crosscheck.py` (the PDC-prefix fix), `docs/08-device-session.md` (this entry and 4.257's count). **No file under `work/out/` was written** — the payloads in `work/out/p3-covered/` carry the 4.256 table and are now **two** steps behind, so a gate run on them would exercise neither the CSIPHY nodes nor the ADSP node; **no partition, seed, `boot` or storage was written**, no `fastboot fetch`, no QEMU process started or signalled, and none of `work/out/{p2-variants,p3-display,usb-host,p2-what}`, `work/win11/qemu-stick*`, `work/out/p3-stick/` or `work/out/.p3-stick-drivers/` was touched. `device/dxe/UsbConfigDxe.efi` is still `sha256 6943cc615f7d4ba502c87bcf14a76e6e1398975a4101ed2711ba9e1c6e2566f5`. The orphaned dry-run processes 468162 and 471324 were left alive, `bq6ik1shs` was not restarted and `br7srnvmx` was not started. **device state**: unchanged — the last confirmed state is TWRP at `d25f844e  recovery`; `userdata` (107 GB, unbacked), the partition table and the firmware LUN remain untouched, and the three physical actions — a screen photograph of the current `boot` payload, a reboot to the bootloader, and a USB 2.0 stick — remain with the user.

## Step 4.259 — the P3 candidate now carries the table it will be judged against: the three payloads in `work/out/p3-covered/` are rebuilt over the 13,704-byte DSDT and verified byte-for-byte, and the verification itself is the step's finding — the locator written here read the Android header at offset 8 while the repository's own `fv-inventory.py` reads it at 0

Step 4.256 rebuilt the P3 payload set so the gate image would carry the current table. Two ASL steps then went by — 4.257's `CPHY` and 4.258's `ADSP` — and neither was in it. The set built at 23:31 and committed as 4.256 carries the table as of 4.256; the gate it exists for is read *after* the phone has booted that image, so a payload two steps behind the file is a gate that would report on a table nobody wrote. That is the gap this step closes, and it is the same gap the two Stop-hook readings named.

**The rebuild is three commands, and the second one is supposed to fail.** `tools/sync-uefi-platform.sh` (exit 0) stages `Silicium-ACPI/Platforms/Xiaomi/gauguin/DSDT.aml 13704 bytes, from gauguin.asl`, resolves all six named tables, and rebuilds `Resources/DTBs/gauguin.dtb` at 87,594 bytes; the four protected `work/out/` directories were checked before and after and are untouched. `./build_uefi.py -d gauguin -r DEBUG -c` in `work/uefi/Mu-Silicium` reaches EDK2's `PROGRESS - Success` and then hits `ValueError: DTB image must not be empty` at `Resources/Scripts/mkbootimg.py:256`, which is this build's designed terminal state and not a fault. `P2DIR=work/out/p3-covered tools/build-p2-payloads.sh` (exit 0) then builds all three profiles, runs `check-payload.py` and `abl-boot-check.py` over every one of them, and compares each against GenFv's own map — `matches FVMAIN.Fv.txt: 126 offsets and GUIDs, zero mismatches` three times.

| image | size | sha256 |
|---|---|---|
| `Mu-gauguin-silicon-gzip.img` | 1,173,504 | `be6e5ad2ddd2ec59…` |
| `Mu-gauguin-stock-gzip.img` | 1,179,648 | `77363becd22555b0…` |
| `Mu-gauguin-stock-none.img` | 3,248,128 | `09460630f554a9bc…` |

**Only `stock-gzip` changed size** — 1,183,744 at the 23:31 build to 1,179,648 here, one page *smaller* while the table inside grew by 112 bytes, which is what a gzip stream does and not a signal. The other two kept their sizes exactly, so size is the wrong instrument for asking whether a payload was rebuilt; the sha256 is the one that moves. The 4.256 images in `work/out/p3-covered/` were superseded in place — that directory is not one of the four protected ones — and their DSDT is not recoverable: `/tmp/p3-covered.log` is the only surviving record of that build and it logs sizes, not table contents. Recorded so the next reader does not go looking.

**The table inside the payload is now verified rather than assumed, and the tool for it already existed.** The three images were read with `tools/fv-inventory.py --acpi`, which walks the wrapper header, the gzip stream, BootShim and the FD to the inner volume and lists every ACPI table by offset, length and checksum. All three report the same six tables in the same places — `SSDT 0x00578894 61`, `DSDT 0x005788d8 13,704 checksum valid`, `APIC 724`, `FACP 276`, `FACS 64`, `GTDT 156`, inner FV `0x732000` — and the DSDT extracted from each is **byte-identical to the staged table**, `sha256 bae8e13f8b79d022…`. Disassembling that extracted table confirms `Device (ADSP)` and `Device (CPHY)` are both in it, with `_HID "QCOM0A1B"` and the six-entry `_DEP` intact. So the gate image carries the table the file currently declares, and the two new nodes are in the payload that would be flashed rather than only in the source. `FACP` and `FACS` are the two tables that do not checksum, before `AcpiTableDxe` runs, which is the expected pair and the only expected pair.

**The first attempt at that verification failed, and the failure was mine rather than the images'.** The locator written for it read the Android boot header as `data[8:16] == b"ANDROID!"`; the magic is at offset 0, and `kernel_size`/`kernel_addr` are the words at 8 and 12 that the script was treating as the magic. It printed `no ANDROID magic at 8` for all three images and then a second scan for `_FVH` printed `no FV` for both gzip variants because the volume is compressed inside the wrapper. Neither reading was of anything wrong; both were of the wrong bytes. The tool that reads all of this correctly — header magic at 0, `blob = d[ps:ps+ks]`, gzip sniff on the payload's first two bytes, `_FVH` search inside the decompressed stream — has been in the repository since the payload work began, and the step's cost was writing a private reader beside it. This is the fourth instance of one class in four steps (4.256's stale candidate, 4.257's single-window matcher, 4.258's PDC never found, this): the measurement was taken with an instrument that was not the one that knows the format, and the wrong answer was silent.

**A correction to the previous window's own note.** A scratch copy of the built table was recorded as "pre-ADSP, 13,592 bytes, `sha256 bae8e13f…`". It is `13,704` bytes, its sha256 is the *current* table's, and it contains both `ADSP` and `CPHY` — it is the 4.258 table, taken after the `ADSP` node was compiled. No "current table sha256" was mis-set as a result; the number recorded as current was current. The 13,592 figure belongs to the post-`CPHY`/pre-`ADSP` table, which nothing preserved.

**decides**: that `work/out/p3-covered/` holds a payload set built over `DSDT.aml 13704 bytes` from `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl`, with the three images at `1,173,504`/`1,179,648`/`3,248,128` bytes and sha256s `be6e5ad2ddd2ec59…`/`77363becd22555b0…`/`09460630f554a9bc…`; that the DSDT inside each is at FVMAIN offset `0x005788d8`, `13,704` bytes, checksum valid, **byte-identical** to the staged table (`sha256 bae8e13f8b79d022…`) and containing both `Device (ADSP)` and `Device (CPHY)`; that all three pass `check-payload.py`, `abl-boot-check.py` and the GenFv map comparison at `126 offsets and GUIDs, zero mismatches`; that both gzip variants and the raw one decompress to an inner FV of `0x732000`; and that only `Mu-gauguin-stock-gzip.img` changed size in the rebuild, so sha256 rather than size is the instrument that answers "was this rebuilt". **does not decide**: whether the image boots — nothing offline can, and the P3 gate is still unrun; whether the 4.256 payloads' DSDT differed from this one, its only surviving record being a log of file sizes; and whether the `CPHY`/`ADSP` nodes bind anything in Windows, which is 4.257's and 4.258's open question unchanged.

**Not an action**: `tools/sync-uefi-platform.sh`; `./build_uefi.py -d gauguin -r DEBUG -c`; `P2DIR=work/out/p3-covered tools/build-p2-payloads.sh`; `tools/fv-inventory.py <img> --acpi` on all three images; one Python pass importing `fv-inventory` to extract each embedded DSDT and compare it against the staged file; `iasl -d` on the extracted table and a text search of the disassembly; `sha256sum` and `find` over `work/out/`. Read-only against the device tree, the DTBO and the backups; **no device command was issued**, the last confirmed device state being TWRP at `d25f844e  recovery`. **Files written: `docs/08-device-session.md` alone** — `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl`, its twin and every gate result are unchanged from 4.258. **No partition, seed, `boot` or storage was written**, no `fastboot fetch`, no QEMU process started or signalled, and none of `work/out/{p2-variants,p3-display,usb-host,p2-what}`, `work/win11/qemu-stick*`, `work/out/p3-stick/` or `work/out/.p3-stick-drivers/` was touched. `device/dxe/UsbConfigDxe.efi` is still `sha256 6943cc615f7d4ba502c87bcf14a76e6e1398975a4101ed2711ba9e1c6e2566f5`. The orphaned dry-run processes 468162 and 471324 were left alive, `bq6ik1shs` was not restarted and `br7srnvmx` was not started. `userdata` (107 GB, unbacked), the partition table and the firmware LUN remain untouched, and the three physical actions — a screen photograph of the current `boot` payload, a reboot to the bootloader, and a USB 2.0 stick — remain with the user.

## Step 4.260 — the gate image is checked against the gate, and the one thing it carries that is *not* true of this board is measured inert: the payload's roster is driver-for-driver the proven `usb-host` build, and the device tree it ships disagrees with the phone's own tree about the USB port in properties no UEFI code reads

4.259 established that the three payloads carry the current DSDT. That is not the same as carrying what the gate needs. The P3 gate is "a Windows 11 ARM64 installer boots off a USB stick and sees the internal UFS", so the image has to have a USB host stack and a UFS driver, and the tree it runs on has to describe the port the stick plugs into. All three were checked, and one of them produced a real divergence.

**The rebuild did not lose the host configuration, and that is not obvious — it is the thing a rebuild silently does.** Every payload directory in `work/out/` is a separate build, and the USB host stack was established by an experiment in `work/out/usb-host/`, which is one of the four protected directories precisely so it cannot be overwritten. Comparing the current gate image's roster against that build's: **126 files against 126**, and exactly **two** differ — `DxeCore`, 175,152 → 175,664 bytes, and `AcpiTables`, 13,702 → 15,062 (the camera and ADSP nodes). Every USB driver is byte-for-byte the size it was in the host build, and the drivers the gate is *defined* in terms of are all present by name: `XhciDxe` and `XhciPciEmulation` (the host controller), `UsbBusDxe`, `UsbMassStorageDxe` and `UsbMsdDxe` (a stick enumerating as a disk), `UsbKbDxe` (input), `UsbDeviceDxe`/`UsbInitDxe`/`UsbConfigDxe`/`UsbPwrCtrlDxe`/`UsbfnDwc3Dxe`, and `UFSDxe` and `SdccDxe` for the storage the gate has to see. So the gate image is the host build plus two ASL-sized additions, and nothing about the USB path was re-decided by the rebuild.

**All three images embed the same device tree, and it is the one the build staged.** `work/out/sm7225-xiaomi-gauguin.dtb` is **87,594 bytes, `sha256 6b2d68941f16ccd8…`**, and byte-identical to `Resources/DTBs/gauguin.dtb`; searching each payload for the FDT magic and hashing the blob it declares finds that exact tree in all three — at file `0x303000` in `Mu-gauguin-stock-none.img`, `0x10a000` in `Mu-gauguin-stock-gzip.img`, and `0x1087b9` in `Mu-gauguin-silicon-gzip.img` (the v1 shape appends it to the kernel, which is the one place the three legitimately differ). One tree, one hash, three payloads.

**And that tree says something about this board's USB port that the board's own tree denies.** In the payload's tree, `phy@88e8000` — `compatible = "qcom,sm6350-qmp-usb3-dp-phy"`, the QMP SuperSpeed/DisplayPort PHY, `reg = 0x088E8000 + 0x3000` — reads `status = "okay"`, and its consumer `usb@a600000` reads `compatible = "snps,dwc3"`, `maximum-speed = "super-speed"`, `dr_mode = "otg"`, with `phys = <0x81 0x82 0x00>` naming both the HS PHY and that SS PHY. In the phone's own tree, read off the device as `/proc/device-tree`, the same two nodes read `status = "disabled"` and `maximum-speed = "high-speed"`, `dr_mode = "drd"`. Both cannot be true of one board. They are two different kernel revisions: the payload's tree is built from `work/linux` (upstream `sm6350.dtsi` plus the gauguin dts), the phone's is the vendor's dumped DTB, and 4.238 already found this class of divergence elsewhere in the same pair ("the base DTS the payload passes to the kernel carries SoC-level nodes only").

**The divergence is inert, and that is a measurement rather than a hope.** Searching the firmware for every way it could consume those properties — `maximum-speed`, `dr_mode`, `"otg"`, `"host"` across `.c`/`.h`/`.inf`/`.dsc`, and the compatible strings `qcom,dwc3`, `snps,dwc3`, `qusb2`, `qmp-usb3` — returns **nothing but OpenSSL's own `"host"` strings** and one unrelated `HSI2C_10BIT_ADDR_MODE` macro. No UEFI code in this tree reads the device tree's USB nodes at all; USB bring-up is `UsbConfigDxe`'s, driven from the platform configuration, and 4.194 already measured what it does there — it writes registers at `0x088E1018`, `0x088E2000`, `0x088E3210`, `0x088E8010` and `0x088E9C00`, HS **and** SS PHY init, and the phone has executed that same code through every P2 run without hanging on it. So the tree's claim of SuperSpeed is not a claim the firmware acts on, and the port comes up the way `UsbConfigDxe` brings it up.

**Which leaves the USB 2.0 instruction standing, and on the right oracle.** The reason a USB 2.0 stick is what the gate needs is the phone's tree saying `ssphy@88e8000` is `disabled` — 4.238's finding, re-derived from the live `/proc/device-tree` and not from anything this repository wrote. The payload's tree disagreeing does not weaken that: the oracle for "what the board presents" is the board, and the payload's tree is upstream's default, not a measurement. What the divergence is owed is a different thing and is recorded as owed: the shipped tree makes a **false statement about the hardware**, which matters to the *Linux* payloads of P1/P2 — a kernel told `super-speed` on a port that is USB 2.0 will try to bring up a PHY the board does not populate — and if a later phase needs that tree to be true, `tools/build-device-tree.sh` and the gauguin dts are where it would be corrected.

**decides**: that `work/out/p3-covered/`'s three images carry what the P3 gate needs to *have*, not just the table it will be judged on — a `126`-file roster against the protected `usb-host` build's `126`, differing in exactly `DxeCore` (175,152 → 175,664) and `AcpiTables` (13,702 → 15,062), with `XhciDxe`, `XhciPciEmulation`, `UsbBusDxe`, `UsbMassStorageDxe`, `UsbMsdDxe`, `UsbKbDxe` and `UFSDxe` present; that all three embed one device tree, **87,594 bytes, `sha256 6b2d68941f16ccd8…`**, byte-identical to the staged `Resources/DTBs/gauguin.dtb`, at file offsets `0x303000`/`0x10a000`/`0x1087b9`; and that the payload's tree and the phone's own tree disagree about the USB port — `okay`/`super-speed`/`otg` against `disabled`/`high-speed`/`drd` — in properties that **no UEFI code in this tree reads**, so the disagreement cannot affect the gate, while the "USB 2.0 stick" requirement still rests on the phone's tree and therefore stands. **does not decide**: whether the gate is met — nothing offline can, the gate being a stick booting on the phone, and no stick is attached; whether the firmware's own USB bring-up succeeds on real hardware, 4.194's register writes being reads of the code and not of the port; whether the DT divergence should be fixed, since fixing it changes the tree every P1/P2 payload carries and no current phase needs it true; and whether `dr_mode`/`maximum-speed` matter to the *Linux* payloads, which would need a Linux USB bring-up to observe.

**Not an action**: `tools/fv-inventory.py --roster` on two images and `--acpi` on three; one Python pass computing the roster diff and locating each payload's declared FDT by magic and hashing it against the staged tree; `dtc -I dtb -O dts` on the payload tree and on the vendor dump; `/usr/bin/grep -rn` across the firmware tree for `maximum-speed`, `dr_mode`, `"otg"`, `"host"`, `qcom,dwc3`, `snps,dwc3`, `qusb2`, `qmp-usb3` and the `phy@88e8000`/`ssphy@88e8000` blocks in both trees; `sed` and `ls`/`sha256sum`. ## Step 4.261 — the child-bus question is answered by the BSP rather than by ACPI: the ids the SLIMbus/audio chain waits on are published by `ADSP_Children`/`WPSS_Children` registry children, `CHLD` appears exactly once in the whole set and is a count, and the interface's own `_SUB` can be the reference board's token without denying the phone

The SLIMbus/BT/audio subtree has been recorded as owed since 4.255, with the reason "needs a `CHLD` publisher, which this port has never exercised". It needs no publisher at all, and that is a finding about the driver package rather than about this table.

**The parents declare their children in their own INF, as registry entries.** `qcsubsys_ext_adsp7280.inf` carries `[ADSP_Children]`: `Desktop\0 DeviceObjectName "SLM1"`, `_HID "QCOM0A0F"` — the exact id `qcslimbus7280.inf:47` binds — and `Desktop\1 "ADCM"`, `_HID "QCOM0A22"`, which is `qcadcm7280.inf:39`'s id. It is the WHQL `Extension.Inf` `AddReg` child-list idiom, and `qcsubsys_ext_wpss7280.inf` does the same for WPSS: `Desktop\0 "QWLN"`, `_HID "QCOM0A28"`, which is `qcwlan7280.inf:32`'s `WPSS\VEN_QCOM&DEV_0A28` with the bus prefix dropped. So `ADSP\QCOM0A0F`, `ADSP\QCOM0A22` and `WPSS\QCOM0A28` are all published by the subsystem driver's child list, and the audio and WLAN chains hang off a node this table already has.

**`CHLD` is a count, and it appears exactly once in 112 INFs.** `qcslimbus7280.inf:82` is `HKR,SLM1\CHLD, "NumChld", %REG_DWORD%, 0`. That is the SLIMbus driver arranging its own children; it is not the ACPI `CHLD` method and it is not a publisher of anything. Consistent with it: no child-list API appears anywhere in `qcadcm7280.sys`, `qcaucd7280.sys` or `qcaudminiport7280.sys`, which are the three drivers 4.258 said would need a `CHLD` publisher — and `qcslimbus7280.sys`'s KMDF imports are `WdfIoTargetCreate`/`WdfIoTargetOpen`/`WdfIoTargetQueryForInterface` only, the enum interface, not an enumerator. The tree's `CHLD` methods and the INF's `_Children` sections are two mechanisms for one thing, and the package chooses the registry one. 4.255's and 4.258's claim that the corpus's `CHLD` was the publisher is corrected: the corpus uses it, the package does not, and the package is what will run.

**What the reference token would activate, stated as the fact it is.** lisa's `PSUB` is `"IDP07280"` and lisa's `ADSP.ADCM.AUDD.CHLD` returns `AUDD\QCOM0A34` and `AUDD\QCOM0A29`; only `QCOM0A29` has a models line anywhere (`qcaudminiport_Base7280.inf:41`), `QCOM0A34` has none, and `QCOM0A23` — the id in lisa's `ADCM` `CHLD` — has none either. So on this package the `IDP07280` branch would add exactly one device, the audio miniport. `QCOM0A0F`, `QCOM0A22` and `QCOM0AC1` bind on their buses with no `_SUB` at all, since `ADSP_Children` and the `ADCM\` bus enumeration are ungated.

**`_SUB` can consequently be the reference token without this table asserting anything false about the phone.** Two independent reasons, both measured: (1) `_SUB` is the *child* device's subsystem id and PEP0's is the children's — the subsystem driver's `[Version]` carries no `_SUB` and no INF appends one — so PEP0's method is a fallback for a battery with expiry 2099, not a board statement; and (2) this file already writes the reference board's *compatible* id verbatim on URS0 (`_CID "PNP0CA1"`, lisa's, on both), so writing the reference board's subsystem id is the same kind of act and no board property is denied by it. lisa's own `PSUB` is `"IDP07280"` while its DT model is not an IDP at all, which is the proof that the token is an interface value rather than a silicon one.

**And the gate is not all-or-nothing, which its earlier readings implied.** Of the 47 ids this ASL presents, **nine** carry a `_SUBSYS`-gated models line somewhere in the set — `QCOM06E0`, `QCOM0A17`, `QCOM0A1B`, `QCOM0A25`, `QCOM0A32`, `QCOM0A33`, `QCOM0A98`, `QCOM0AD3`, `QCOM0AE2` — and the current token `MTP07225` opens **none** of them. `CRD07280` appears in **22 of the 26** gated INFs and covers **all nine**; `IDP07280` appears in 19 and also covers all nine. So the choice of token decides whether nine devices' extension INFAs install, and `MTP07225` — this port's invention, carrying no information — guarantees nine failures. Nine features are in reach of a string, and a text search could not have found the decisive one: `qcdx7280.inf`'s `QCOM0A36` is a plain `DriverVer`-style suffix, not a `_SUBSYS` token, and it depends on nothing.

**Correction to 4.241/4.242.** Those entries recorded a census of "5 of 25 subsystem-qualified ids gated on `CRD07280`/`MTP07280`/`QRD07280`/`IDP07280`/`CLS07280`/`CDP07280`/`IDPS7280`". The measurement here is **26 gated INFs, 25 tokens, 27 ids**, 22 of the INFs on `CRD07280`; the earlier figures came from a narrower scan that did not count the `Extension.Inf` sections. The conclusion the numbers support is unchanged in kind and different in size.

**decides**: that `ADSP\QCOM0A0F` (SLIMbus) and `ADSP\QCOM0A22` (ADCM) are published by `qcsubsys_ext_adsp7280.inf`'s `[ADSP_Children]` and `WPSS\QCOM0A28` (WLAN) by `qcsubsys_ext_wpss7280.inf`'s `[WPSS_Children]`, so the ADSP-node-only design 4.258 landed is enough for the chain and the "owed publisher" is withdrawn; that `CHLD` occurs **once** in the 112-INF set, as `NumChld = 0`, and none of the audio drivers carries a child-list API, so the corpus's `CHLD` idiom is not what this package uses; that **9 of the 47 ids this ASL presents** are `_SUBSYS`-gated and the current `MTP07225` opens zero of them, while `CRD07280` covers all nine (22 of 26 gated INFs) and `IDP07280` also covers all nine (19 of 26); that `_SUB` is the child's subsystem id and not the parent's, and that writing the reference board's token denies no board property, this file having already written lisa's `_CID` verbatim on URS0; and that only one audio device (`QCOM0A29`) hangs off the reference token's `AUDD` `CHLD`, the other three chain ids binding on their buses ungated. **does not decide**: whether the `Extension.Inf` child-list mechanism enumerates on Windows as read — the mechanism is documented but unexercised here; whether `CRD07280` or `IDP07280` matters in practice for this board's nine gated devices, since the camera and subsystem models lines are the same gated or ungated in most cases and the difference is the extension's registry entries rather than the base driver; whether the four remaining owed measurements below are worth their nodes; and whether any of it binds, no driver having bound anything on this device yet.

**Not an action**: `cabextract` on the seven audio-chain cabinets into `/tmp/k260/`, `iconv -f UTF-16` over the BSP's INFs, `/usr/bin/grep -a` over the extracted `.sys` import tables and over `/tmp/lisa-dsdt/DSDT.dsl`, `python3` passes for the `_SUBSYS` token census, the gated-id/ASL-id join, the bus-access census and the `[ADSP_Children]` read, `dtc`. All read-only against `~/work/woa-ref` and the backups; **no device command was issued** — the last confirmed device state remains TWRP at `d25f844e  recovery`. **Files written: `docs/08-device-session.md` alone** — `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl` and its twin are unchanged from 4.258 and no node, id, window or `_SUB` was altered by this step. **No partition, seed, `boot` or storage was written**, no `fastboot fetch`, no QEMU process started or signalled, and none of `work/out/{p2-variants,p3-display,usb-host,p2-what}`, `work/win11/qemu-stick*`, `work/out/p3-stick/` or `work/out/.p3-stick-drivers/` was touched. `device/dxe/UsbConfigDxe.efi` is still `sha256 6943cc615f7d4ba502c87bcf14a76e6e1398975a4101ed2711ba9e1c6e2566f5`. The orphaned dry-run processes 468162 and 471324 were left alive, `bq6ik1shs` was not restarted and `br7srnvmx` was not started. `userdata` (107 GB, unbacked), the partition table and the firmware LUN remain untouched, and the three physical actions — a screen photograph of the current `boot` payload, a reboot to the bootloader, and a USB 2.0 stick — remain with the user.

## Step 4.262 — the trigger-mode check 4.258 called impossible is written, and it fires: the phone's own device tree makes the ADSP interrupt **edge**, not level; the "eleven PDC entries, all type 4" the last three steps rested on was a parser artefact, and the real count is nine with three distinct types, while PEP0's edge on `0x265` is not a slip because the corpus's own PEP0 asks edge for the same number

**What was open.** Step 4.258 recorded two things as unmeasurable and this step closes one of them. The first was a count:
*"the coincidence that every one of the eleven PDC entries in this tree is type 4 is recorded below as a limit rather than a confirmation"* — a limit,
because a value that is the same everywhere confirms nothing about any single line. The second was the ADSP node's own trigger, written `Level, ActiveHigh` on that
non-discriminating evidence, with *"whether `acpi-dt-crosscheck.py` should grow a trigger-mode check, which would require a tree that discriminates — this one does
not"* left as the owed question. Both were measured this step. The value is not uniform, the count is not eleven, and the tree discriminates.

**The count was a parser artefact and the type cell was being read as the wrong thing.** `interrupts-extended` entrances are `<phandle> <cells...>`, and the number of
cells is the *controller's* `#interrupt-cells` — 3 for this board's GIC, 2 for its PDC — not a fixed 3. A first pass at this step walked every
`interrupts-extended` in groups of three cells regardless of controller and got nonsense for the PPI/SPI entries, which is how the count came to look like eleven
rather than nine and how pin 6's type came to read as `1` in one run and `4` in another depending on where the walk happened to land. Parsed by each controller's own
cell count — which is what `tools/acpi-dt-crosscheck.py` has done since 4.256 and which this step's throwaway script did not — gauguin's tree carries **nine** PDC
consumer entries, not eleven:

| node | PDC pin | type | GSI |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `remoteproc@3000000` (ADSP) | 6 | **1** | `0x206` |
| `ssusb@a600000` (USB0) | 14 | 3 | `0x20E` |
| `ssusb@a600000` (USB0) | 15 | 3 | `0x20F` |
| `ssusb@a600000` (USB0) | 17 | 4 | `0x211` |
| `qcom,tsens` uplow | 26 | 4 | `0x21A` |
| `qcom,tsens` uplow | 28 | 4 | `0x21C` |
| `qcom,tsens` crit | 27 | 4 | `0x21B` |
| `qcom,tsens` crit | 29 | 4 | `0x21D` |
| `spmi@…` | 1 | 4 | `0x201` |

Three types, not one: `1` at pin 6, `3` at both USB edge pokes, `4` at every other line. The old reading of three steps had been an artefact of the same class this
file keeps recording — an instrument that did not know the format, answering silently and wrongly.

**And the same table is the discriminating measurement 4.258 asked for.** ADSP's pin 6 is type `1`, which is the GIC's edge type, while the eight other consumers are
`3` and `4`. So the type cell is not uniform in this tree and does separate these lines, and the ADSP node's `Interrupt (ResourceConsumer, Level, …)` was wrong.
**The descriptor is now `Edge, ActiveHigh, Exclusive`** at `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl:598`, and the twin in
`uefi/Silicium-ACPI/Platforms/Xiaomi/gauguin/gauguin.asl` was regenerated rather than hand-edited.

**Two trees, one edge and one level, and the one that boots is the edge one — which took a second pass to get right and is the most useful thing to fall out of this
step.** `work/twrp-trip/flashed.dtb` (the DTB the live payload actually passes) and `work/out/sm7225-xiaomi-gauguin.dtb` (the tree the firmware carries) both read
`remoteproc@3000000`, PDC pin 6, type **1**. `/tmp/live-gauguin.dtb`, the vendor dump, reads the *same address, same SPI, same GSI* as `qcom,lpass@3000000` with
type **4**. The three disagree on the type and agree on everything else — 486 either way — and that is a property of the two trees rather than of the number. The
explanation is that they use different bindings: `flashed.dtb` and the payload's tree write the pin specifier `<&pdc 6 1>`, upstream's `qcom,pdc` binding where the
second cell *is* the GIC type; the vendor tree writes the same cells under `qcom,lpass@3000000`, its own driver's name for the node, whose reader may or may not
interpret that cell as a type at all. So the tree the firmware passes is the upstream one, its type cell is the one the ACPI descriptor has to match, and 4.258's
`Level` was wrong against it. **The first reading of this step — that the vendor's `Level` was authoritative — was taken from the wrong tree and is withdrawn in this
entry rather than carried:** the correction is what the paragraph records.

**Three checks run against the three trees, and one of the lines one of them raises is a corpus default rather than a slip.** Against `/tmp/live-gauguin.dtb`:

| device | GSI | ASL | the phone's tree | what it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ADSP` | `0x206` | Edge | Level | **settled by the tree that boots**: the payload's tree and the flashed tree both say type 1, so the vendor dump's `Level` is its own spelling and the descriptor stays Edge |
| `CAMP` | `0x1EB` | Level | Edge | **a ported line, and it was changed**: gauguin's `qcom,cam-cpas` — the *same DT node* lisa's `CAMP` is built around — says `interrupts = <0x00 0x1CB 0x01>`, type 1. lisa's DSDT has CAMP **Edge** on all three of its GSIs (`0x1EC`, `0x12F`, `0x1EB`), so this file's `Level` on its one GSI was a transcription slip and is corrected below |
| `PEP0` | `0x265` | Edge | Level | **not a slip**: the tree's line is GIC type 4 on a *different* block — `system-cache-controller@9200000` / `pmu@90b6300` (LLCC/bwmon), not a PEP0 resource |

The third is not a defect and the reason is stronger than the trigger cell. lisa's own `PEP0`, read out of `work/uefi/Mu-Silicium/Silicium-ACPI/Platforms/Xiaomi/lisa/Decompiled/DSDT.dsl`,
carries the **identical eleven-interrupt `_CRS` byte for byte**, `Edge, ActiveHigh, Exclusive` on `0x265` included. The port copied that resource block whole; the
board's device tree then attaches the number to a block PEP0 inherits. Writing the GIC SPI 0x83 back into two PEP0 lines would move the whole block from a table that
compiles `0 Error` — they are its *only* interrupts — so the finding is recorded here and in **does not decide** rather than acted on.

**CAMP was the second correction, and it is the same lesson one device over: the descriptor now follows the board's tree rather than the corpus's block.** lisa has
`Edge` on the one GSI this board keeps, so the change is *to* the corpus's own value and not away from it. The comment at the site says so and the twin was
regenerated. With both changes in, the check reports **one** line against the payload tree and the flashed tree — PEP0 — and **one** against the vendor dump, PEP0
again, the ADSP disagreement having disappeared once the descriptor matches the type cell the booting tree carries.

**The check is written into `tools/acpi-dt-crosscheck.py`, and its first placement was wrong in the way this tool has already named twice.** A GIC type cell decodes
to the ACPI word the descriptor must carry (`1`/`2`/`3` edge, `4` level; `TYPE_TRIGGER`), `Tree.triggers(gsi)` returns the *set* of triggers every node declaring a
number asks for (two nodes can share one — `system-cache-controller@9200000` and `pmu@90b6300` both sit on `0x265` — so a set and not a word), and `asl_resources`
now returns the source's own trigger per line rather than a flag. The report is a warning and not a failure, because a mismatch is either a descriptor to change here
or a corpus default the board overrides and only a reader can say which. **The asl loop was first written after the window-match logic**, where a device with no
`Memory32Fixed` — `ADSP`, `CAMP`, `PEP0` and `PM01` among them, four of the nodes the check was written for — would `continue` past it and never be checked. Run
against the payload tree the check printed nothing and the omission was silent; moved above the `continue`, the payload tree and both phone trees report the rows
above. That is the third time in this file that a checker's own placement has made findings disappear rather than fail loud, and the fix is recorded where the tool
prints.

**The tree that will boot is the phone's, and this makes that concrete.** `flash.dtb`'s `__symbols__`/`ramoops` divergence from `work/out/sm7225-xiaomi-gauguin.dtb`
(4.260) is the only difference between the tree inside the payload and the one ABL actually hands the kernel: ABL takes the payload's tree, applies the vendor
overlay, and rewrites it (4.193's logfs), so the booting tree is the phone's in cell values and this board's in board-id. The practical consequence is the table
above: **firmware that reads the trigger from the booting tree and the GSI from the table gets a level-high ADSP line on an edge pin**, and the P3 gate is the first
place that can be seen. `Level, ActiveHigh` on type 1 is exactly the pairing an APIC/GIC line rejects at assert time, and it survived three steps because nothing
that judged it existed.

**decides**: that `interrupts-extended`'s cell count is the controller's `#interrupt-cells` and that the "eleven PDC entries, all type 4" the record has carried
since 4.253 was a parser artefact — gauguin's tree carries **nine** PDC consumer entries at types **1, 3 and 4**; that the type cell is therefore discriminating in
this tree after all, which is the measurement 4.258 asked for and could not find; that `Device (ADSP)`'s interrupt is **Edge**, not Level, corrected at
`tools/acpi/gauguin.asl:598` and regenerated into the tracked twin, and that the change cites the right tree — the payload's tree and the tree ABL actually hands the
kernel both read type `1` at that pin, while only the vendor dump's `qcom,lpass@3000000` reads `Level`, so the descriptor follows the tree that boots; that `tools/acpi-dt-crosscheck.py` now judges trigger mode, reports it as a warning per GSI against every tree at once, and that its first
placement was wrong in the direction that hides findings rather than raising them; and that PEP0's `0x265` Edge is **not** a defect, because lisa's own PEP0 carries
the identical eleven-interrupt `_CRS` verbatim and gauguin's tree attaches that number to an LLCC/bwmon block PEP0 inherits. **does not decide**: whether PEP0's `0x265` line should
follow the board — the corpus's PEP0 and this one are the same resource block and they are its only interrupts, so changing it moves the whole device; whether the PDC pin 6 → GSI 486
mapping survives the vendor tree's own loader, which the payload's tree and the phone's agree on and which the ASL therefore rests on unchanged; whether any of the
three disagreements matters at runtime, since `acpiexec` has no GIC and no ITS and nothing here has seen a PnP manager; whether the `PEP0` block should be re-derived
from gauguin's tree at all, that being a decision about a device this board's AML may never ask about; and whether the ADSP node compiles into an ACPI table the
DSP's driver will actually open, which is the P3 gate and remains the P3 gate. **Not an action**: `dtc -I dtb -O dts` on both trees the phone owns; one Python pass
re-decoding every `interrupts-extended` in each tree by the controller's own cell count; `iasl -tc tools/acpi/gauguin.asl` (`0 Errors, 26 Warnings, 109 Remarks,
415 Optimizations`); `tools/acpi-runtime-check.py` (`PASS`, 50 top-level devices, 29 `_STA` bodies, 32 `_CRS` bodies identical and 0 mismatched); `tools/acpi-dt-crosscheck.py`
against the payload tree, `/tmp/live-gauguin.dtb`, `work/twrp-trip/flashed.dtb` and the two at once, plus `--strict`; `tools/make_uefi_platform.py --repo . --xhci-host`;
`diff`, `cmp`, `python3 -m py_compile`, `/usr/bin/grep`, `sed`, `wc`. **Files written**: `tools/acpi-dt-crosscheck.py` (the trigger check and its two placement
fixes), `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl` and the regenerated `uefi/Silicium-ACPI/Platforms/Xiaomi/gauguin/gauguin.asl`, and this entry. **Two `iasl` artefacts under
`tools/acpi/` (`DSDT.aml`, `gauguin.hex`) were written by the compile and deleted afterwards, neither being tracked.** **No file under `work/out/` was written** — the
payloads in `work/out/p3-covered/` still carry the 4.258 table and would exercise neither the CSIPHY nodes nor the ADSP node, so a gate run on them would test a
trigger this step just corrected. **No device command was issued** — the last confirmed device state remains TWRP at `d25f844e  recovery`; **no partition, seed,
`boot` or storage was written**, no `fastboot` command of any kind, no `fastboot fetch`, no QEMU process started or signalled, and none of `work/out/{p2-variants,p3-display,usb-host,p2-what}`,
