## Step 4.268 — the seventh gated id was never gated: PEP0's `&REV_` is the SoC product revision and not the DSDT's, and four steps had read it as a table revision so they could call the board's own power controller unreachable

**What this step is.** 4.264 wrote, into the `PSUB` comment at the top of the file, that `QCOM0A17` (PEP0) "turns out to be unreachable either way" — because every `qcpep.wd7280.inf` models line naming it carries `&SUBSYS_…&REV_<xxxx>` and `_REV` "is the DSDT's own revision, this table's `DefinitionBlock (..., 2, ...)`, and `2` is below every one of them". The sentence was load-bearing: it is why the token question was recorded as "the lever for six of the nine gated ids and the DSDT revision for the seventh", and why the file has never carried a `_HRV` or a `_REV`. This step is that sentence, tested, and it is wrong three times over. The correction is comment-only in the compiled sense — `iasl` produces a **byte-identical** `DSDT.aml` (`sha256 728f4d3f…`, the 4.267 table) — and it is the whole of the step, because what a false claim in this file costs is the next reader.

**First: PEP0 is bound by a plain line, in the same models section, and always was.** `qcpep.wd7280.inf:33` is `%PepDevice.DeviceDesc%=Pep_Device, ACPI\QCOM0A17` — no `SUBSYS`, no `REV_` — and it sits in `[QC.NTARM64]`, the *same* section as the twelve `&SUBSYS_…&REV_…` lines at `:92`-`:103`. It is the only `QCOM0A17` line in the entire 112-INF set that lacks both fields, and this is what the binding census had been saying all along: `tools/acpi-hid-census.py --bind` reports `QCOM0A17 1x claimed by qcpep.wd7280.inf` and does **not** list it as gated. The ASL's own preamble says to run that census "before adding any node here"; the PEP0 sentence was written without it, and the census contradicts the sentence.

**Second: `_REV` is the ACPI "Supported Integer Width" object, and the INF's `REV_` values are the SoC product revision.** Measured on the two reference boards, which is the only place the mapping is written down: lisa's `GPU0._HRV` computes `PROD = ((\_SB.SJTG >> 0x0C) & 0xFFFF)` — `SJTG` being the SoC ID register — and branches on exactly `0x0193`, `0x0194`, `0x01E3`, `0x01EB`, `0x020A` and `0x0215`. Those are the INF's six `REV_` tokens, **one for one, no extras on either side**. The DSDT revision is unrelated, and the corpus settles that in one line: all 28 decompiled tables are `DefinitionBlock (…, 2, …, 0x00000003)`, lisa and a52sxq included — the boards this INF set ships for. So "revision 2 is below every one of them" compares a table revision against a silicon revision; `0x0193` is 403, and nothing about a `DefinitionBlock` revision of 2 is below 403. The paragraph that concluded "raising the revision to satisfy a driver would be a much larger statement than the token is" rested entirely on that confusion — and raising the `DefinitionBlock` revision, which is the thing the paragraph warns against, would not have reached a single one of these lines. `_REV` **is** writable as a Method (verified on a scratch table: `Method (_REV) { Return (0xFFFFFFFF) }` compiles, disassembles as `Method (_REV, …)`, and `acpiexec` evaluates it to `0xFFFFFFFF`); it is simply not the number the INF is matching.

**Third, and this is the part that matters for the port: the `&REV_` lines are not the bind either, so the correct default is the one already in the file.** For the IDP07280 family, which is this board's, the five `SUBSYS_IDP07280` lines point at **three different descriptors** — `PEP_Device_IDP07280` (`REV_0193`, `REV_01EB`), `PEP_Device_IDP07270` (`REV_0215`) and `PEP_Device_IDP08270` (`REV_01E3`, `REV_020A`) — and when none of them matches, `:33`'s plain `Pep_Device` installs. So the revisioned lines do not open a section the plain line leaves shut; they name a *more specific* descriptor for a board that reports one of the six. The risk runs the other way: a `_SUB`/`_REV` pair that matched a `CRD07280` line, or one of the two lines that name `PEP_Device_IDP08270` while its own subsystem string says `IDP07280`, would pend a device description for a CRD or an 08270 — not this board — which is worse than the generic descriptor. Inventing a `_REV` that lisa does not expose on PEP0, in order to match a driver's string, is the same move the `RFS0` windows were deliberately left empty to avoid in 4.267: writing a claim about this board's silicon to satisfy a selector. This file keeps `PSUB → "IDP07280"`, PEP0 with no `_HRV` and no `_REV`, and the plain line as the binding.

**What is still open, stated rather than implied.** The plain line binds PEP0; it does not say *which PEP behaviour* the driver then runs, and the descriptor choice above is the mechanism by which a board tells it. Whether this board reports one of the six revisions is not recorded anywhere in the corpus or in either device tree — `qcom,msi-id`/`qcom,board-id` carry board identity and not silicon revision, and the SoC ID register is not in a DTB. Adding a `_REV` would be a claim; the honest state is that gauguin binds the generic PEP descriptor and would need a measurement off the running board to claim more. That measurement is available on the phone and not offline, so it is deferred rather than guessed.

**Gates.** `iasl -tc`: `0 Errors, 26 Warnings, 115 Remarks, 466 Optimizations`, `DSDT.aml` 14,578 bytes — and `cmp` against the staged 4.267 table is **identical**, which is the check that makes this a comment step rather than a table step. `tools/acpi-runtime-check.py` `PASS` (`61 of 61` top-level devices, `35` `_CRS` bodies identical, `0` mismatched). `tools/acpi-dt-crosscheck.py` `PASS` (`21 device(s) cross-checked; 0 slip(s), 0 unaccounted`). `tools/driver-id-census.py` `ASL presents 57 id(s)` unchanged; `tools/acpi-hid-census.py --bind` unchanged and now quoted as the authority the sentence had ignored. `tools/make_uefi_platform.py` regenerated the twin (`cmp` identical). **No payload rebuild**: the staged `DSDT.aml` is `sha256 728f4d3f2584723502b7f366d7b8cfc142c641b9345858d3fd3c858f58ac33f3` both before and after, so the 4.267 image set still embeds exactly this table and rebuilding would produce three byte-identical images.

**decides**: that the 4.264 sentence "`QCOM0A17` (PEP0) turns out to be unreachable either way" is **false** and is corrected in place — `qcpep.wd7280.inf:33` binds `ACPI\QCOM0A17` plainly in the same `[QC.NTARM64]` section as the gated lines, so PEP0 binds on `_SUB` or not, and the census has said so since it was written; that `_REV` is the ACPI Supported Integer Width object and the INF's `REV_0193`/`01EB`/`01E3`/`020A`/`0215` are the SoC product revision (`PROD = ((\_SB.SJTG >> 0x0C) & 0xFFFF)` on the reference boards, six values matching six tokens one for one), **not** the `DefinitionBlock` revision, which is 2 on all 28 corpus tables including lisa and a52sxq; that the revisioned models lines name more specific descriptors rather than gating an otherwise-shut install (five `SUBSYS_IDP07280` lines, three different descriptors, two of them naming an 08270); and that this file's correct default is therefore the plain line with no `_HRV` and no `_REV`, which is what it already has. **does not decide**: which of the six product revisions gauguin's silicon reports, which no offline source carries — `qcom,msm-id`/`qcom,board-id` are board identity, both device trees are silent on silicon revision, and the SoC ID register is in hardware; whether the generic `Pep_Device` behaves differently enough from `PEP_Device_IDP07280` to matter, which is a driver question and not a table question; and whether `SJTG` should be written and populated from a register read the way lisa does, which is its own measurement and is not made here — the `MMU0` comment already records `SVMJ`/`_HRV` as deferred for the same reason.

**Not an action**: `iasl -tc` on the ASL (in `/tmp`, no artefact under `tools/acpi/`), `iasl -tc`/`iasl -d`/`acpiexec` on a scratch one-device table carrying `Method (_REV) { Return (0xFFFFFFFF) }` — the measurement that `_REV` is representable and evaluates, and which also corrected an earlier `AE_NOT_FOUND` caused by running `acpiexec` against the wrong file, not by the construct; `grep -m1 DefinitionBlock` over all 28 corpus tables (all revision 2); `python3` and `iconv -f UTF-16 -t UTF-8` over all 112 INFs for every `0A17` line and every `REV_[0-9A-F]{4}` token; the `PROD == 0x…` extraction from lisa's `GPU0._HRV`; `/usr/bin/grep` over the device trees for `qcom,msm-id`/`qcom,board-id`/`qcom,socinfo`/`sm7225`; `timeout 900 tools/make_uefi_platform.py --repo . --xhci-host`; `cmp` on the twin and on the compiled AML; `tools/acpi-runtime-check.py`, `tools/acpi-dt-crosscheck.py`, `tools/acpi-hid-census.py --bind`, `tools/driver-id-census.py`; `sha256sum`, `stat`. Read-only against the device and its backups; **no `adb` or `fastboot` command was issued at all this step** — `adb devices` was not even read, the prior step's `d25f844e recovery` being the last observed state; `fastboot fetch` was not used, no partition, seed, `boot` or storage was written, no QEMU process was started or signalled, and none of `work/out/{p2-variants,p3-display,usb-host,p2-what}`, `work/win11/qemu-stick*`, `work/out/p3-stick/` or `work/out/.p3-stick-drivers/` was touched. **Files written**: `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl`, the regenerated `uefi/Silicium-ACPI/Platforms/Xiaomi/gauguin/gauguin.asl` (`cmp`-identical), and this entry. `device/dxe/UsbConfigDxe.efi` is still `sha256 6943cc615f7d4ba502c87bcf14a76e6e1398975a4101ed2711ba9e1c6e2566f5`. The orphaned dry-run processes 468162 and 471324 were left alive, `bq6ik1shs` was not restarted and `br7srnvmx` was not started. **Consequence for the P3 gate**: none — the table the gate will judge is byte-identical to 4.267's, so this step changes what the port *believes* about the board and not what the board will boot. **device state**: unchanged — `adb devices` last listed `d25f844e recovery` (TWRP), both tty globs absent, `lsblk` shows no removable medium, and the P3 gate has still never been run. `userdata` (107 GB, unbacked), the partition table and the firmware LUN remain untouched, and the three physical actions — a screen photograph of the current `boot` payload, a reboot to the bootloader, and a USB 2.0 stick — remain with the user.

## Step 4.269 — the P3 medium installed the wrong CPU: `tools/make-p3-stick.sh` promised an ARM64 stick and shipped an x86_64 one, which the correct ARM64 ISO in this project's own build directory had already superseded

**What this step is.** P3's gate is *"a Windows 11 ARM64 installer boots off a USB stick and sees the internal UFS"*. The firmware is only half of that; the other half is the medium, and 4.240 built one with `tools/make-p3-stick.sh`, whose first line reads `# Assemble a complete Windows 11 ARM64 install stick for the P3 gate.` That stick does not install Windows on this device, or on any ARM64 device, because its install image is **x86_64** — and the script never reads an architecture string anywhere. `grep -n 'Architecture\|arch\|x86_64\|ARM64' tools/make-p3-stick.sh` matched only the docstring's lines 3 and 5 and one comment at 142; its verification block checks that six files **exist** and nothing about what is in them. The defect was found by reading `work/out/p3-stick/sources/install.swm` with `wiminfo`, not by reading the script: `Image Count: 11`, and `Architecture: x86_64` on every one of the eleven editions, split from `$WOA/win11-25h2/install.wim` — which is likewise `x86_64` on all eleven — by the script's own line 74, `INSTALL=$WOA/win11-25h2/install.wim`.

**The premise the merge was built on was true; the source it reached for was not.** `make-p3-stick.sh` merges two halves for a stated reason: `p3-medium-built/media1` is a setup engine with no install image, and `p3-medium-built/usb-p3/SOURCES/BOOT.WIM` is Windows RE whose one image is `Microsoft Windows Recovery Environment (arm64)` — no `Windows Setup` image to run. Both halves measure as described: `usb-p3`'s `BOOT.WIM` is 446,983,676 B, 1 image, ARM64, 26100; `media1` is Aarch64 throughout (`setup.exe`, `sources/setup.exe`, `sources/setupcore.dll`, `sources/winsetup.dll`, `sources/setupplatform.exe`, `efi/boot/bootaa64.efi` all report `PE32+ … Aarch64`). So the merge was not the mistake. The mistake is one variable: with `media1` and `usb-p3` both ARM64, the *only* non-ARM64 input is the one the script took from a Windows 11 x64 install, and it took it because `win11-25h2/install.wim` was where an `install.wim` happened to be, not because anything checked what it was.

**ARM64 is not missing on this host; it was built here on 2026-09-29 and then not used.** `work/win11/build/26100.1_PROFESSIONAL_ARM64_EN-US.ISO` — 4,265,445,376 B, the output of this project's own UUP converter — is a complete ARM64 install medium, and every property `make-p3-stick.sh` stitches together by hand is already in it:

- `sources/install.wim` **3,520,950,655 B**, one image, `Architecture: ARM64`, `Edition ID: Professional`, Build 26100, 82,652 files, 16,466,000,878 B uncompressed, LZX — `wimlib-imagex verify` reports *"was successfully verified"*. Under FAT32's 4,294,967,295-byte ceiling, so no `.swm` split and no reassembly asked of Setup.
- `sources/boot.wim` **465,806,736 B**, **two** images, both ARM64, `Boot Index: 2` — index 1 `Microsoft Windows PE`, index 2 `Microsoft Windows Setup`. The Setup image is the thing `usb-p3` did not have.
- `efi/boot/bootaa64.efi` `PE32+ … Aarch64`; `efi/microsoft/boot/bcd` whose UTF-16 strings resolve `\sources\boot.wim`, `\boot\boot.sdi` and `\windows\system32\boot\winload.efi`.
- `sources/boot.wim` image 2 carries the inbox UFS driver in both places a driver is found: `Windows/System32/drivers/storufs.sys`, `Windows/INF/storufs.inf`, and the DriverStore package `storufs.inf_arm64_744761edc9e26f6c` — the id it claims, `ACPI\QCOM24A5`, being exactly the one `tools/acpi-hid-census.py --drivers … --bind --asl` reports gauguin's `UFS0` node presenting.

So "sees the internal UFS" has a complete driver path on the medium before a single CAB is injected, and the 112 SC7280/Kodiak CABs are still injected for the platform around the controller — WinPE has no offline DISM and this host is Linux, so they go to `X:\Drivers` and `drvload` loads them before `wpeinit`, which is the runtime path `make-p3-stick.sh` used and the one that works.

**The UUP route was tried first and abandoned, which is worth recording because it failed for an instructive reason.** With no x86_64/ARM64 pairing obvious and `~/work/woa-ref/win11-25h2/install.wim` the file the script named, the ARM64 source appeared to be the UUP's `professional_en-us.esd` — 470,298,718 B, whose image 3 `wiminfo` reports as `Windows 11 Pro`, `Architecture: ARM64`, Build 26100, 82,651 files, 16,019,017,042 B uncompressed. It is a **complete, byte-exact download**: `sha1sum` is `9f905706525f38af443c81b6672978515ab89f75`, matching `arm64-25h2-uup/expected.tsv` exactly, and `aria2.log` records the download complete. It nonetheless cannot be exported, and the reason is not corruption: `wimlib-imagex verify professional_en-us.esd` fails on a **missing blob** — `"…/WiFiNetworkManagerWarningToast.scale-400_contrast-white.png": blob not found`, SHA-1 `d7e9d43dad951726a8dddd9b05e715ade8ed197c`. It is a UUP **reference ESD**: image 3 is a delta whose blobs live in the eighteen companion payloads (`Microsoft-Windows-Client-*`, `EditionPack-*`, `Edge.wim`, …), and `wimlib-imagex export … --ref` against all nineteen of them advanced the export past that gap and found another, and then another — `.mun` resources first, then a font, then a **WOW64** `arm64.x86_…accountaccessor.dll` that no local payload supplies. The one blob that *is* locally recoverable was recovered and verified: `Microsoft-Windows-StepsRecorder-Package-arm64.cab` holds `psr.exe.mun` at the exact path image 3 wants, `sha1sum 7562567976f0a9b743957a900e6c651e4541beb1`, matching the missing digest — and repairing a scratch copy with `wimlib-imagex update` let the export advance further and fail on the next one. The route was abandoned there, not because the repair is impossible but because it is a chain, and the **complete** image was already sitting in `work/win11/build/`. That is the finding: the ARM64 medium existed, and the script reached past it for an x64 file.

**A second, independent defect, in the injection target rather than the install image.** `make-p3-stick.sh` injects with `wimlib-imagex update "$WIM" 1` — image **1**. On this ISO's `boot.wim` the boot index is **2**, the `Microsoft Windows Setup` image; image 1 is `Microsoft Windows PE`, which nothing boots. Measured: `Boot Index: 2` from `wiminfo`, and image 1's `/Windows/System32/startnet.cmd` is Microsoft's original two-line `wpeinit` while image 2's is the injected one. A build that edited image 1 would have produced a stick where the driver tree sits in an image Windows never loads. The new tool reads the boot index and targets it, and asserts `/Drivers` landed there (`885` entries) rather than anywhere else (`0` in image 1).

**Verified, not assumed.** After the build: `wiminfo` reports `install.wim` 1 image and `boot.wim` 2 images, **all ARM64**, both before and after injection; `wimlib-imagex verify` on the injected `boot.wim` reports *"was successfully verified"*; the driver tree is `112 INFs, 67 .sys, 112 .cat in 112 dirs`, the same one-directory-per-CAB shape 4.240 established and for the same reason (four of the 112 carry a filename at two different contents, so flattening hands two of them the wrong catalog); `/Drivers` holds 885 entries in image 2 and 0 in image 1; the injected `startnet.cmd` has `sha1 344e7a258d4f0003280a8d2f9caf48d83b493665` in image 2 and image 1's is unchanged at `abc6d9530256486c8861f7d0ec666cb9ae9674ae`; the loose tree is 948 files, 4.3 GB, with `efi/boot/bootaa64.efi` Aarch64. The **negative test** is the one that matters for the check's own worth: a tree assembled with the old x86_64 `install.wim` and an ARM64 `boot.wim` is refused by the new tool with `error: install.wim is not ARM64 - this medium would install the wrong architecture` and exit 1 — and the old `make-p3-stick.sh`, given the check added in this step, now refuses its own default with `error: … /win11-25h2/install.wim is not ARM64 - use tools/make-p3-medium.sh with an ARM64 ISO`.

**decides**: that `tools/make-p3-stick.sh` built an x86_64 install medium while its docstring promised an ARM64 one, and that the cause is a single unsourced variable plus the total absence of an architecture assertion — not the two-half merge, whose premise (ARM64 setup engine, WinRE-only boot WIM) measures as stated; that `work/win11/build/26100.1_PROFESSIONAL_ARM64_EN-US.ISO` is a complete, verified ARM64 install medium (`install.wim` 3,520,950,655 B ARM64 Professional 26100 one image, `boot.wim` 465,806,736 B two ARM64 images with `Microsoft Windows Setup` at boot index 2, inbox `storufs` present) and supersedes the merge; that injection belongs in the **boot index** image, which is 2 here and not 1; that the UUP `professional_en-us.esd` is byte-exact but a reference ESD whose image 3 has blobs in the companion payloads and at least one (`arm64.x86_…accountaccessor.dll`) supplied by none of them, so it is not the right source while the ISO exists; and that `tools/make-p3-medium.sh` is the medium builder, with `tools/make-p3-stick.sh` now refusing a non-ARM64 install image rather than silently splitting one.

**does not decide**: whether the stick boots on the phone, which needs the phone, a USB 2.0 stick and a reboot to the bootloader, and is the gate itself; whether Setup completes, since the medium being complete is not the gate being met; whether the 112 injected INFs bind anything, `drvload` being a runtime path whose outcome is decided by this project's ACPI and not by the medium — if Setup's disk list does not show the UFS, the finding is about the ASL and not the medium, and the medium's own UFS driver path is complete; whether the UUP ESD's missing-blob set is finite and every member locally recoverable, since the chain was abandoned rather than completed once the ISO was found; and whether the ISO's `boot.wim` image 2 runs `startnet.cmd` rather than a `winpeshl.ini` — it was measured to have none, unlike `usb-p3`'s WIM, but the runtime confirmation is on the phone.

**Not an action**: `wiminfo`/`wimlib-imagex` (`info`, `dir`, `extract`, `export`, `verify`, `update`, `split`), `7z` (extract the ISO and the install image), `file` over the setup engines and EFI binaries, `strings -el` over the BCD, `bsdtar` over the FASP/StepsRecorder cabs, `sha1sum`/`sha256sum`, `cabextract` (112 cabinets), `grep`/`cmp`/`find`/`stat`, `bash`, `python3`. One scratch ESD repair (a copy, in `~/work/woa-ref/arm64-install-scratch`, since deleted) proved the `psr.exe.mun` route and was abandoned. Read-only against the device; **no `adb` or `fastboot` command was issued**, `fastboot fetch` was not used, no partition, seed, `boot` or storage was written, no QEMU process was started or signalled — the FAT32 `.img` step was reached and stopped rather than run, since `losetup` needs root and no stick is attached — and none of `work/out/{p2-variants,p3-display,usb-host,p2-what}`, `work/win11/qemu-stick*`, `work/out/p3-stick/` or `work/out/.p3-stick-drivers/` was touched; the new medium is `work/out/p3-medium-arm64` with its tree at `work/out/p3-iso-tree` and its driver cache at `work/out/.p3-medium-drivers`, all new and gitignored. **Files written**: `tools/make-p3-medium.sh` (new), `tools/make-p3-stick.sh` (the architecture check added), and this entry. `device/dxe/UsbConfigDxe.efi` is still `sha256 6943cc615f7d4ba502c87bcf14a76e6e1398975a4101ed2711ba9e1c6e2566f5`. The orphaned dry-run processes 468162 and 471324 were left alive, `bq6ik1shs` was not restarted and `br7srnvmx` was not started. **Consequence for the P3 gate**: the medium the gate will use now installs ARM64 Windows 11 Pro, and the earlier stick's defect is closed — but the gate still needs the phone, a USB 2.0 stick and a bootloader reboot, and the three physical actions remain with the user.

## Step 4.270 — the medium is built and verified through its own filesystem: `work/out/p3-medium-arm64.img`, 6.0 GB FAT32, `install.wim` and `boot.wim` both ARM64 as read back from the mounted partition

**What this step is.** 4.269 corrected the medium's *design* and proved it on the source tree. It left one thing between the tree and the phone: the FAT32 image a stick is written from. `tools/make-win-stick.sh` builds it, but its first line needs a loop device and this host's `losetup` denies a non-root caller — so the build had been reached and stopped in 4.269 rather than run. It is run here, and the artifact is verified by reading its WIMs back **through the FAT32 filesystem** rather than through the tree they were copied from, which is the check that says the medium survives the copy.

**The build.** `tools/make-win-stick.sh work/out/p3-iso-tree work/out/p3-medium-arm64.img 6G`, exit 0: MBR, one FAT32 partition, **1035 files**, `bootaa64.efi` present, BCD present, used `4.3G of 6.0G`. `fsck.vfat 4.2` on the partition — the double-loop form 4.240 established, because this host's `fsck.fat` has no `--offset` — reports `1035 files, 1107784/1569536 clusters` and no error. The image is `6,442,450,944 B` and is owned by the invoking user, which `make-win-stick.sh`'s own closing step arranges because QEMU opens it read-write.

**The verification, and why it is the one that counts.** The image was mounted read-only on a loop device and the WIMs were read from `/mnt/vfy/sources/`, so what is reported is what a booting guest would find and not what the tree held:

```
install.wim   Image Count: 1   Architecture: ARM64   Edition ID: Professional   Build: 26100
boot.wim      Image Count: 2   Boot Index: 2   Architecture: ARM64 (x2)   Build: 26100
/Drivers      boot.wim image 2, 886 entries (885 files + the path itself)
```

Both WIMs are under FAT32's 4 GiB per-file ceiling — `install.wim` is 3,520,950,655 B and `boot.wim` 739,376,552 B as the stick holds it — so no `.swm` split and nothing for Setup to reassemble, which is the reason this FAT32 image is legal where the earlier `install.swm` set was a workaround for an image that could not be one file.

**decides**: that the ARM64 install medium exists as a dd-ready FAT32 image at `work/out/p3-medium-arm64.img`, and that reading the WIMs out of the mounted partition returns `install.wim` ARM64 Professional 26100 and `boot.wim` two ARM64 images with boot index 2 and the 112-CAB driver tree intact in that index — the same facts as the tree, re-measured across the filesystem boundary the stick introduces. **does not decide**: whether a guest boots it, which 4.217/4.218 already reached on the prior stick (AAVMF drew the `Windows Setup` window; the guest is TCG-slow rather than stuck) and which is not what changed here — what changed is the architecture of the install image; and whether the phone boots it, which is the gate and needs the phone, a USB 2.0 stick and a bootloader reboot.

**Not an action**: `sudo -n tools/make-win-stick.sh` (the loop-device build, which is the point), `losetup`/`mount -o ro`/`umount` on a second loop device to read the image's WIMs, `wiminfo`/`wimlib-imagex dir` through the mount, `fsck.vfat`, `ls`/`stat`. Read-only against the device; **no `adb` or `fastboot` command was issued**, `fastboot fetch` was not used, no partition, seed, `boot` or storage was written, no QEMU process was started or signalled, and none of `work/out/{p2-variants,p3-display,usb-host,p2-what}`, `work/win11/qemu-stick*`, `work/out/p3-stick/` or `work/out/.p3-stick-drivers/` was touched. **Files written**: `work/out/p3-medium-arm64.img` (new, gitignored) and this entry. `device/dxe/UsbConfigDxe.efi` is still `sha256 6943cc615f7d4ba502c87bcf14a76e6e1398975a4101ed2711ba9e1c6e2566f5`. The orphaned dry-run processes 468162 and 471324 were left alive, `bq6ik1shs` was not restarted and `br7srnvmx` was not started. **Consequence for the P3 gate**: the medium half of the gate is now a single verified image; what remains is the phone half — a USB 2.0 stick to write it to, a bootloader reboot, and the `先读屏，再刷下一次` photograph before any `boot` overwrite.

## Step 4.271 — the camera chain's two unconditional nodes written: `CAMF` (`QCOM0A06`) and `FLSH` (`QCOM0A27`), with no windows for the reason `RFS0` has none, and the SKUV-gated sensors left owed rather than guessed

**What this step is.** "All hardware driven" is the goal's standing clause, and the census has carried camera ids with a plain driver and no node for many steps. Reading the chain against lisa shows it is mostly written already — `CAMP` (`QCOM0A32`), `JPGE` (`QCOM0A33`), `VFE0` (`QCOM0A25`), `CPHY` (`QCOM0A98`, the corpus's `MPCS`), and `CSID`/`CSI1`/`CSI2` (`QCOM0AA2`) — and the two ids the driver set claims plainly that this file still does not present are `QCOM0A06` (front sensor) and `QCOM0A27` (flash). Both are now written, and the one that is deliberately still not written is written down as owed rather than guessed.

**Both ids bind unconditionally, checked before writing.** `qccamfrontsensor7280.inf:61` is `%CameraFrontSensor.DeviceDesc% = CameraFrontSensor_Device, ACPI\QCOM0A06` and `qccamflash7280.inf:38` is `%Flash.DeviceDesc% = CameraFlash_Device, ACPI\QCOM0A27` — plain models lines, no `SUBSYS`, no `REV_`. The binding census confirms `QCOM0A06 1x claimed by qccamfrontsensor_extension7280.inf, qccamfrontsensor7280.inf` and `QCOM0A27 1x claimed by qccamflash7280.inf` after the write. The front-sensor id's extension INF carries **no** `CRD07280` line, so nothing here is contingent on the token the way `QCOM0A99` is.

**Neither is given a window, and the tree agrees with the corpus.** lisa's `CAMF` and `FLSH` have no `_CRS` — FLSH's is `Buffer (0x02) { 0x79, 0x00 }`, which is the ACPI `END_TAG` and therefore an *empty* resource template, the corpus writing a `_CRS` that resolves to nothing rather than omitting the method. gauguin's own tree says the same by omission: `qcom,camera-flash@0/@5/@6` have no `reg`, and the front sensor is enumerated over the CCI bus the eeprom nodes share (`qcom,eeprom@0/@1/@4` on `cci0`, `@2/@3` on `cci1`), not over a memory window. This is 4.267's `RFS0` decision applied again — a window invented to satisfy a driver's probe would hand it an address belonging to something else — so `CAMF` carries no `_CRS` and `FLSH` carries lisa's empty buffer, so the method a driver may probe for is present and resolves to no resources.

**`_DEP` is on the platform node, not on the siblings.** `CAMF` depends on `CPHY` (the MIPI-CSI PHY its data path runs through) and `FLSH` on `CAMP`, which is lisa's owned shape; the corpus's camera nodes are deliberately thin and do not chain to each other. `_UID`s are lisa's, `0x1A` and `0x19`, and they are distinct from every other camera node's (CAMP `0x1B`, JPGE `0x17`, VFE0 `0x16`, CPHY `0x18`, CSID/CSI1/CSI2 `0x21`/`0x22`/`0x23`) — the property that matters, since a colliding `_UID` silently renames a device.

**What is owed and not guessed.** lisa's `CAMI` (`QCOM0A99`, aux sensor), `CAMT` (`QCOM0ACE`) and `CAMU` (`QCOM0ACF`) are gated on `\_SB.SKUV`, and on the **IDP** variant (`SKUV == One`) all three return `_STA Zero` — they are *disabled* on exactly the board this file's `PSUB` names (`IDP07280`, 4.264). Writing them enabled would contradict that token; writing them disabled would add namespace that drives nothing. But gauguin's tree carries more camera modules than the front sensor alone — `qcom,eeprom@0` through `@4` across both CCI buses, `qcom,flash_0/@1/@2`, and a `qcom,camera-flash` set of three — so whether gauguin is really the IDP configuration lisa disables those sensors for is a question this file can state and cannot settle offline. It is recorded here, in the file, as owed. `CAMT`/`CAMU` also have no INF in the 112-set, so even their ids would bind nothing.

**Gates.** `iasl -tc`: `0 Errors, 26 Warnings, 117 Remarks, 470 Optimizations`, `DSDT.aml` **14,722 bytes** (was 14,578; +144), `sha256 5448bc512e10551c…`. `tools/acpi-runtime-check.py` `PASS` (59 top-level devices, 36 `_CRS` bodies identical, 0 mismatched). `tools/acpi-dt-crosscheck.py` `PASS` (`21 device(s) cross-checked; 0 slip(s), 0 unaccounted`). `tools/acpi-hid-census.py --bind`: `QCOM0A06` and `QCOM0A27` both now claimed, `ASL presents 59 id(s)` (was 57). `tools/driver-id-census.py`: `ASL presents 59 id(s)`, `driver-has-id-but-ASL-has-none: 109` (was 120/111), `ASL-has-id-but-no-driver: 8`. `tools/make_uefi_platform.py` regenerated the twin (`cmp` identical); `tools/sync-uefi-platform.sh` installed it; `build_uefi.py -d gauguin -r DEBUG -c` reached `PROGRESS - Success` (the trailing `DTB image must not be empty` is by design). `P2DIR=work/out/p3-camera tools/build-p2-payloads.sh` rebuilt three images, each embedding `DSDT 14,722 B sha256 5448bc512e10551c`, GenFv map 126 offsets/GUIDs zero mismatches.

**decides**: that the camera chain's two unconditional ids — `QCOM0A06` (`CAMF`) and `QCOM0A27` (`FLSH`) — are written and bind from this driver set; that neither takes a memory window, on the corpus's and this board's tree's agreement, for the same reason `RFS0` takes none; that `_DEP` is on the platform node; and that lisa's `CAMI`/`CAMT`/`CAMU` are `SKUV`-gated and disabled on the IDP variant whose token this file's `PSUB` returns, so writing them enabled would contradict 4.264 and writing them disabled would add nothing. **does not decide**: whether gauguin's silicon is the IDP configuration those three are disabled for, which gauguin's bus carrying five eeproms and three flash nodes puts in doubt and which no offline source settles; whether the camera chain works end to end, which needs the phone; and whether the `QCOM0AA2` borrow for the CSID blocks is the right id (4.66's open item, unchanged).

**Not an action**: `iasl -tc` (in `/tmp`, no artefact under `tools/acpi/`), `iconv -f UTF-16 -t UTF-8` over the camera INFs, `python3` over `work/out/dt-decomp/vendor.dts` for the camera node regs and interrupts, `sed`/`grep` over lisa's decompiled `DSDT.dsl`, `tools/make_uefi_platform.py`, `cmp`, `tools/sync-uefi-platform.sh`, `build_uefi.py`, `P2DIR=... tools/build-p2-payloads.sh`, `python3` importing `tools/fv-inventory.py` to extract each embedded `DSDT`, `tools/acpi-runtime-check.py`, `tools/acpi-dt-crosscheck.py`, `tools/acpi-hid-census.py --bind`, `tools/driver-id-census.py`, `sha256sum`, `stat`. Read-only against the device; **no `adb` or `fastboot` command was issued beyond reading `adb devices`** (which lists `d25f844e recovery`), `fastboot fetch` was not used, no partition, seed, `boot` or storage was written, no QEMU process was started or signalled, and none of `work/out/{p2-variants,p3-display,usb-host,p2-what}`, `work/win11/qemu-stick*`, `work/out/p3-stick/` or `work/out/.p3-stick-drivers/` was touched. **Files written**: `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl`, the regenerated twin (`cmp`-identical), and this entry; `work/out/p3-camera/` (new, gitignored). `device/dxe/UsbConfigDxe.efi` is still `sha256 6943cc615f7d4ba502c87bcf14a76e6e1398975a4101ed2711ba9e1c6e2566f5`. The orphaned dry-run processes 468162 and 471324 were left alive, `bq6ik1shs` was not restarted and `br7srnvmx` was not started. **Consequence for the P3 gate**: none — the gate is storage and not camera — but "all hardware driven" gains the two nodes that were missing a driver rather than a window, and the three that remain unbound are recorded as owed with their reason.

## Step 4.272 — the SKUV gate is never written in the corpus and the branch directions differ: 4.271's camera comment claimed the three gated sensors disable together, and only one does

**What this step is.** 4.271 wrote, in its ASL comment, that lisa's `CAMI` (`QCOM0A99`), `CAMT` (`QCOM0ACE`) and `CAMU` (`QCOM0ACF`) "are gated on `\_SB.SKUV`" and that "on the IDP variant `SKUV == One`, CAMI's `_STA` returns Zero and CAMT/CAMU's do too". Reading the three `_STA` methods one by one says the first clause is right and the second is wrong: `CAMI` returns `Zero` when `SKUV == One`, but `CAMT` and `CAMU` return `0x0F` on that branch and `Zero` otherwise. `SKUV == One` **disables CAMI and enables CAMT/CAMU** — the mirror image. The correction is comment-only in the compiled sense (`iasl` produces a byte-identical `DSDT.aml`, `sha256 5448bc512e10551c…`), so no payload is rebuilt; what it buys is that the next reader does not act on a sentence that points the wrong way.

**The larger finding under it: `SKUV` is never written.** `grep -nE 'SKUV\s*=' lisa.dsl` returns only *reads* — every hit is an `If ((SKUV == …))` — and the name is declared once, at `DSDT.dsl:239`, as `Name (SKUV, 0xFFFFFFFF)`, with no `Store` to it anywhere in the 40 occurrences. So when a reference DSDT is read on its own, every `SKUV`-gated branch resolves to its **else** leg: `CAMI` becomes `0x0F` and `CAMT`/`CAMU` become `Zero`, which is the opposite of what the `SKUV == One` leg says and the opposite of what 4.271's comment assumed. The value is meant to arrive from the platform at runtime — the boot firmware's soft-SKU — and it is not in the corpus or in either device tree; gauguin's declares neither `qcom,softsku-id` nor `qcom,pmic-id` (which is also why its board overlay is appended unconditionally, a fact already recorded), and its `bootargs` carry no `softsku`. This file does not define `SKUV` at all, so none of the gates it would drive fire here — which is why `CAMP`'s `Alias (^PSUB, _SUB)` is safe, as 4.264 argued, but it also means the gated *devices* have no value to branch on and the honest state is to leave them out.

**The same gate governs the thermal family, and it is the larger half.** The twelve ids of `qcthermalmdm7280.inf` a census still reports absent — `QCOM04B4`, `QCOM04B5`, `QCOM04B6`, `QCOM04B7`, `QCOM04B8`, `QCOM04B9`, `QCOM04BA`, `QCOM04BB`, `QCOM04BC`, `QCOM04BE`, `QCOM04BF`, `QCOM06D4` — are, in lisa, twelve devices (`MPA`, `MPA1`, `MBJ0`-`MBJ3`, `MBS0`-`MBS2`, `MSKN`, `MJCT`, `MBCL`) that are each `_DEP {IPC0}`, `_SUB = PSUB`, carry **no `_CRS`**, and return `Zero` when `SKUV` is 4, 6 or 7 and `0x0F` otherwise. So the thermal sensors are windowless sensor endpoints whose enablement depends on the same unwritten soft-SKU. They are not written here for exactly the reason the three camera sensors are not, and the comment now says so in one place instead of leaving it to be rediscovered.

**decides**: that `SKUV == One` disables `CAMI` and enables `CAMT`/`CAMU`, not all three together, and 4.271's comment is corrected in place; that `SKUV` is declared `0xFFFFFFFF` and **never written** in the reference tables, so every `SKUV`-gated branch resolves to its else leg when the table is read alone, and the true value comes from a soft-SKU that is in neither device tree nor the corpus; and that the twelve `qcthermalmdm7280` sensor ids are gated by the same name and left unwritten for the same reason. **does not decide**: what soft-SKU gauguin's boot firmware reports, which is a runtime value no offline source carries and which would settle both the three camera sensors and the twelve thermal ones at once; and whether writing the `SKUV` name and a `Store` to populate it from a register read would be correct here, which is the same deferred-measurement question 4.268 left open for `SJTG`/`_HRV`.

**Not an action**: `grep`/`sed` over lisa's decompiled `DSDT.dsl` for the `_STA` methods, the `SKUV` declaration and every `SKUV` occurrence; `python3` to enumerate the twelve thermal nodes by `_HID`; `iasl -tc` (in `/tmp`); `cmp` on the twin and a `python3` extraction of the embedded `DSDT` from the 4.271 payloads to confirm the change compiles identically. Read-only against the device; no `adb`/`fastboot` command, no `boot`/storage write, no QEMU. **Files written**: `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl`, the regenerated twin, and this entry. `device/dxe/UsbConfigDxe.efi` still `sha256 6943cc615f7d4ba502c87bcf14a76e6e1398975a4101ed2711ba9e1c6e2566f5`. `bq6ik1shs` not restarted, `br7srnvmx` not started, pids 468162/471324 untouched. **Consequence for the P3 gate**: none — the table is byte-identical to 4.271's, and the gate is storage.

## Step 4.273 — the device read before the write: `boot` holds the 09-23 16:20:52 build, which settles the `90b21643…` fork the record had named wrongly, and the P3 medium was never on the phone

**What this step is.** The standing rule is 「对照的那张必须在覆盖之前读」 — the reference has to be read before it is overwritten — and the phone is in TWRP at `d25f844e`. So the `boot` partition was read off the device read-only, at the last moment before any P3 write, to establish what the control actually is. The reading does three things: it confirms the payload identity the record has been carrying as *owed*, it gives the first *fresh* copy of the only instance of that build, and it forecloses one failure mode of the P3 gate — the medium is not on the device and never was.

**The reading, in one place.** `/dev/block/by-name/boot` → `/dev/block/sde55`, `blockdev --getsize64` = **134,217,728**, exactly the partition the restore path names. The read is the full partition, **134,217,728 B**, sha256 `a56e593335807b5ba7045f5c44f0b3ed2c8b2c7290c6f745f1c61943a708f359`; re-reading the first 4 MiB returns the same digest, so the read is deterministic and faithful. The Android boot header is **version 1, page_size 2048**, `kernel_size` **1,136,864**, `ramdisk_size` **5** (the sentinel ramdisk the P2 payloads carry), so the payload occupies `0x0..0x116000` and its **1,142,784-byte** extent hashes to **`7c8fdb5a1a272ab65d806c2833eb849f441c3ef2092121aac0d5df40d0e1ef44`**. Inflated, the gzip kernel is the PE volume **3,145,840 B**, sha256 **`64d7702d08519034dd56a1a698a013a8…`**, carrying **13 of the 14** instruments — every rung but `P2FreeWhy` — and the build stamp inside it is **`Sep 23 2026 16:20:52`**.

**The fork is settled, and the record's `90b21643…` was wrong.** `work/out/p2-variants/Mu-gauguin-silicon-gzip.img` is `90b21643…` at `1,142,784 B` **today**, but its mtime is **2026-09-25 09:20:34** and its stamp reads **`Sep 25 2026 01:20:06`** — it is a rebuild, not the file that went to the phone. Byte-comparing it against the device confirms the divergence at the header itself: the device's `kernel_size` is **1,136,864**, the rebuild's **1,138,014**, and the two inflate to the same 3,145,840 bytes with different content. So the phone holds a build that is **older than the rebuild and older than the 4.74 set**, and a fresh 09-30 read reproduces step 4.211's `7c8fdb5a…` and step 4.188's `64d7702d…` / 13-of-14 exactly. That is the point worth recording: **three independent readings of the same partition, months apart in the record, agree byte for byte**, and the one name the record carried for `boot` between them was the one thing that did not. A rebuild under the same filename is not the same file, and a filename in the record is not a reading.

**And the P3 medium was never written to the phone.** The whole 128 MiB partition was scanned for the structures the medium would leave: **no `FAT16`, no `FAT32`, no `MSWIN4.1`, no `EFI PART`, no `BOOTAA64`, no `\EFI\`, no `PE32+`** anywhere in it. The only `MZ` is at `61195`, inside the payload's own PE volume. The medium `work/out/p3-medium-arm64.img` is a FAT32 filesystem and could not be present without those signatures, so the P3 gate has not been attempted through `boot` and this partition carries no medium residue. What follows the 1,142,784-byte payload — nonzero from `0x121000` out to partition offset `0x2dd4cdb`, roughly 48 MB — is the **tail of the Smartisan image the payload was flashed over**, which is exactly the residue the 4.33 record describes and is where a P3 write would begin to diverge the control the restore path depends on.

**Gates and the restore path.** No gate is affected: the ASL is untouched by this step, so `tools/acpi/gauguin.asl` is byte-identical to 4.272's (`DSDT.aml` **14,722 B**, sha256 `5448bc512e10551c…`). The restore path is intact and re-verified: `~/backup/gauguin/images/part-boot.img` is **134,217,728 B** and its sha256 still begins `50ef59beb17e75de…`, matching the `EXPECT` pinned at `tools/restore-stock-boot.sh:36`, so stock `boot` remains recoverable. `device/dxe/UsbConfigDxe.efi` is still `sha256 6943cc615f7d4ba502c87bcf14a76e6e1398975a4101ed2711ba9e1c6e2566f5`.

**decides**: that `boot` holds the **09-23 16:20:52** build — payload extent 1,142,784 B, sha256 `7c8fdb5a…`, inflated volume 3,145,840 B, sha256 `64d7702d08519034…`, 13 of 14 instruments — and that this is **not** `work/out/p2-variants/Mu-gauguin-silicon-gzip.img` as that path stands today (`90b21643…`, mtime 09-25 09:20:34, stamp `Sep 25 01:20:06`), so the fork the record carried between `90b21643…` and the on-device readback resolves against `90b21643…` **for the second time and with the same answer as 4.211**; that the new read is faithful and deterministic (full-partition read, identical on re-read) and reproduces both `7c8fdb5a…` and `64d7702d…` exactly; that the P3 medium has **no** presence on the partition (no FAT, EFI, or PE-image signature outside the payload's own), so the gate has not been run and `boot` carries no medium residue; and that the restore path and the `UsbConfigDxe` asset are both unchanged. **does not decide**: *which* source revision produced the 09-23 16:20:52 build, which remains the ten-step window between 4.31 and 4.41 that 4.210 bounded and which this step narrows only by confirming the stamp; whether `boot`'s payload should be preserved before a P3 write or whether the gate should overwrite it, the two being in tension because the phone holds the last instance of that build while the gate needs `boot` for its own payload; and whether 13-of-14 rather than 14-of-14 matters for the gate, which it does not — the gate is storage, not instrumentation.

**Not an action**: `adb devices`, `adb shell getprop`, `adb shell blockdev/readlink`, `adb exec-out dd` (read-only, the whole point), `sha256sum`, `cmp`, `stat`; `python3` to compare the readback against `p2-variants` and `p2-4.74`, to diff the two inflated volumes and read their build stamps, and to scan the partition for FAT/EFI/PE signatures; `find` + `sha256sum` across repo, `/tmp`, `~/backup`, `~/Downloads` and `~/work` for the `90b21643` digest. Read-only against the device throughout; **no `fastboot` command was issued, `fastboot fetch` was not used, and no partition, seed, `boot` or storage was written**. **Files written**: this entry, and `~/backup/gauguin/images/boot-readback-2026-09-30.img` (the fresh, verified copy of the only instance of the on-device build). No file in the repository was modified except this entry; `work/out/` was not written; none of `work/out/{p2-variants,p3-display,usb-host,p2-what}`, `work/win11/qemu-stick*`, `work/out/p3-stick/` or `work/out/.p3-stick-drivers/` was touched; no QEMU process was started or signalled. The orphaned dry-run processes 468162 and 471324 were left alive, `bq6ik1shs` was not restarted and `br7srnvmx` was not started. **Consequence for the P3 gate**: the control is now read and preserved, so a P3 write to `boot` no longer destroys the last copy of the 09-23 build; the outstanding physical actions remain the user's — a **USB 2.0 stick** to carry `work/out/p3-medium-arm64.img`, and a reboot to the bootloader — and `userdata` (107 GB, unbacked), the partition table and the firmware LUN remain untouched.
